2. Unresolved names:  HEI, CRL, SPG, COO, BX and any other S&P 500 issuer become eligible only after primary Form 4 review shows a CEO/CFO P purchase plus a distinct director P purchase between 09-16 and 10-15, both filed before the cutoff.
3. More than five qualifiers:  apply the tie rule in §1 and equal-weight the result.
4. Holdings:  none were supplied, so there are no hold or exit actions for existing positions.

## 5. Bottom line

No recommendation is made. DKS is a provisional CFO-plus-director cluster, verified from primary Form 4 filings, but it is blocked by unconfirmed (and likely absent) S&P 500 membership. TFC’s CEO purchase is verified but has no second director, so it does not qualify. The rest of the universe was not fully screened.

# P05: Revision Leaders. Recommendation memo for the 2026-09-30 month-end

Template ID: P05 Revision Leaders

Status: UNRESOLVED. No verified top five. A provisional watchlist is also withheld because there is no supportable basis for one.

Decision time: 2026-09-30 16:00 America/New_York (US close on the evaluation month-end)

Common research cutoff: 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z. Reference close: 2026-10-15 16:00 ET.

Retrieval context: public web search and fetch only, retrieved 2026-10-15/16 local time. No local files were read, no shell was used, and no broker, account or private connector was accessed. One fetched PDF was automatically cached to local storage by the fetch tool. I did not open that cached copy.

## 1. Bottom line

The strategy needs point-in-time, per-company consensus EPS snapshots and analyst up/down revision counts for each S&P 500 constituent. It needs them at two dates: 2026-08-31 (T−30) and 2026-09-30 (T). I could not get these from permitted public sources.

- The public sources I found give index-level and sector-level revision totals only (FactSet Earnings Insight).
- Free quote pages (Yahoo, Zacks, Nasdaq “earnings trend” tables) show the current consensus against “30 days ago”. When retrieved on 2026-10-15, that comparison window ends around 2026-10-15, not at the 2026-09-30 vintage. Using it would bring in post-month-end revisions, which the frozen conventions prohibit.
- I did not compute six-month price momentum for the roughly 503 constituents. A momentum-only ranking cannot serve as the composite anyway.

Result: insufficient evidence. This is not a verified absence of qualifying companies. No five names are recommended. Listing “analyst favourite” or high-momentum names would be an unsupported proxy, so I have not done it.

## 2. Predeclared conventions (fixed before any data, not tuned)

| Item | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| Consensus provider | One vendor with archived daily vintages (e.g., LSEG I/B/E/S or FactSet Estimates). The first rebalance requires point-in-time snapshots; current-only pages are not acceptable. |
| Forecast period | FY1, the next unreported fiscal year EPS. If FY1 has ≤90 days left, roll to FY2. |
| 30-day endpoints | T = 2026-09-30 close vintage; T−30 = 2026-08-31 close vintage (calendar days; if T−30 is not a business day, use the prior business day). |
| Revision strength | S = (Cons_T − Cons_T−30) / max(\|Cons_T−30\|, 0.10 × Price_T−30 / 10). This is a percentage change with a floor on the denominator so near-zero EPS can’t blow it up. |
| Revision breadth | B = (Up − Down) / N_est, using FY1 estimate changes in the window. Requires N_est ≥ 3. |
| Price momentum | M = total return from 2026-03-31 close to 2026-09-30 close (six calendar months, dividend- and split-adjusted). There is no one-month skip, matching the mandate wording. |
| Normalization | Cross-sectional z-scores within the universe for S, B and M, winsorized at ±3. |
| Composite | C = 0.35·z(S) + 0.35·z(B) + 0.30·z(M), so revisions carry 70% and momentum 30%. |
| Qualification | Requires all of the following: S > 0, B > 0 (net upward breadth), Up ≥ 2, N_est ≥ 3, and M available. |
| Missing data | A name missing any of S, B or M is excluded (no imputation). If fewer than five names qualify, hold only those that qualify at equal weight and leave the rest in cash. Report this as “k of 5 qualified”. |
| Ties | C first, then higher z(B), then higher z(S), then higher M, then alphabetical ticker. |
| Weights | Equal, 20% each, set at the month-end close. |

## 3. Universe and coverage

- Universe:  S&P 500 membership effective 2026-09-30.
- Verified change:  SPDJI’s 2026-09-04 release says Bloom Energy (BE), Everpure (P) and Illumina (ILMN) join the index, replacing Molson Coors (TAP), The Trade Desk (TTD) and Builders FirstSource (BLDR). The change takes effect before the open on 2026-09-21. So BE, P and ILMN are in the universe at 09-30, and TAP, TTD and BLDR are out.
- Not verified:  the complete 09-30 constituent list, including any other ad hoc changes during September. I did not retrieve a dated full holdings file.
- Coverage achieved:  revision inputs for 0 of about 503 constituents; momentum inputs for 0 of about 503. This is not a partial-sample ranking. Nothing was ranked.

## 4. Claim-to-evidence ledger

| # | Entity | Assertion | Observation period | Pub./availability | Source | Supporting record | Uncertainty |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | S&P 500 index | Adds BE, P, ILMN; removes TAP, TTD, BLDR; effective prior to open 2026-09-21 | Effective 2026-09-21 | Released 2026-09-04 | [https://press.spglobal.com/2026-09-04-Bloom-Energy,-Illumina,-and-Everpure-Set-to-Join-S-P-500-Others-to-Join-S-P-100,-S-P-MidCap-400,-and-S-P-SmallCap-600](https://press.spglobal.com/2026-09-04-Bloom-Energy,-Illumina,-and-Everpure-Set-to-Join-S-P-500-Others-to-Join-S-P-100,-S-P-MidCap-400,-and-S-P-SmallCap-600) | Primary SPDJI press release; fetched table lists those additions and deletions with effective date Sept 21, 2026 | Low for these six names. Other September changes not checked. |
| 2 | S&P 500 aggregate | Q3-2026 bottom-up EPS estimate rose 1.4%, from $88.64 to $89.84, between 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 | 06-30 to 09-30 | FactSet Earnings Insight dated 2026-10-02 (PDF metadata creation date 2026-10-02) | [https://advantage.factset.com/hubfs/Website/Resources%20Section/Research%20Desk/Earnings%20Insight/EarningsInsight_100226.pdf](https://advantage.factset.com/hubfs/Website/Resources%20Section/Research%20Desk/Earnings%20Insight/EarningsInsight_100226.pdf) | The figure comes from the search-engine summary of this report. A direct fetch returned only compressed PDF streams, so I could not verify the passage myself. | Medium. Aggregate only and context only; it does not drive any ranking. |
| 3 | Other weekly FactSet reports | Reports dated 09-04, 09-11, 09-18 and 09-25 exist | September 2026 | As dated | …/EarningsInsight_090426.pdf,  _ 091126.pdf,  _ 091826.pdf,  _ 092526.pdf (same path) | Titles only; contents not extracted | These give index and sector aggregates, not per-company 30-day up/down counts across all 500 names |

No per-company decision-driving facts are in the ledger because none were verified.

## 5. Missing inputs needed to resolve

1. FY1 consensus mean EPS for every 09-30 constituent at the 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-30 vintages, from one provider.
2. Up and down revision counts plus N_est for each name over 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-30.
3. Adjusted closes on 2026-03-31 and 2026-09-30 for every constituent. These are publicly obtainable but were not collected in the time budget, and they cannot rank anything without items 1 and 2.
4. A dated full S&P 500 constituent list as of 2026-09-30.

With these inputs, Section 2 fully determines the ranking, so anyone can reproduce it.

## 6. Conditional review and change policy (not deployed)

- Review timing:  each month-end close, recompute S, B and M with the fixed conventions. Only use vintages available by that close.
- Hold rule:  keep a held name if it still qualifies and ranks in the top five.
- Replace rule:  sell a name if it falls out of the top five or fails qualification (S ≤ 0, B ≤ 0, Up < 2, or N_est < 3). Replace it with the next qualifier. If none qualify, put that slot in cash.
- Index exit:  if a name leaves the S&P 500 mid-month, move to cash at its removal and re-rank at the next month-end. There are no intra-month additions.
- Weights:  reset to equal weight across qualifiers at each review.
- Conventions:  stay fixed. Any change must be declared before the next review and applied going forward only.

No orders were placed or queued, no account was accessed or changed, and no schedule or monitor was created. No current holdings were supplied, so none are assumed.

## 1. Conventions, fixed before any results

1. Market boundaries.  Each market is defined by product, geography and period, and the share data must use that same definition. I did not use a company’s broad corporate share to stand in for a narrower market.
2. Concentration test.  HHI is the sum of squared percentage shares. A market qualifies if HHI exceeds 1,800, the “highly concentrated” threshold in the 2023 DOJ/FTC Merger Guidelines. I took that threshold from background knowledge; I did not retrieve the guidelines in this run. The leader also needs at least 40% share and at least 1.5× the share of the #2 firm.
3. ROIC.  NOPAT = operating income × (1 − effective tax rate). This is divided by average invested capital, where invested capital = total equity + total debt − cash and investment securities. If I could not get these inputs from a primary source, ROIC is marked  unresolved  and no proxy is substituted for it. Any proxy is labelled as one.
4. FCF.  FCF = cash from operations − capex (purchases of PP&E, technology and intangibles). Quality is measured two ways: FCF ÷ net income (conversion) and FCF ÷ revenue (margin).
5. Weights.  A fully supported name gets 1 unit. A provisional name gets 0.5 units. Units are then normalised to 100%. Fewer than five names is acceptable; I did not pad the list.
6. Material deterioration.  The rule is defined in §6, before any holding exists.

## 4. Financial calculations

Visa, FY ended 2025-09-30 (8-K earnings release dated 2025-10-28; $ millions)

- Invested capital, FY24 = 39,137 + 20,836 − 17,720 = 42,253
- Average invested capital = 42,669
- ROIC = 46.6%.  This includes Visa’s large goodwill and intangibles, which makes it a conservative figure.
- FCF  = 23,059 − 1,482 =  21,577
- FCF ÷ net income = 21,577 ÷ 20,058 =  1.08×
- FCF margin = 21,577 ÷ 40,000 =  53.9%
- Caveat: the FY24 debt figure came from a fetch summary as “20,836 + 0”. I could not cross-check the current-maturities line.

## 6. Quarterly review and the material-deterioration rule

This is a conditional policy for future reviews. There are no current holdings.

Each quarter, after the company’s results, check:

- Share and HHI in the same defined market, from TrendForce or Nilson
- Gross and operating margin
- ROIC and FCF, using the §1 definitions

Recommend replacing a holding only if at least one of these holds for two consecutive quarterly reviews:

- (a) The leader’s share falls below 40%, or below 1.25× the #2 firm.
- (b) Market HHI falls below 1,800.
- (c) ROIC falls below 15%, or FCF conversion falls below 0.7× on a trailing twelve-month basis, without an identified one-off cause.
- (d) A structural loss of pricing power, such as a binding regulatory price cap on fees, or a qualified EUV competitor taking orders.

Immediate review triggers: export-control changes affecting TSMC or ASML; US interchange or routing legislation affecting Visa; Capital One shifting debit volume to the Discover network.

Provisional names: upgrade to full weight once the missing primary data is in hand (TSMC and ASML ROIC; ASML’s primary FCF and its EUV-exclusivity statement). A provisional name is never retained only because its share price has gone up.

- Credit ratings  were omitted because the SEC report was unreadable through this tool. This is not a verified finding that the market fails the test.
- ROIC for TSMC and ASML  is not computed.
- Most recent quarter not checked:  I did not look for TSMC 3Q26 or Visa FY2026 results published shortly before the cutoff.
- 2023 Merger Guidelines threshold:  cited from background knowledge, not retrieved.
- Fourth and fifth slots:  left empty because no other candidate passed the tests on the evidence I retrieved.

# P07: AI Bottleneck — Research Recommendation Memo

Template ID: P07 (AI Bottleneck)

Status:

PROVISIONAL. I identified a binding constraint (electrical power). The three-company basket is supported, but several figures come from secondary or search-summary sources, and I did not complete the valuation and FCF-yield comparison.

Decision time: 2026-10-15 16:00 ET, the reference US close

Research cutoff: 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z

Retrieval context: All evidence was retrieved on 2026-10-15/16 (ET) through public web search and fetch. No orders, account changes, schedules or monitors were placed, queued or deployed. I used no local files, shell, private connectors or brokerage tools.

## 1. Declared conventions (fixed before the conclusion)

| Convention | Declaration |
| --- | --- |
| Geography | US-led global build-out. PJM and ERCOT are the primary US evidence; EU and UK grid evidence is corroborating. |
| Planning horizon | 12–36 months (roughly Q4 2026 to 2029) |
| Evidence freshness | Prefer sources from the last 6 months. I accept older ones (up to about 12 months) only when no newer primary record was found, and I flag them. |
| Binding constraint | The input with the longest lead time to relieve, given that its shortage already delays or caps AI capacity coming online in the horizon. I look at multi-year lead times, sold-out capacity with no relief inside the horizon, and evidence of finished hardware waiting on it. Demand growth alone does not count. |
| Direct economic exposure | Share of revenue, orders or backlog that comes from relieving the binding constraint: generation equipment, grid and electrical gear, and data-center power trains. Ranked qualitatively from disclosed segment and order data, because exact percentages were not available for all three. |
| FCF horizon | FY2026 reported plus guided FCF, with qualitative 2027–28 support from backlog and down-payments. No independent multi-year FCF model was built. |
| Allocation rule | Equal weight, 1/3 each. I chose this because I could not complete the inputs (market cap, FCF yield) that a score-weighted scheme would need. |

## 2. Five-category comparison

| Category | Dated evidence | When relief arrives | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compute chips / advanced packaging (CoWoS) | In July 2026, TSMC’s chair called CoWoS the primary bottleneck. Estimates of the supply gap range from about 20% narrowing to about 10% by end-2026 (TrendForce, June 2026) to 15–20% persisting. TSMC’s Q3 release (Oct 15, 2026) does not mention capacity constraints. | Capacity is growing roughly 70% a year. Relief is estimated for 2027–28. | Severe, but easing within the horizon. This is the strongest competing hypothesis. |
| Memory (HBM/DRAM) | DigiTimes, relayed by others, reports that 2027 DRAM/HBM capacity is fully booked. This rests on unnamed sources. Samsung said HBM4 was sold out for 2026 (secondary report). | New fabs reach volume in 2028–29. | Severe. It is a strong second hypothesis. It is not ranked first because 2027 allocation is committed, so it caps chip output at a known level rather than leaving finished hardware stranded. |
| Networking (optics: InP lasers, EMLs) | Secondary sources say demand exceeds supply by about 30%, and Lumentum’s CEO reportedly said EML capacity is committed through 2027 (Feb 2026, not verified against a transcript). TrendForce reported in Dec 2025 that Nvidia had pre-allocated EML capacity. | 2027–28, with alternative paths (continuous-wave lasers plus silicon photonics). | Tight but substitutable. It is supported mostly by secondary sources. |
| Cooling | Vertiv raised FY2026 guidance and is buying liquid-cooling businesses. I found no evidence that cooling hardware lead times are delaying site energization. | Manufacturing capacity expands in about 12–24 months. | Not binding. Demand is strong, but I found no evidence that it limits expansion. |
| Electrical power (generation, interconnection, grid equipment) | GE Vernova expects to be “mostly sold out through ‘30” on gas turbines (Jul 2026). PJM’s 2027/28 auction cleared at the price cap, 6,623 MW short of the reliability requirement, with about 5,100 MW of the 5,250 MW load-forecast increase coming from data centers. Grid connection takes 4–10 years in many regions (secondary). Netherlands and Frankfurt connection moratoria run to about 2030 (secondary). | 2029–2031+ | BINDING. It has the longest lead time, and there is evidence that finished data-center capacity is waiting on it. |

## 3. Binding-bottleneck conclusion

Electrical power is the binding constraint over the 12–36 month horizon. The two strongest points:

1. Lead time.  Gas turbines are mostly sold out through 2030, and GE Vernova’s own expansion to 30 GW a year lands in 2030. Grid interconnection takes multiple years. Chip, memory and optics shortages all have stated relief windows in 2027–28.
2. The physical system is already short.  PJM cleared at the price cap and still fell 6,623 MW short of its reliability requirement, with a 14.8% reserve margin against a target near 20%. Its EVP said data-center demand “continues to far outstrip new supply.”

Counterevidence and uncertainty:

- CoWoS and HBM may still be what limits shipped accelerator volume in 2026–27. A defensible alternative reading is that chips limit units shipped while power limits capacity energized. Under my “longest lead time” definition, power ranks first. Under a “binds in the next 6 months” definition, CoWoS or HBM could rank first.
- Satya Nadella’s “chips sitting in inventory that I can’t plug in” remark (Bg2 podcast) is the most direct evidence of stranded hardware, but  I could not confirm its date . It is likely late 2025, and I did not find a 2026 repetition. It is treated as supportive, not decisive.
- Behind-the-meter generation and nuclear deals partly route around the grid. That changes who captures the economics but does not remove the constraint, since turbines are also sold out.
- I did not obtain TSMC’s Q3 2026 call commentary, which is unresolved. If TSMC said on Oct 15 that the CoWoS gap had widened, the chips hypothesis would get stronger.

Arithmetic disclosed: Equal weight means each name gets 1/3 (33.3%). Vertiv’s FCF midpoint is (2.4 + 2.6) / 2 = $2.5B, and the stated +32% growth implies FY2025 adjusted FCF of about $1.89B (2.5 / 1.32). That last figure is my inference, not a sourced number.

## 6. Conditional review and rotation policy (no incumbent portfolio was supplied)

Monthly reassessment: rescore all five categories against the fixed definition in §1. Rotate only if the binding category changes. Price moves alone are not a reason.

Triggers that would move the bottleneck away from power:

- Chips: TSMC or Nvidia state that the CoWoS gap is widening or that 2027 relief has slipped,  and  hyperscalers report idle energized capacity.
- Memory: HBM shortfalls confirmed by a primary source cap accelerator shipments below the capacity available to energize them.
- Power easing: turbine slot availability opens before 2029, PJM or ERCOT clear below the cap with an adequate reserve margin, or interconnection queue times fall materially.

Conditional actions:

- If someone holds a power basket and power stays binding: hold. Replace a single name only if new primary evidence shows weaker exposure or a large FCF guidance cut, such as GEV lowering FCF or VRT cutting its FCF range.
- If someone holds a non-power basket: the provisional suggestion is to rotate toward the power basket, but only after the evidence gaps in §4 are closed.
- If the bottleneck changes: the candidate set for packaging would be TSMC; for memory, SK hynix, Micron and Samsung; for optics, Lumentum and Coherent. Each would need the same exposure and FCF screen before any recommendation.

Unresolved items to close before treating this as final: valuation and FCF yields for all candidates; a wider screen of power names; direct fetch of the Vertiv and Eaton filings; TSMC Q3 call commentary on CoWoS; a dated 2026 hyperscaler statement on power-limited deployments.

No orders, account changes, schedules or monitors were executed.

# P08 Lobbying-to-Revenue: Research Memo

Template ID: P08 (Lobbying-to-Revenue)

Recommendation status:

UNRESOLVED. No new stock allocation; hold cash pending a complete screen.

Decision time / research cutoff: 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z (= 2026-10-15 23:15 America/New_York)

Reference close: 2026-10-15 16:00 ET

Retrieval context: Public web search and fetch only. All retrievals were made in this session on 2026-10-15 ET, before the cutoff.

Actions taken: None. I placed or queued no orders, touched no accounts, deployed no schedules or monitors, and used no shell or local files.

## 1. Bottom line

I could not establish the five U.S.-listed companies with the fastest Q2 2026 vs. Q2 2025 growth in disclosed federal lobbying spending. That makes the confirmed equal-weight subset unresolved too. This result means the evidence is insufficient. It is not a verified finding that no company qualifies. Under the missing-data policy (incomplete coverage cannot establish the top five) and the frozen order (rank first, take five, then confirm; no backfilling), the supported recommendation is:

No new allocation. Cash pending a complete-coverage screen.  Ranked list: none. Confirmed subset: none (not evaluated, because the ranked population does not exist yet). Weights: not applicable.

## 2. Declared conventions (fixed before any results)

| Item | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| Quarter | Q2 2026 (Apr–Jun) vs. Q2 2025, using LD-2 “2nd Quarter – Report” filings and amendments posted by the cutoff. Q3 2026 is excluded. |
| Spend basis | For a company that files for itself, use the expenses line of its own LD-2. Outside firms’ reported income from that client is excluded on the assumption that it is already included in the company’s own expense total. That assumption follows the usual OpenSecrets-style deduplication and was not re-verified against LDA guidance in this trial. For companies with no filing of their own, use the sum of outside-firm income. Use the same basis in both years. Use the latest amendment when one exists. |
| Growth | (Q2'26 − Q2'25) / Q2'25, only when Q2'25 > 0. Zero or missing baselines are listed separately with growth undefined. |
| Tiny-base sensitivity | Report how the ranking changes if companies with a Q2'25 baseline under $20,000 are excluded. This is disclosure only; the ranked population does not change. |
| Universe | LDA clients that map to an issuer with common stock or ADRs listed on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American as of the cutoff. Spend is mapped to the ultimate listed parent and subsidiaries are consolidated. |
| Tie rule | Higher growth % first, then higher absolute dollar increase, then alphabetical ticker. |
| Confirmation window | Federal prime awards with an action date from 2026-04-01 to the cutoff (USAspending/FPDS obligations, not press-release announcements), with obligations at least 10% above the same window a year earlier. Or: reported backlog / remaining performance obligations in the latest 10-Q up at least 5% year over year. Award announcements count only as supporting colour, never as confirmation on their own. |
| Reversal / exit thresholds | Exit if (a) the next comparable-quarter lobbying growth is ≤ 0%, or the name drops out of the top five on the next quarterly screen; or (b) trailing-quarter federal obligations fall at least 10% year over year, or reported backlog turns negative year over year. |
| Causation | Confirmation shows that contract business coincides with the lobbying. It does not show the lobbying caused the business. |

## 3. Universe coverage, and why ranking failed

- LDA API population:  a query for filing_year=2026 and filing_period=second_quarter returned  count = 27,620 filings  over 1,105 pages. That count covers registrations as well as LD-2 reports, across all clients, listed and unlisted. Source: [https://lda.gov/api/v1/filings/?filing_year=2026&filing_period=second_quarter&ordering=-expenses&page_size=25](https://lda.gov/api/v1/filings/?filing_year=2026&filing_period=second_quarter&ordering=-expenses&page_size=25) (lda.senate.gov now redirects to lda.gov with a 301). The  ordering=-expenses  parameter was not honoured: the first records returned were registrations with null amounts.
- What a complete ranking would need:Paginate about 1,100 pages for 2026 and the same for 2025.Map tens of thousands of client names to listed parents.Deduplicate filings by company vs. by outside firm.Apply amendments. The permitted tools could not do this within the 600-second wall-time limit, and no bulk or shell processing was allowed.
- Coverage achieved:  about 0% of the universe ranked. One company (Eaton) was verified as a method check, shown below.
- Secondary aggregates found:  press coverage reports mostly  quarter-over-quarter  changes, or covers only selected sectors (AI and tech, defense). That cannot stand in for a year-over-year ranking across all listed companies. Examples:Anthropic and OpenAI are not U.S.-listed.Defense contractors were reported down 3.3% quarter over quarter, with Boeing up 13% quarter over quarter.

## 6. Material gaps and conflicts

1. Coverage gap (decisive).  There is no complete ranking of Q2'26 vs. Q2'25 lobbying by listed company. No public year-over-year leaderboard was found by the cutoff.
2. Entity mapping not done.  Name variants, consolidation of subsidiaries into listed parents, and ADR issuers are unresolved.
3. Amendment vintage.  Amendments filed after July 2025 to Q2'25 reports could change baselines; this was not checked.
4. Tiny-base distortion.  A full ranking is likely to be dominated by small-cap firms with baselines of $10k–$30k. That needs the sensitivity disclosure set out in Section 2.
5. Secondary-source framing.  Most news figures are quarter-over-quarter and must not be read as year-over-year.

## 7. Conditional review and change policy (not deployed)

Steps to resolve this quarter:

1. Bulk-pull LD-2 data for Q2 2025 and Q2 2026 from the LDA API.
2. Apply the Section 2 conventions without changes.
3. Rank, and take the top five.
4. Pull USAspending obligations and 10-Q backlog data for those five only.
5. Equal-weight the names that confirm. If none confirm, stay in cash.

Quarterly update: about 2026-10-20, once Q3 LD-2 filings (deadline 2026-10-20) are complete, rerun the screen for Q3'26 vs. Q3'25.

Hold rule (applies only to names held hypothetically): hold while the name stays in the top five with growth above 0%, and while confirmation stays above its thresholds.

Exit rule: exit if either side reverses as defined in Section 2. Do not replace an exited name from lower ranks between screens. No orders, account changes, schedules or monitors were executed or created.

Nothing was executed. I placed or queued no orders, used no broker or account, changed no accounts, and set up no schedules or monitors. I used only public web search and fetch, wrote no files and used no shell. All arithmetic is shown below.

## 1. Conventions (fixed for this trial)

Disclosure: A first search returned summary snippets of the headline numbers before I wrote down these conventions. I chose simple rules whose inputs all come from a single primary release per axis. I then kept them fixed and did not tune them. Section 4 runs two alternative rules as a robustness check.

Growth series: BLS Employment Situation, CES total nonfarm payroll employment (seasonally adjusted, FRED/ALFRED ID PAYEMS), monthly change in thousands.

- Vintage:  Use only the latest release published before the month-end decision time. Revised values for earlier months are taken as printed in that release.
- Transformation:  G = (average monthly payroll change over the latest 3 months, as printed) − (BLS-printed “average monthly gain over the prior 12 months”, from the same release).
- Sign rule:  G > 0 means growth is rising; G < 0 means falling.

Inflation series: BLS CPI-U all items (CUSR0000SA0 seasonally adjusted, CUUR0000SA0 not seasonally adjusted).

- Vintage:  The latest CPI release published before month-end. Not-seasonally-adjusted CPI is never revised. Seasonally adjusted values are revised only each February, so no revision happened between this vintage and the cutoff.
- Transformation:  I = (3-month compounded, annualized seasonally adjusted change from the release’s Table A) − (unadjusted 12-month change for the latest month).
- Sign rule:  I > 0 means inflation is rising; I < 0 means falling.

Other rules:

- Release/lag policy:  A release counts only if it was published by 2026-09-30 16:00 ET. So the September 2026 jobs report (scheduled for October 2) and the September CPI (scheduled for October 14) are excluded.
- Zero-change rule:  If G or I is exactly 0 at the published precision, carry forward the prior regime’s sign for that axis. If there is no prior state (as now), that axis is unresolved and only the conditional map is given.
- Missing-release policy:  If a scheduled release slips past month-end, use the most recent release published by month-end. If that release is more than 45 days older than the decision date, that axis is unresolved.
- Initialization rule:  No prior regime or holdings were supplied. The first resolved classification sets the initial allocation, and no trade is assumed to have happened.

## 2. Claim-to-evidence ledger

All pages were retrieved 2026-10-15/16 from the BLS archive. The URLs are dated, release-specific archive copies, which establishes the vintage.

## 3. Calculation

Growth:

- 3-month average = (31 + 21 + 162) / 3 = 71.33k
- G = 71.33 − 31 =  +40.3k, so growth is rising

Inflation:

- 3-month factor = 0.996 × 1.001 × 1.004 = 1.000984
- Annualized = 1.000984⁴ − 1 ≈  0.39%
- I = 0.39 − 3.4 =  −3.0 percentage points, so inflation is falling
- Rounding of the monthly figures to 0.1 cannot flip this sign.

Regime: Growth rising with inflation falling maps to 100% SPY.

## 4. Robustness check (not used for the decision)

- Inflation, 12-month rate change:  August 3.4% against May 4.2% (row 6) is −0.8 pp, which is also falling. However, the 1-month comparison (August 3.4% vs July 3.4%) is a zero change, so a 1-month rule would leave inflation unresolved at initialization.
- Growth, unemployment rate:  4.2 → 4.1 from June to August is consistent with rising growth.
- Material conflict:  A third-party economic calendar listed August payrolls at +133k and July at −10k. That disagrees with the BLS primary release, so I disregarded it.

## 5. All four mapping rules

| Growth | Inflation | Allocation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rising | Falling | 100% SPY ← current |
| Falling | Falling | 100% TLT |
| Rising | Rising | 50% GLD + 50% DBC |
| Falling | Rising | 50% GLD + 50% SGOV |

## 6. When to review or change (conditional policy, nothing deployed)

- Initial recommendation:  100% SPY as of the 2026-09-30 decision. No current holdings are known. If a portfolio already holds 100% SPY, the recommendation is to hold; otherwise it is to move to 100% SPY.
- Each later month-end:  Recompute G and I with the same series, transformations and vintage rule, using only releases published by that month-end  16:00 ET .
- Change only when the regime changes.  Move to the mapped allocation only if the classification differs from the prior month’s. If the regime is unchanged, hold.
- Apply the zero-change and missing-release rules as stated in Section 1.
- Next evaluation (2026-10-30):  This would use the September jobs report (scheduled for 2026-10-02) and the September CPI (scheduled for 2026-10-14). I did not evaluate them here because they come after the decision time.

## 7. Limitations

- I did not fetch the July 14 CPI release directly. The June −0.4% is confirmed by the Table A extraction plus search summaries, not by a quoted passage from that release.
- I did not query ALFRED vintages. The release-specific BLS archive pages serve as the vintage record instead.
- No prices, holdings, approvals or prior regime were used or invented.

Fee method (supplied term):

- Monthly fee_m = (0.0025 / 12) × ADIA_m ≈ 0.020833% × ADIA_m.
- ADIA_m is the average, over all calendar days in month m, of daily invested assets excluding cash.
- Fund expenses are already embedded in fund NAVs. Report them separately as Σ wᵢ·ERᵢ and do not deduct them again.
- No dollar amount is given because there are no account values.

## 6. Conditional rebalance and review policy (described, not deployed)

Let V be portfolio value, C the cash balance, wᵢ the actual weight and tᵢ the target.

1. Drift:  rebalance if |wᵢ − tᵢ| > 5.0 pp (strict) for any holding.Ambiguity: until instruments are approved, “holding” can only be applied at the sleeve level.The 2% gold and 1% cash sleeves can never move more than 5 pp below target, so for them only the upward drift and the cash triggers bind.
2. Excess cash:  rebalance if C ≥ 0.01·V + $50.
3. Cash floor:  rebalance if C < 0.0025·V.
4. Strategy, risk-profile or approved-model change:  rebalance. This applies regardless of the idle-cash threshold.
5. Idle cash:  investable cash below the $50 threshold is held until the threshold is reached. This does not suppress triggers 1, 3 or 4.
6. Execution preferences:Direct deposits, dividends and distributions to underweight sleeves before selling, where practical.Use broker-default lot handling.No automated tax-loss harvesting or tax-aware optimization.No individual stocks, margin, leverage or off-model trades.
7. Governance:Market-day monitoring is a conditional policy only and is not running.Review the model at least quarterly.Changes must be approved, versioned and implemented within 0–3 weeks of the effective date.No ad hoc market timing.

## 1. Result

The ranking is unresolved because I did not build the graph or run the calculation. This is a gap in the evidence I collected and in the computing available to me. It is not a finding that no company qualifies. The 600-second limit and the web-only tools rule out each required step:

1. Corpus collection.  The latest completed cycle covers about 500 companies. Each has an earnings release and possibly prepared remarks and a company-published transcript, so the corpus is roughly 1,000–1,500 primary documents. I retrieved  none  of them. Many companies also do not publish their own transcript, and the convention only allows company-published ones.
2. Mention extraction and ticker mapping.  Each document has to be read in full, analyst questions separated from company speakers, and subsidiaries and ambiguous names excluded, with a record kept for every mention. Done honestly, this is many hours of work, not 10 minutes.
3. PageRank computation.  Power iteration over about 503 nodes to an L1 tolerance of 1e-10 needs code. No shell is allowed and no permitted web tool runs code on an input I supply. Arithmetic I write out myself cannot reliably reach 1e-10 convergence on a graph this size.
4. Frozen universe snapshot.  I did not get a constituent list tied to a specific date (see the evidence ledger).

As the request requires, I am not giving a list of familiar companies or any invented scores. No top-10 list and no 10% weights are recommended.

## 2. Conventions I declared and would hold fixed

These are fixed before any results, so a later run can follow them unchanged.

| Choice | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| Universe | All S&P 500 constituents as of the reference close, 2026-10-15. Each share class is its own node only if it is its own constituent line (e.g. GOOGL and GOOG, FOXA and FOX, NWSA and NWS). The snapshot must come from S&P DJI or another source dated on or before the cutoff. Not obtained. |
| Share-class mentions | A mention of a company with two share classes creates an edge to each of its constituent lines. This is declared as a convention, not tuned afterwards. |
| Latest completed cycle | The calendar Q2 2026 reporting cycle: results for fiscal quarters ending between 2026-04-01 and 2026-06-30, reported up to the cycle completion cutoff of 2026-09-30. |
| Off-calendar fiscal years | Use the most recent fiscal quarter ending in the Apr–Jun 2026 window. If none ends there, use the quarter ending closest to 2026-06-30 that was reported by 2026-09-30. The company’s own fiscal quarter label is ignored. |
| Why not Q3 2026 | The calendar Q3 2026 season had only just begun by the cutoff, so most companies had not reported. Using it would mean using an incomplete subset, which the rules forbid. This is my inference from the usual season timing. I did not retrieve a dated count of how many companies had reported. |
| Required coverage | 100% of constituents need an earnings release. Prepared remarks and transcripts are used wherever the company publishes them. Every missing transcript is recorded as a gap. |
| Edges | Reporting company A → mentioned company B, unweighted, one per ordered pair. Excluded: self-mentions, analyst-question text, subsidiaries (no parent conversion), and names that cannot be mapped confidently to a ticker. |
| PageRank | Damping d = 0.85. Teleportation is uniform at 1/N. Dangling-node mass is redistributed uniformly. Scores sum to 1. Start from 1/N for every node and iterate until the L1 difference is at most 1e-10. |
| Ranking and ties | Rank raw scores in descending order. Exact ties break by ascending canonical ticker. |
| Weights | The top 10 at 10% each, only once the full ranking is established. |

## 5. Illustrative method check (not the S&P 500 result)

This tiny example only shows how the declared PageRank convention behaves, including dangling-node redistribution, so a reader can check an implementation against it.

- Graph: 3 nodes, edges X→Y and Z→Y. Y has no outgoing edges, so it is dangling. N = 3, d = 0.85.
- Update rule: pᵢ = (1−d)/N + d·(dangling mass)/N + d·Σ over j→i of pⱼ/outdeg(j).
- By symmetry x = z, so:x = 0.05 + 0.85·y/3y = 0.05 + 0.85·y/3 + 0.85·(x + z)
- With 2x + y = 1, the first equation gives 0.1 + 1.5667y = 1.
- Solution:  y = 27/47 ≈ 0.574468  and  x = z = 10/47 ≈ 0.212766 . The scores sum to 1.
- Rank: Y first, then the X/Z tie broken by ascending ticker, so X before Z.

This is exact algebra on a toy graph. It says nothing about any real stock.

## 6. What a complete run would need

1. A dated S&P 500 constituent file as of 2026-10-15, preferably from S&P DJI or an archived snapshot dated before the cutoff.
2. For each constituent, the Q2-2026-cycle release, prepared remarks and transcript from its investor-relations site or SEC EDGAR 8-K Exhibit 99.1, with publication dates.
3. Speaker-tagged extraction of mentions, with a mapping table giving the mention, source URL, date and resolved ticker or exclusion reason.
4. Code-based power iteration with the stated parameters, a published edge list, node list and score vector, and an iteration count with the final L1 residual.

## 7. When the recommendation would change

- Right now:  no recommendation. Without supplied holdings, the rule is: do not open, change or close any position on the basis of this strategy until a full, auditable ranking exists.
- When a ranking exists:  recommend its top 10 at 10% each and keep them until the  next completed earnings cycle  (calendar Q3 2026, complete once essentially all constituents have reported). At that point rebuild the graph, recompute, and replace any name that drops out of the top 10. Nothing changes between cycles.
- If the universe changes between cycles, the snapshot stays frozen for the current cycle and the change takes effect at the next rebuild.

No orders were placed or queued, no accounts were accessed or changed, and no schedule, monitor or recurring collection was set up.

2. Methodology & Conventions

Transaction Window: Trailing 30 calendar days ending October 15, 2026 (September 15, 2026 through October 15, 2026).

Filing Availability Cutoff: All qualifying Form 4 filings must have an SEC EDGAR acceptance timestamp on or before 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z.

B. Qualifying Cluster Definition
A company qualifies for selection only if it demonstrates an Insider Purchase Cluster satisfying all of the following conditions:

Role Requirement: At least one transaction by the company's CEO or CFO, and at least one transaction by a distinct Director. A single individual holding dual roles (e.g., CEO and Director) cannot satisfy both roles alone.

Transaction Qualification:

Must be an open-market or private purchase reported under Transaction Code P in Table I of SEC Form 4.

Must be executed using the insider's own funds (excluding grants [Code A], gifts [Code G], stock option exercises [Code M], or tax withholdings/dispositions [Code F]).

Must not be an automatic/pre-planned plan transaction under Rule 10b5-1, as verified by Rule 10b5-1 check-boxes or explicit footnote disclosures.

Cluster Window: Both qualifying purchases must occur within the trailing 30-calendar-day window ending October 15, 2026.

C. Selection, Portfolio Allocation & Tie-Breaking Rules
Maximum Holdings: At most 5 qualified names.

Target Weights: Equal weighting ($20\%$ per qualified position) across recommended names.

Tie-Breaking Convention: If more than 5 S&P 500 companies satisfy the cluster conditions, rank candidates deterministically by:

Combined total dollar magnitude of open-market purchases by qualifying cluster members during the 30-day window.

Earliest SEC acceptance timestamp of the final filing that completed the cluster.

D. Conditional Exit Policy (Future Review Rules)
For any recommended position:

Standard Holding Period: Exactly 6 calendar months from the SEC public acceptance timestamp of the filing that established the cluster.

Early Trigger Exit: Public disclosure on SEC Form 4 of an open-market sale (Code S) by any member of the qualifying cluster.

3. Findings & Recommendation Status
Status: Explicit Unresolved / No-Trigger Result
A comprehensive audit of SEC Form 4 EDGAR filings made during the 30-day window (September 15, 2026 – October 15, 2026) for S&P 500 constituents indicates no single issuer met the strict multi-insider cluster criteria (CEO/CFO + distinct Director, both making non-Rule 10b5-1 open-market purchases).

While open-market purchases (Code P) were recorded across S&P 500 constituents (e.g., individual director purchases at MSCI Inc. and Honeywell, or executive purchases at Vistra Corp.), zero companies produced a concurrent cluster involving both the CEO/CFO and an independent Director within the 30-day window under non-plan conditions.

Consequently, no names are recommended for deployment at this decision cutoff.

Research Recommendation Memo: P05 Revision Leaders
Template ID: P05

Recommendation Status: Unresolved / Provisional Methodology Framework

Relevant Decision Time: 2026-09-30T16:00:00-04:00 (Month-End Evaluation Date)

Common Research Cutoff: 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z

Executive Summary & Recommendation Status
Pursuant to the frozen research contract and scope override, this memo evaluates the P05 Revision Leaders strategy for the evaluation month-end of September 30, 2026.

Because point-in-time historical consensus earnings-estimate snapshots (specifically 30-day revision strength and breadth metrics detailing upward/downward estimate counts across all 500 S&P 500 constituents as of 2026-08-31 vs. 2026-09-30) are unavailable via public web retrieval without proprietary database access (e.g., FactSet, Refinitiv IBES, or Bloomberg consensus vintage archives), a verified universe-wide top-five ranking cannot be definitively calculated.

In strict adherence to the missing-data policy, the formal strategy recommendation is classified as UNRESOLVED. Below, we explicitly define the predeclared reproducible methodology, universe specifications, and a provisional framework for evaluation when point-in-time consensus databases are available.

Note: No orders, paper accounts, trading venue connectors, background schedules, or ongoing monitoring scripts were placed, queued, deployed, or executed.

2. Predeclared Methodology & Strategy Conventions
To ensure reproducible implementation without post-hoc curve fitting, the following delegated conventions are declared prior to scoring:

Universe & Membership: S&P 500 index constituents effective at 16:00 EDT on 2026-09-30.

Consensus Provider & Horizon: Institutional Brokers' Estimate System (IBES) consensus or equivalent standard earnings aggregate, focusing on EPS for the Next Twelve Months (NTM) / FY1 consensus estimate.

Revision Observation Window: 30 calendar days ending at 2026-09-30 (Endpoint $T_0$: 2026-09-30; Endpoint $T_{-30}$: 2026-08-31).

Scoring Components:

Upward Revision Strength ($\text{REV\_STR}$): Percentage change in consensus NTM EPS over 30 days:

$$\text{REV\_STR}_i = \frac{\text{EPS}_{i, T_0} - \text{EPS}_{i, T_{-30}}}{\vert{}\text{EPS}_{i, T_{-30}}\vert{}}$$
Upward Revision Breadth ($\text{REV\_BRD}$): Net upward analyst revisions as a fraction of total analyst revisions over 30 days:

$$\text{REV\_BRD}_i = \frac{N_{i, \text{up}} - N_{i, \text{down}}}{N_{i, \text{total}}}$$
(If $N_{i, \text{total}} = 0$, $\text{REV\_BRD}_i = 0$).

6-Month Price Momentum ($\text{MOM\_6M}$): Total price return from 2026-03-31 close to 2026-09-30 close:

$$\text{MOM\_6M}_i = \frac{P_{i, \text{2026-09-30}}}{P_{i, \text{2026-03-31}}} - 1$$
Normalization & Composite Score: Each metric across the universe is converted to a cross-sectional percentile rank ($Z$-score or $0-100\%$ rank percentile $R$).

$$\text{Composite Score}_i = 0.35 \times R(\text{REV\_STR}_i) + 0.35 \times R(\text{REV\_BRD}_i) + 0.30 \times R(\text{MOM\_6M}_i)$$
Qualification Threshold & Eligibility:

Minimum analyst coverage: $N_{i, \text{total}} \ge 5$.

$\text{REV\_STR}_i > 0$ and $\text{REV\_BRD}_i > 0$ (must have positive net upward revisions).

Tie-Breaker: Higher 6-month price momentum ($\text{MOM\_6M}$); if still tied, higher market capitalization at $T_0$.

Portfolio Construction & Allocation: Top 5 qualifying companies ranked by Composite Score, weighted equally ($20\%$ target weight each). If fewer than 5 qualify, hold remaining weight in cash equivalents.

3. Coverage, Data Limitations & Unresolved Status
Universe Coverage Goal: 500 Constituents as of 2026-09-30.

Retrieved Public Data: Primary price endpoints for S&P 500 benchmarks and large-cap reference stocks are available via public market records.

Missing Decision-Driving Inputs:

Point-in-time NTM EPS consensus figures as of 2026-08-31 vs. 2026-09-30 across the full index.

Analyst upgrade/downgrade counts ($N_{\text{up}}, N_{\text{down}}, N_{\text{total}}$) within the exact 30-day window ending 2026-09-30.

Precise Gap: Point-in-time estimate revision archives are restricted behind commercial financial software APIs. Synthesizing revision breadth from delayed secondary news releases creates survivorship and availability bias, violating the frozen research contract.

Original strategy mandate (verbatim reference; scope override controls):
Run a public-disclosure-faithful SoFi Classic-style robo portfolio for a 10+ year horizon and a Moderately Aggressive risk profile exclusively in the Jango Alpaca paper-trading account. Treat this as a tax-neutral simulation and use the latest approved and publicly disclosed broad-bond target model, with broad USD bonds, long Treasuries, and mortgage-backed securities rather than municipal bonds. No additional user classification or clarification is required before implementation. All positions must be long-only and total 100%, including a target allocation of 1% to non-interest-bearing cash. Do not restrict the investment universe to only broad U.S., developed-market, emerging-market, Treasury, investment-grade bond, and TIPS sleeves. As a fallback snapshot, use the April 2026 aggregate mix of 83% stocks, 14% broad USD bonds including long-Treasury and mortgage-backed exposure, 2% gold, and 1% cash. Begin implementation as soon as the holdings and paper venue state are verified; missing profile details are never a blocker.

Review the model at least quarterly and monitor it continuously. Evaluate backward-looking investment and risk metrics, forward-looking capital-market estimates, benchmark-relative expectations, exposure, total cost, liquidity, and risk analytics. Change target holdings or weights only when approved and warranted. Do not state that SoFi uses a shrinkage covariance matrix, the objective max_w mu^T w - (lambda/2) w^T Sigma w, a particular lambda, or a 12% volatility target. When those methods are used as a transparent independent approximation, label them explicitly as such and report and persist their assumptions and outputs. Permit approved model-level allocation changes based on economic and risk analysis, but prohibit ad hoc market timing or off-model trades.

Monitor the account on every market day. Rebalance when an individual holding is more than approximately 5 percentage points from its target; cash is at least $50 above its 1% target; cash falls below 0.25% of portfolio value; the strategy or risk profile changes; or the approved model changes. Use deposits, dividends, and other distributions to reduce underweights before selling where practical. Hold investable cash below the $50 trading threshold until that threshold is reached. Version every model change and allow an implementation window of zero to three weeks. Do not wait for additional confirmation before placing the initial paper orders once holdings, quotes, and buying power are validated.

Use the paper broker's default lot handling for sales. Do not perform automated tax-loss harvesting or tax-aware optimization. Hold only approved ETFs, mutual funds, and cash; use no individual stocks, margin, direct leverage, or off-model trades. Model a 0.25% annual advisory fee monthly on average daily invested assets, excluding cash, and account for underlying fund expenses.

Persist each model version's effective date, paper-simulation profile inputs, holdings, target weights, cash target, data sources, assumptions, benchmark, expected net return and volatility when independently estimated, fees, rebalance triggers, transactions, implementation status, and rationale for every change. Do not characterize any undisclosed optimization method or risk target as SoFi's proprietary methodology.

Add an edge from reporting company A to company B when A explicitly mentions B; collapse repeated mentions to one edge per company pair per cycle, and exclude self-mentions, generic words, subsidiaries, and ambiguous entities that cannot be mapped confidently to a U.S.-listed ticker. Run standard PageRank on that graph with damping factor 0.85 and dangling-node redistribution. Equally own the 10 U.S.-listed stocks with the highest PageRank scores and rebalance only after a new earnings cycle. Persist the universe snapshot, source URLs and publication dates, mention-to-ticker evidence, graph edges, PageRank parameters, scores, and deterministic tie-break rules.

Frozen recommendation request:
Research and compute, if feasible within the permitted public-web surface and budget, the original earnings-mention PageRank recommendation over a frozen S&P 500 universe. Supply an auditable graph and scores before claiming a top-10, equal-weight recommendation. Otherwise report exactly why the ranking is unresolved; a familiar-company list or invented scores is not a substitute.

Frozen conventions:
- Before reporting ranks, declare the frozen constituent universe and effective timestamp, latest completed earnings-cycle definition and completion cutoff, required source coverage, and a transparent policy for fiscal calendars that do not align with calendar quarters. - Use primary-source company earnings releases, prepared remarks and company-published earnings-call transcripts for that cycle. - Collapse repeated mentions to one unweighted directed edge per ordered pair per cycle. Preserve exact supporting mention, source URL, publication date, reporting company, resolved company/ticker and exclusion reason for ambiguous candidates.
- Use damping 0.85, uniform teleportation across all frozen nodes, and uniform redistribution of dangling-node mass. Define scores to sum to 1. The recommendation remains UNRESOLVED / HOLD (Conditional) until a complete earnings-transcript corpus for all ~500 S&P 500 constituents is compiled and processed via full power iteration.

2. Frozen Conventions & Universe Specification
To ensure auditability and prevent post-hoc parameter tuning, the following deterministic conventions were established prior to research evaluation:

Frozen Constituent Universe: S&P 500 Constituent List as of the cutoff (2026-10-16T03:15:00Z). Total Node Count ($N$) = ~500.

Latest Completed Earnings-Cycle Definition: Q2 2026 Earnings Cycle (covering earnings reported through the cycle completion cutoff of October 15, 2026).

Fiscal Calendar Non-Alignment Policy: Companies with offset fiscal year-ends (e.g., Q1/Q3 reported within the same calendar window between July 1, 2026, and October 15, 2026) are evaluated using their single most recently published primary earnings release and transcript prior to the research cutoff.

Primary Source Scope & Filtering:

Allowed Sources: Company-issued earnings press releases, official management prepared remarks, and company-published earnings call transcripts.

Transcript Q&A Rule: Only remarks attributable to reporting company representatives (CEOs, CFOs, IR officers) are analyzed. Mentions made by sell-side analysts or external guests during the Q&A section are strictly excluded.

Entity Mapping & Exclusion Rules: Exclude self-mentions, generic words (e.g., "Apple" as fruit, "Amazon" as rainforest), subsidiaries (e.g., "Waymo" is not mapped to GOOGL; subsidiary mentions are excluded and NOT converted to parent tickers), and unmapped ambiguous candidates.

Edge Definition: Unweighted directed edge $A \to B$ from reporting company $A$ to target company $B$. Multiple mentions of $B$ within $A$'s transcript collapse to exactly one edge per cycle.

PageRank Mathematical Specification:

Damping Factor $d = 0.85$.

Teleportation Vector $v = \left[\frac{1}{N}, \frac{1}{N}, \dots, \frac{1}{N}\right]^T$.

Dangling Node Handling: Mass of nodes with out-degree $0$ is distributed uniformly across all $N$ nodes.

Iteration Method: Power iteration starting with $p^{(0)} = \left[\frac{1}{N}, \dots, \frac{1}{N}\right]^T$.

Convergence Criterion: $L_1$ norm difference $\Vert{}p^{(k+1)} - p^{(k)}\Vert{}_1 \le 10^{-10}$.

Tie-Breaking Rule: Descending by PageRank score; exact numerical ties broken by ascending canonical ticker string (e.g., GOOGL before MSFT).

3. Capability Gap & Data Limitation Disclosure
Under the enforced tool access constraints (public web search/fetch only, no Python/shell environment, no local code execution, and no bulk transcript database connection):

Corpus Extraction Limitation: Fetching, parsing, and verifying ~500 full-length primary earnings call transcripts across the S&P 500 universe for the latest completed cycle exceeds the budget and surface capabilities of live public web fetching within the target wall time.

Computational Limitation: Executing full power iteration to $10^{-10}$ $L_1$ convergence on a 500-node graph with dangling-node redistribution cannot be executed manually without risking arithmetic fabrication or unverified estimations.

Missing Data Policy Compliance: As mandated by the missing-data policy, presenting an arbitrary, incomplete subset of 10-20 companies or inventing scores is strictly prohibited. Consequently, the top-10 equal-weight ranking is formally declared UNRESOLVED.

4. Illustrative Demonstrator Graph (Methodology Verification Only)
Note: The following 5-node graph is provided strictly as a deterministic, reproducible methodological demonstrator to prove algorithmic logic. It does NOT represent the full S&P 500 universe result.

D. Power Iteration Matrix Formulation & Convergence
Initial uniform score $p_i^{(0)} = 0.2000000000$ for all $i \in \{1..5\}$.

Damping equation for node $i$:

$$p_i^{(k+1)} = \frac{1 - d}{N} + d \left( \sum_{j \in \text{In}(i)} \frac{p_j^{(k)}}{out(j)} + \sum_{j \in \text{Dangling}} \frac{p_j^{(k)}}{N} \right)$$
Applying $d = 0.85$, $N = 5$, and uniform dangling distribution, the converged scores after power iteration are:

### Methodology, Conventions, and Coverage
Frozen conventions applied (declared and fixed before any ranking or conclusion):
- Entry screen uses the 30-calendar-day interval based on public disclosure availability: (2026-10-16 minus 30 days, 2026-10-16], i.e., roughly 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-16 inclusive of availability dates. Original trade dates recorded but not the actionable clock.
- Require purchases attributed to ≥3 distinct members. Spouse/dependent transactions disclosed by a member count under that reporting member (who still counts once); ownership attribution labeled explicitly where available.
- Confirmed qualification requires sum of disclosed range lower bounds ≥$500,000. Upper-bound-only or midpoint possibilities reported separately as unconfirmed; midpoints never treated as observed exact amounts.
- Deterministic selection/tie rules (if >5 names qualified): rank by confirmed lower-bound total (desc), then distinct-member count (desc), then alphabetical ticker; select top ≤5 for equal weights. None qualified under available evidence.
- Holding clock (frozen interpretation, distinguished from any original wording): starts when the threshold first becomes publicly confirmable; lasts six calendar months (last calendar day if anniversary absent); ends earlier on any public disclosure of a sale of that security by a member whose purchase helped qualify the entry. Performance measurement (if any) starts at actionable disclosure availability.
- U.S.-listed stocks only (tickers tradable on U.S. exchanges). Bonds, private LLCs, non-equity, and non-priceable assets excluded from equity screen.

Coverage: Official sources are House Clerk PTR PDFs (https://disclosures-clerk.house.gov/) and Senate eFD (https://efdsearch.senate.gov/). Aggregators (Coldpine, Capitol Ledger, Yield Theory, Pelosi Tracker, Wealthnow, Benzinga, HoldingsIntel, etc.) parse these and were used as secondary indexes with links or references back to filings; primary PDFs were spot-checked where URLs surfaced. Aggregators note incomplete Senate feeds in places, scanned PDFs awaiting review, and typical 15–45+ day lags. Material unresolved conflicts: differing aggregator coverage of exact filing dates/amounts; some large ranges appear near the window edge (e.g., Sep 14).

Arithmetic: Lower bounds taken directly from reported ranges (e.g., $1,001–$15,000 → $1,001; $250,001–$500,000 → $250,001). Sums computed only on verified disclosure-window purchases of the same ticker by distinct members.

Exclude grants, gifts, option exercises, and automatic plan transactions. Hold at most five names and exit after six months or when one of the qualifying insiders reports an open-market sale.

Frozen recommendation request:
Screen SEC Form 4 filings for qualifying S&P 500 insider purchase clusters and recommend at most five names, with conditional six-month or qualifying-insider-sale exits.

Frozen conventions:
- Use S&P 500 membership effective at the reference market close. A cluster requires a CEO or CFO and a second distinct person who is a director, with roles supported as of the transaction dates. A dual-role person cannot satisfy both required people alone.
- Use transaction dates within the trailing 30 calendar dates ending on 2026-10-15 for the current purchase cluster, while requiring each relevant filing to have become publicly available by the research cutoff. Record both transaction dates and SEC acceptance times.
- Count only supported open-market purchases. Exclude grants, gifts, option exercises and automatic-plan transactions; use transaction codes, footnotes and plan disclosures together, and leave uncertain classifications unresolved rather than assuming that a purchase code alone proves eligibility.
- Declare deterministic selection/tie rules when more than five companies qualify and declare target weights, which the original leaves unspecified, before presenting the recommendation.
- For this research convention, six months runs from public availability of the final filing that establishes the cluster; the early exit is public disclosure of an open-market sale by any qualifying insider. Keep qualifying insider identities attached to each recommendation. No incumbent holdings are supplied.

Missing-data policy:
If membership, roles, plan status or filings cannot be established, identify the specific unresolved candidates and evidence gaps. Do not treat partial searching as a complete no-qualifier result.

Required output:
- State template ID, recommendation status, relevant decision time and the common research cutoff.
- Give the requested concrete recommendation when supported; otherwise an explicit unresolved/provisional/no-qualifier result that distinguishes insufficient evidence from verified absence.
- Provide a claim-to-evidence ledger for decision-driving facts: entity/identifier, value or assertion, observation period, publication/availability date, exact source URL, supporting record/passage and uncertainty.
- Expose methodology, chosen conventions, calculation inputs, coverage and material unresolved conflicts so the result can be independently checked.
- Explain the strategy's future review/change conditions as a conditional recommendation policy and state that no orders, account changes, schedules or monitors were executed.
- Company/membership evidence and cluster ledger with distinct insider identities, roles, transaction codes, dates, SEC acceptance times, footnotes and source URLs.
- At most five names, declared weights and selection rule, or explicit unresolved/no-trigger result.
- Per-name qualifying insider identity set and conditional exit rules.

Cite public URLs and decision-driving figures with dates. Do not ask the evaluator

**Template ID:** P05: Revision Leaders  
**Recommendation status:** Unresolved (insufficient company-level point-in-time historical consensus coverage).  
**Relevant decision time:** 2026-09-30 16:00 America/New_York (evaluation month-end).  
**Common research cutoff:** 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z.  
**Retrieval context:** Public web search/fetch performed on/after the cutoff using sources whose publication or availability dates allow verification of pre-decision information only. No post-month-end revisions treated as known on 2026-09-30.

### Declared Conventions (Fixed Before Any Rankings)
These are defensible choices declared in advance and held fixed. Differing alternatives would not be incorrect solely by differing.

- **Consensus provider:** FactSet as primary for aggregate/sector (most detailed public monthly/quarterly reports); Zacks/LSEG secondary for corroboration. Company-level mean consensus EPS.
- **Fiscal forecast period:** Primarily current-quarter (Q3 2026) and current-year (CY 2026) mean consensus EPS; NTM where explicitly available.
- **30-day endpoint convention:** Consensus snapshot as of 2026-09-30 versus snapshot as of 2026-08-31 (calendar-day window ending at decision close).
- **Upward-revision strength:** Percentage change in mean consensus EPS over the 30-day window: \((\text{EPS}_{2026-09-30} / \text{EPS}_{2026-08-31} - 1) \times 100\).
- **Breadth:** Count (or percentage of covering analysts) of upward revisions in the window (upward minus downward, or upward-only where reported).
- **Normalization:** Percentile ranks or z-scores of strength and breadth within the universe; composite revision score = average of the two normalized metrics.
- **Six-calendar-month momentum:** Price return \((P_{2026-09-30} / P_{2026-03-31} - 1)\), using regular-session closes, split-adjusted (dividends not added unless total-return series explicitly used).
- **Composite weights:** 50% normalized revision score + 50% normalized momentum.
- **Qualification threshold:** Positive revision strength (or positive net breadth) and positive momentum; prefer top-quartile on both components.
- **Missing-data treatment:** Exclude any name lacking both endpoint consensus snapshots with adequate analyst coverage, or lacking reliable price endpoints. No imputation.
- **Tie-breaker:** Higher revision strength, then higher momentum, then alphabetical ticker.
- **Fewer than five qualifiers:** Report the partial set of qualifiers (equal-weighted) and explicitly note the shortfall; do not fill with non-qualifiers. Distinguish partial sample from universe-wide ranking.
- **Universe:** S&P 500 membership effective at 2026-09-30 close (503 constituents per official factsheet).

### Universe and Coverage Statement
Official S&P 500 factsheet (as of 2026-09-30) reports 503 constituents, index level 7,651.54, float-adjusted market-cap weighted, covering ~80% of U.S. equity market cap. Top names by weight include NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, AVGO, GOOG, META, MU, TSLA.

Membership changes effective prior to the open on 2026-09-21 (quarterly rebalance): additions BE (Bloom Energy), ILMN (Illumina), P (Everpure); deletions TAP (Molson Coors), BLDR (Builders FirstSource), TTD (The Trade Desk). These were in force on 2026-09-30.

**Coverage gap (decision-driving):** Suitable public point-in-time company-level consensus snapshots for the exact 30-day endpoints (2026-08-31 vs 2026-09-30) across the S&P 500 universe, including revision counts/breadth and mean EPS changes, are unavailable. Aggregate and sector-level data exist; isolated company anecdotes exist; systematic company-level strength-and-breadth data do not. Therefore the ranking is unresolved per the missing-data policy. A labeled provisional/illustrative watchlist is supplied below and is **not** a verified top five.

### Aggregate and Sector Evidence (Verified, Not Company-Level)
FactSet: Q3 2026 bottom-up EPS estimate rose 1.4% from $88.64 (June 30) to $89.84 (September 30). Energy +18.0%, Information Technology +3.5%; eight sectors declined (Materials −10.2%, Consumer Staples −4.0%, Health Care −3.3%). Second consecutive quarter of aggregate increase (vs. historical average quarterly decline of ~2.2–2.5%). Positive guidance elevated (72 of 116 companies). CY 2026 bottom-up EPS also rose 6.2% over the quarter.

Zacks/LSEG corroborate a positive overall revisions trend through mid-to-late September, with Energy and Tech leading and breadth broadening relative to prior periods.

S&P 500 closed at 7,651.54 on 2026-09-30.

### Provisional Watchlist (Illustrative Only — Not Verified Ranking)
Based solely on sector-level upward revisions plus publicly noted company-level estimate increases (primarily since quarter-start, not verified 30-day endpoints), Energy refiners and certain Technology names show the strongest anecdotal upward revision activity. Six-month price momentum is not computed here due to incomplete paired data and is not claimed. Equal-weight illustrative names (provisional only):

- Marathon Petroleum (MPC) — large Q3/CY 2026 estimate increases noted in secondary sources.
- Valero Energy (VLO) — similar refining-margin-driven estimate lifts.
- Phillips 66 (PSX) — grouped with refiners in contemporaneous commentary.
- NVIDIA (NVDA) — IT sector leadership; frequent mention in growth/revision context.
- Micron Technology (MU) — IT/semiconductor exposure; top-weight and sector revision contributor.

These five are **not** ranked by the predeclared formula, do not constitute the strategy’s top five, and must not be treated as a recommendation. Coverage is partial; many other names lack verifiable 30-day snapshots.

### Methodology Exposure and Material Unresolved Conflicts
Predeclared formula and source/vintage conventions are fixed above. No computations or rankings were produced that could not be completed from available evidence. No silent tuning occurred. Aggregate/sector data and anecdotes are secondary to the required company-level strength-and-breadth series. No material conflicts among primary sources for the aggregate facts; the conflict is absence of the required granularity.

### Conditional Recommendation Policy (Future Reviews)
At each subsequent month-end (decision time = last regular-session close of the calendar month, America/New_York), re-apply the identical conventions: obtain point-in-time consensus snapshots for the trailing 30 calendar days and six-calendar-month prices for all then-current S&P 500 members; compute scores; select the top five qualifiers (or fewer if the threshold yields <5) at equal weights; rebalance conceptually only. Hold/change rules are conditional on the new ranking: names that remain in the top five are retained at equal weight; those that exit are replaced by new entrants. No current positions are assumed or invented.

**Template ID:** P07 AI Bottleneck  
**Recommendation status:** Provisional (power identified as binding under declared conventions; memory is a material competing hypothesis; three-company basket supported on exposure and guided FCF but not fully resolved given dual constraints).  
**Relevant decision time / research cutoff:** Research decision cutoff 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z; reference US market close 2026-10-15T16:00:00-04:00 (America/New_York). All facts drawn from material available by the cutoff; retrieval context is 2026-10-15/16 public web sources.

### Declared conventions (fixed before rankings/conclusions)
- **Geography:** United States and Western markets (primary locus of large-scale public AI capacity expansion, grid constraints, and US-listed equity exposure). Asia (notably China) has differentiated constraints (chips rather than power) and is treated as secondary.
- **Planning horizon:** Binding-constraint assessment through 2028 (aligned with cited shortfall windows); FCF outlook focused on company-guided full-year 2026 figures, supported by multi-year order backlogs and customer commitments.
- **Evidence freshness:** Prefer primary company disclosures/guidance and dated industry analyses published or available by ~15–16 October 2026. Secondary commentary is labeled as such.
- **Meaning of binding constraint:** The factor that most limits the rate of expansion of *usable* (energized and operational) AI compute capacity, evidenced by multi-year non-price-elastic lead times, quantified shortfalls, and rationing of deployments. Generic demand growth is not treated as evidence.
- **Direct-economic-exposure measure:** Material revenue share, order backlog growth, or primary business focus on power generation (turbines, on-site), distribution (switchgear, transformers, UPS, busways), or associated thermal management required to energize high-density AI racks.
- **FCF forecast horizon:** Management-guided 2026 free cash flow (or adjusted FCF where specified).
- **Allocation rule:** Equal weights (~33% each) of the three selected companies. No portfolio or risk model was supplied; this is a fresh recommendation.

### Five-category comparison (dated decision-driving evidence)
**1. Compute chips.** Constrained by advanced packaging (TSMC CoWoS allocated/limiting customer growth per mid-2026 statements), wafer capacity, and Nvidia supply commitments extending into 2028. Nvidia data-center revenue remains strong (e.g., Q2 figures cited in Oct 2026 reporting) and management projects continued growth despite bottlenecks. Not the primary limiter of usable capacity expansion; chips continue to ship at scale.  
**2. Memory (HBM/DRAM).** Severe and multi-year. Suppliers (Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung) report 2026–2027 HBM largely or fully committed; conventional DRAM contract prices rose ~90–95% QoQ in Q1 2026 (TrendForce references); HBM4 pricing spikes reported; Microsoft and AMD executives securing multi-year supply; Micron states supply tighter in 2027–2028 than 2026 with >75% of 2027 output committed. Competing hypothesis for binding status because accelerators cannot ship without HBM. Premiums can still allocate some volume on spot markets.  
**3. Networking.** Interconnect fabric and high-speed links (Ethernet back-end growth, InfiniBand, emerging co-packaged optics) limit utilization and scale-out efficiency. Important but not the primary barrier to the rate of adding new capacity.  
**4. Cooling.** High rack densities (50–100+ kW) render traditional air cooling inadequate; liquid cooling is required and being deployed. Solutions exist and are commercial (Vertiv and peers); secondary to power delivery.  
**5. Electrical power.** Multi-year constraints: grid interconnection typically 24–72 months (up to 5–7 years for large loads); generator step-up transformer lead times >160 weeks (Q1 2026, up from 143 weeks in 2024); high-voltage circuit breakers ~125 weeks; new transformer plants take 3–5 years. Morgan Stanley estimates ~32–33 GW / ~34% net US data-center power shortfall through 2028 after accounting for on-site generation and fuel cells (underlying analysis ~21 Sep 2026, reiterated early Oct). EMSNow (15 Oct 2026): “For some regions, e.g. the U.S., the binding limit is now power rather than chips or buildings.” GMI Cloud (Nvidia partner) CEO (interview early Oct, published ~13–14 Oct 2026): electricity is a more fundamental bottleneck than HBM because HBM can be obtained on the spot market at a premium while power requires transformers, transmission, and faces community/political barriers. North American vacancy record-low with heavy preleasing; shortage expected through at least 2027, easing unevenly from 2028.

### Binding-bottleneck conclusion and uncertainty
**Electrical power is assessed as the tightest current constraint on AI infrastructure expansion** under the declared conventions and geography. It exhibits the longest, least price-elastic lead times and is explicitly identified as binding for US capacity by multiple contemporaneous sources. Usable compute requires energization; chips and memory can be produced or allocated at premium prices, but multi-year grid and transformer timelines cannot be compressed similarly.

**Counterevidence / uncertainty:** Memory scarcity is extreme, multi-year, and could independently limit accelerator shipments even where power exists. Some commentary (e.g., Wing VC Sept 2026) treats memory as the present constraint with electrical equipment next. Power and memory are co-binding in practice; the ranking is sensitive to whether “expansion” is measured by component production or by energized operational capacity. Cooling and networking are real but secondary. Regional differences exist (China more chip-constrained). No single quantitative model ranks all five categories on identical metrics; the conclusion rests on lead-time and shortfall evidence available by the cutoff.

### Three-company recommendation (provisional)
Equal-weighted basket of three publicly traded companies with the most direct economic exposure to the electrical-power constraint and strongest supported free-cash-flow outlook:

1. **Vertiv Holdings (VRT)** — Most concentrated pure-play exposure to data-center power distribution, UPS, and thermal/cooling systems required for high-density AI racks. 2026 guidance (post-Q2): net sales ~$14B midpoint, organic growth ~30–32%, adjusted free cash flow $2.4–2.6B. Q2 adjusted FCF $925M (+234% YoY). Direct economics: every high-density AI deployment needs its power and thermal solutions.  
2. **GE Vernova (GEV)** — Exposure via gas turbines (behind-the-meter / on-site power), transformers (Prolec GE), and electrification equipment. Data-center orders >$5B YTD 2026 (more than double full-year 2025); gas equipment backlog + slot reservations 116 GW. 2026 free-cash-flow guidance raised to $11.5–12.5B. Largest absolute guided FCF of the three.  
3. **Eaton (ETN)** — Switchgear, busways, UPS, and power-management equipment for data centers; expanding liquid-cooling capability. Data-center-related revenue growth cited ~65%; US data-center backlog described as equivalent to multi-year build rates. 2026 free-cash-flow guidance ~$3.9–4.3B (reaffirmed with raised organic growth 11–13% and adjusted EPS $13.40–13.60). Diversified but material and growing AI exposure.

**Weights:** ~33% each.  
**Exposure linkage:** All three supply (or enable) the electrical equipment and generation needed to energize AI capacity that is otherwise rationed by grid and transformer lead times.  
**FCF assumptions:** Relies on company guidance and reported backlogs/order growth; not independent forecasts. Absolute FCF is strongest at GEV; relative growth and purity strongest at VRT.

**If memory were instead treated as binding,** Micron (MU) would dominate on pure exposure and FCF (Q4 FY2026 adjusted FCF ~$33B; 2027 HBM largely committed at higher prices; management expects continued sequential growth and tight supply into 2028). It is excluded under the power convention.

### Conditional recommendation policy and rotation triggers
Monthly reassessment is required. Rotate or change the basket only when new evidence (company filings, primary grid/transformer lead-time data, or quantified shortfall revisions) demonstrates that the binding bottleneck has changed (e.g., sustained multi-year relief in US power lead times while memory remains sold out, or the reverse). With no incumbent portfolio supplied, this is an initial recommendation; hold the basket unless such evidence appears. Competing hypotheses remain open.

**No orders were placed or queued, no broker/trading-venue/private-account/connector access occurred, no account state was changed, no schedule was deployed, and no ongoing monitoring was started.** This is a research memo only.

### Claim-to-evidence ledger (decision-driving facts)
- **US power as binding (EMSNow):** “For some regions, e.g. the U.S., the binding limit is now power rather than chips or buildings.” Observation: H1 2026 vacancy/construction data; grid 24–72 months, transformers >160 weeks. Published ~15 Oct 2026. URL: https://www.emsnow.com/global-datacenter-capacity-where-are-the-bottlenecks/. Uncertainty: regional synthesis; secondary aggregation of CBRE, Wood Mackenzie, etc.
- **Morgan Stanley ~32–33 GW / 34% shortfall through 2028:** After on-site measures. Underlying ~21 Sep 2026 analysis; reiterated early Oct. - **GMI Cloud CEO (Nvidia partner):** Electricity more fundamental than HBM; HBM obtainable at premium, power requires multi-year infrastructure and faces political barriers.
