6. Conditional holding, exit and performance policy

These are recommendations for a future verified state, not instructions executed here.

  Entry clock: Start at the first public-availability instant when three distinct members and $500,000 in purchase lower bounds become confirmable within the rolling interval—not at any member’s original transaction date.

  Holding period: Six calendar months from that instant, using the last calendar day if the anniversary date does not exist.

  Early exit: Recommend ending the entry when any member whose purchase contributed to that qualifying entry publicly discloses a sale of the same security. A partial sale counts. A spouse/dependent sale is attributed to its reporting member. This is the frozen interpretation, not an inference that the original mandate unambiguously specified these details.

  Contributor set: Freeze all members whose eligible purchases were included at threshold confirmation. If a filing simultaneously establishes a trigger and discloses a qualifying contributor’s sale, treat the sale as controlling and recommend no new entry.

  Conditional hold: If an incumbent entry is later supplied and verified, recommend holding only while its six-month period remains open and no contributor sale has become public. Missing sale coverage means exit status is unresolved, not “no sale.”

  Performance: Report no returns here. For a future calculation, record the disclosure-confirmation instant and use the first regular-session opening price strictly after that instant as the reproducible entry mark; use the first regular-session open after an exit event as the exit mark. Measure total return with dividends and corporate actions handled consistently, and identify the gap between the information timestamp and price timestamp. Never use pre-disclosure transaction prices or retrospectively use the October 15 close for a signal confirmed afterward.

7. Precise unresolved requirements

A definitive recommendation requires a complete cutoff-bounded inventory from both chambers; first-public-availability evidence; full row extraction and amendment reconciliation; security/listing verification; historical threshold reconstruction; and contributor-sale review.

The research found accessible primary evidence for the partial ledger and a material mismatch between secondary cluster methodology and the frozen mandate. It did not establish the complete inventory or availability history needed to confirm either qualifying names or their absence.

No orders were placed or queued. No private accounts, brokers or private connectors were accessed. No local files or shells were used. No account changes, schedules or ongoing monitors were executed.

1. Fixed methodology and selection conventions

The following conventions were fixed before presenting conclusions:

  Universe: S&P 500 companies effective at the reference close, identified by issuer CIK. Multiple share classes do not create separate company slots.

  Required people: one CEO or CFO plus a different person who was a director on the relevant transaction date. A CEO/director cannot satisfy both legs alone. Roles are issuer-specific.

  Transaction eligibility: require supported open-market purchases, not merely code P. Exclude awards, gifts, exercises, dividend reinvestments and automatic employee/compensation-plan purchases. Uncertain open-market or plan classifications remain unresolved.

  Availability: require relevant filings accepted by the cutoff. SEC acceptance is the operational public-availability proxy; this trial did not independently audit dissemination latency.

  Cluster establishment: use the earliest acceptance time by which an eligible two-person pair is established. If several pairs establish a company simultaneously, choose the pair with the lexicographically lowest ordered reporting-owner CIK tuple. Attach that identity set to the recommendation.

  Selection: if more than five companies qualify and remain free of an exit trigger, sort by earliest cluster-establishing acceptance, then ascending issuer CIK. Select the first five. No discretionary valuation or purchase-size ranking.

  Target weights: 20% of the hypothetical P04 sleeve per selected company. Unused slots remain unallocated; fewer names are not automatically increased above 20%.

  Amendments: evaluate amendments available by the cutoff; do not use later amendments retrospectively to repair the cutoff information set.

P05: Revision Leaders — Research Recommendation Memo
Memo date: October 16, 2026
Template ID: P05
Status: UNRESOLVED — insufficient point-in-time evidence; no verified five-name recommendation.

Decision time: September 30, 2026, 16:00 America/New_York, or 2026-09-30T20:00:00Z.
Common research cutoff: 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z.
Reference market close: October 15, 2026, 16:00 America/New_York. That later close is not an input to the September recommendation.
Retrieval context: Public web searches and page retrievals during this October 16, 2026 session. Retrieval dates are not publication dates or proof of historical data availability.

1. Recommendation

Do not designate or endorse a September 30 five-stock Revision Leaders portfolio from the evidence obtained.

The ranking is unresolved because I did not obtain the required company-level, point-in-time consensus snapshots and analyst-level endpoint records for August 31 and September 30, 2026. I also did not establish a complete September 30 constituent roster or assemble the corresponding six-month price inputs.

This is insufficient evidence, not a finding that no companies qualified. No securities have been assigned recommendation weights. In particular, there is no verified universe-wide top five and no provisional stock watchlist presented as a substitute.

The conditional target, if established with adequate evidence, is five qualifying companies at 20% each.

2. Fixed methodology and source conventions

The following are delegated research choices, fixed for this reconstruction before any ranking. They are proposed conventions, not claims that the required observations were retrieved.

Universe and company representation

Use S&P 500 membership effective at September 30, 2026, 16:00 New York time. Start from an authenticated earlier constituent roster and apply every announced change effective through that time.

Rank companies, not duplicate share classes. For a company with multiple constituent share classes, select the class with the highest median daily dollar volume during the preceding 60 trading sessions, using only data available by the decision time. Break a volume tie by ascending permanent security identifier. Apply the convention before calculating company rankings.

Consensus provider and forecast period

Use FactSet Estimates, default consensus class, annual EPS, with its standard 100-day consensus window. Do not mix providers, accounting classes, EPS definitions, currencies or fiscal periods.

Select the annual FY1 period identified at the September 30 decision time, then lock its exact fiscal-period-end date at both endpoints. Do not compare rolling FY1 labels if they refer to different fiscal years.

FactSet documents historical consensus and analyst/broker detail as separate data categories. Its manual identifies FY1 as the current unreported fiscal year and describes the default consensus window. These documents establish intended field definitions, not the missing 2026 observations. [E2, E4] ([insight.factset.com](https://insight.factset.com/resources/factset-consensus-estimates-datafeed))

Endpoint and vintage convention

  t0 = August 31, 2026, 16:00 America/New_York.
  t1 = September 30, 2026, 16:00 America/New_York.
  Revision interval = (t0, t1], exactly 30 calendar days.

Require archived “as-known” records with provider receipt/availability timestamps no later than each endpoint. A report’s research date alone is insufficient. Exclude later corrections and backfilled contributions unavailable at the endpoint.

Important source limitation: FactSet’s documented PIT consensus product uses local-midnight snapshots, not 16:00 snapshots. Its white paper also describes that product as consensus-only. Therefore, that product alone would not satisfy this fixed exact-close convention or supply the matched contributor detail required below. Genuine archived endpoint records would be necessary; midnight observations would not be silently relabeled as close observations. [E1, E3] ([insight.factset.com](https://insight.factset.com/resources/at-a-glance-factset-estimates-point-in-time-consensus))

Revision strength

For company i, let C0 and C1 be the provider’s mean annual EPS consensus for the same locked fiscal period at t0 and t1.

  S_i = C1 / C0 - 1

Require both consensus values to be positive. This avoids unstable percentage changes around zero and treats loss-making cases as outside this convention rather than assigning misleading large scores.

Revision breadth

Match contributors by stable broker/analyst identifier, using one active estimate per contributor, in the same consensus class at both endpoints.

  N_i = number of matched contributors.
  U_i = contributors whose endpoint EPS estimate increased.
  D_i = contributors whose endpoint EPS estimate decreased.
  Z_i = contributors whose endpoint EPS estimate was unchanged.
  N_i = U_i + D_i + Z_i.
  B_i = (U_i - D_i) / N_i.

Count each matched contributor once. This measures net endpoint revision breadth, not the number of intervening research reports. New initiations and withdrawals do not count as upgrades or downgrades.

Require at least five consensus contributors at each endpoint and at least five matched contributors. Show total contributors, matched contributors, initiations and withdrawals separately. Provider summary revision fields are not substitutes unless their interval and counting definitions exactly match this convention.

Six-calendar-month momentum

Use regular-session closing prices on March 30 and September 30, 2026. For a non-trading anchor date in future reviews, use the last regular-session close on or before that date.

  M_i = P_i(t1) / P_i(March 30, 2026) - 1.

Express both prices on the September 30 share basis, adjusting for splits effective within the interval. Exclude cash dividends: this is price momentum, not total return. Exclude later corporate actions and later-restated adjustment factors. Require sufficient history; do not splice a spun-off company to its former parent.

The intended public price source is Nasdaq historical daily quotes, reconciled to issuer/exchange corporate-action records. Nasdaq’s public overview describes historical prices and volumes, but it does not establish the specific prices or adjustment histories needed here. [E6] ([nasdaq.com](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/quotes/historical))

Normalization and composite

Across companies with all required valid inputs, calculate ascending midrank percentiles separately for S, B and M:

  Percentile(x_i) = (midrank(x_i) - 1) / (n - 1).

Use 0.5 if n = 1. Higher values receive higher percentiles. Do not sector-neutralize or winsorize.

  Score_i = 0.40 × Percentile(S_i)
          + 0.30 × Percentile(B_i)
          + 0.30 × Percentile(M_i).

This assigns 70% of composite weight to revisions and 30% to momentum.

Qualification and deterministic ties

Require all of the following:

  S_i > 0.
  B_i > 0.
  M_i > 0.
  U_i >= 3.
  Contributor and data-validity requirements satisfied.

Rank qualifiers by descending unrounded composite score. Break exact ties by higher breadth, then higher strength, then higher momentum, then ascending permanent company identifier.

Missing data and fewer than five names

Do not impute estimates, breadth or prices. Mark unavailable evidence separately from a verified failure to qualify.

If complete universe accounting establishes only k qualifying companies, where 1 <= k < 5, recommend 20% per qualifier and leave the remaining allocation unassigned in this research model; do not increase concentration. If complete evidence establishes zero qualifiers, report “verified no qualifiers.”

If material universe or input coverage remains unknown, report an unresolved ranking. A partial sample cannot be called the S&P 500 top five.

The principal unresolved source conflict is between the chosen exact-close endpoints and the documented midnight PIT product. Ordinary historical research-date data or midnight snapshots cannot silently resolve it. A different endpoint convention would be a separately disclosed methodological trial, not a repair made after seeing results.

This search did not establish that suitable public historical data cannot exist. It established that the necessary records were not obtained and verified here. Product descriptions, current consensus, analyst ratings and price-only screens cannot resolve that gap.

At each future completed month-end, issue a new research recommendation using the same fixed methodology and only information available by that month-end close.

Conditionally retain a previously recommended company if it remains in the verified qualifying top five. Recommend replacement if it leaves that set, fails qualification or leaves the eligible universe. Recommend restoring equal 20% weights when five names are verified. Apply the stated partial-allocation rule when fewer than five are demonstrably qualified.

If evidence becomes inadequate, label the update unresolved rather than inferring deterioration or recommending a forced sale. No current holdings were supplied, so this memo makes no position-specific hold, sell or rebalance claim.

P07: AI Bottleneck
Dated research memo — October 16, 2026
Status: PROVISIONAL power-bottleneck assessment; definitive three-company basket unresolved.

Decision time: October 15, 2026, 11:15 p.m. America/New_York.
Common research cutoff: 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z.
Reference valuation time: October 15, 2026, 4:00 p.m. EDT.
Retrieval context: Public webpages and documents retrieved October 16, 2026. Publication dates, rather than retrieval dates, determine eligibility. No reference-close prices or valuation multiples were verified; this is an exposure-and-cash-flow recommendation, not a price-sensitive entry recommendation.

1. Fixed conventions and method

Geography and horizon
    U.S. AI-data-center expansion during the next 12–24 months, through approximately October 2028. Global publicly traded suppliers are eligible.

Evidence freshness
    Prefer records published within 180 days before the cutoff. Older records establish mechanisms and historical experience, not proof that an earlier shortage remains unresolved.

Meaning of binding constraint
    The input whose shortage most delays energised, usable AI capacity on a project’s critical path. Demand growth, order growth and market size alone do not qualify.

    The conceptual test is:
        Commissioning date = latest readiness date among compute, memory,
        networking, cooling and electrical power.

    A national conclusion ideally requires project-level, capacity-weighted readiness dates. Those data were not obtained, so the result is qualitative rather than a computed national bottleneck ranking.

Direct economic exposure
    First preference: disclosed AI/data-center revenue or orders attributable to products or services that relieve the constraint.
    Second preference: relevant segment revenue divided by consolidated revenue, explicitly identified as an imperfect proxy.
    Backlog is supporting evidence, not equivalent to revenue, cash flow or an independently verified shortage.

Company universe
    Eaton, GE Vernova, Schneider Electric, Vertiv, Siemens Energy, ABB, Hubbell and Quanta Services. This fixed, purposive supplier roster is not an exhaustive global equity universe.

FCF definition and horizon
    Assess FY2026–FY2027 operating cash flow less capital expenditure, including capitalised software where disclosed. Preserve and reconcile company-specific non-GAAP definitions. Do not substitute EBITDA or adjusted EPS for FCF.

Selection and allocation
    Require a causal connection to the bottleneck, disclosed economic exposure, and supported cash generation after capacity investment. Missing comparable evidence prevents a definitive “strongest three” ranking.
    Any three-company research basket is equal-weighted: one-third each. No optimisation or backtest was performed.

2. Recommendation

Electrical power—specifically timely access to deliverable grid capacity and the equipment needed to connect or supply it—is the leading bottleneck hypothesis for U.S. expansion over the declared horizon. It is not established as the single binding constraint across all U.S. projects.

The strongest independent evidence is the IEA’s October 14, 2026 assessment: grid capacity, connection queues and permitting constrain development; Texas and Virginia have exceptionally large requested connection pipelines; onsite generation also depends on equipment with long waits. This supports a commissioning constraint, not merely a demand-growth narrative. The IEA also warns that queues contain speculative or duplicate projects. [E1] ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/reports/powering-artificial-intelligence/executive-summary))

Memory is a serious competing hypothesis, not a dismissed runner-up. Micron’s September 30 prepared remarks forecast continuing supply constraints through 2027–2028, while NVIDIA’s August 26 call describes its own outlook as supply-constrained and identifies memory scarcity. These records prevent a high-confidence declaration that power alone is binding. [E3–E4] ([s25.q4cdn.com](https://s25.q4cdn.com/621799436/files/doc_financials/2026/q4/Q4-FY26-Prepared-Remarks.pdf))

Provisional power-exposure research basket:
    GE Vernova — NYSE: GEV — one-third.
    Eaton — NYSE: ETN — one-third.
    Quanta Services — NYSE: PWR — one-third.

These are complementary provisional exposures, not verified first-, second- and third-place rankings. The full mandate remains unresolved because comparable FY2027 FCF forecasts and AI-specific economic-exposure measures were not established across the roster. There is insufficient evidence to certify the strongest three; this is not evidence that three qualifying companies do not exist.

3. Five-category comparison

Electrical power
    Evidence: The October 14 IEA report identifies actual connection and equipment constraints. Older Virginia legislative research explains the critical-path mechanism: new data-center load cannot be connected until required transmission improvements are operational. [E1–E2] ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/reports/powering-artificial-intelligence/executive-summary))

    Assessment: Leading hypothesis for new-site commissioning. More chips cannot make an unenergised site usable.

    Counterevidence: Relocation, phased connections, flexible loads and onsite generation can alleviate the constraint. Queue totals overstate committed demand. No capacity-weighted U.S. delay attribution was obtained. [E1] ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/reports/powering-artificial-intelligence/executive-summary))

Memory
    Evidence: On September 30, Micron forecast supply-constrained DRAM and NAND markets in calendar 2027 and 2028, with HBM shipments growing faster than conventional DRAM. Its discussion attributes continuing tightness partly to cleanroom limitations. [E3] ([s25.q4cdn.com](https://s25.q4cdn.com/621799436/files/doc_financials/2026/q4/Q4-FY26-Prepared-Remarks.pdf))

    Assessment: Strong competing bottleneck, particularly for equipment entering already-powered facilities.

    Uncertainty: Supplier forecasts are interested-party evidence. Memory-market tightness does not quantify how much U.S. commissioning it delays relative to electricity.

Compute chips
    Evidence: NVIDIA’s August 26 earnings transcript says supply remains a bottleneck through its fiscal 2028. The same discussion identifies memory scarcity, so “compute supply” cannot be treated as proof that GPU silicon itself is the limiting component. [E4] ([investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/files/content_files/TRANSCRIPT_-NVIDIA-Corp-NVDA-US-Q2-2027-Earnings-Call-26-August-2026-5_00-PM-ET.pdf))

    Assessment: A genuine competing system-supply constraint. The retrieved evidence does not separate wafer fabrication, packaging, memory, rack integration and customer-site readiness sufficiently to rank compute silicon independently.

Networking
    Evidence: Arista’s August 4 release reports the introduction of 1.6-Tbps AI fabric platforms, including liquid-cooled options. It establishes product advancement, not a quantified networking shortage. [E5] ([arista.com](https://www.arista.com/company/news/press-release/24401-pr-20260804?utm_source=openai))

    Assessment: Necessary infrastructure, but no retrieved dated evidence establishes networking as the dominant national commissioning constraint. This is insufficient evidence, not verified absence of local networking bottlenecks.

Cooling
    Evidence: Vertiv’s July 29 release reports temporary supply-chain congestion and phased project-execution timing effects, while increasing capacity investment. The release covers both power and thermal infrastructure and does not isolate cooling-caused delays. [E6] ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1674101/000162828026050323/q22026exhibit991vrt07292026.htm))

    Assessment: Credible site- and rack-specific constraint; not established as the dominant nationwide constraint. No comparable dataset of cooling readiness versus energisation readiness was obtained.

Conclusion from the comparison
    Power is the most defensible working hypothesis for greenfield commissioning. Memory or integrated compute supply may bind first at powered sites. A different geography or a shorter equipment-delivery horizon could defensibly produce a different conclusion.

4. Provisional companies: economics and FCF

GE Vernova — GEV

    Exposure: Generation equipment and grid infrastructure address upstream electrical availability. Management reported more than $5 billion of year-to-date Electrification data-center orders at its July 22 release. Power plus Electrification represented approximately 82% of Q2 revenue using rounded segment figures; this is broad electrical-system exposure, not AI revenue purity. [E7] ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1996810/000199681026000147/gev2q2026form8-k.pdf))

    FCF: FY2026 management guidance was $11.5–$12.5 billion. However, customer down payments and reservation agreements materially supported cash generation. Treat this as cash received against future obligations, not a perpetual run rate. [E7–E8] ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1996810/000199681026000147/gev2q2026form8-k.pdf))

    Research assumption: Scarcity can support orders and pricing, but FY2027 FCF need not rise if advance-payment inflows normalise. A comparable FY2027 forecast remains unresolved.

Eaton — ETN

    Exposure: Electrical Americas and Electrical Global supplied 75.8% of Q2 revenue. Electrical backlog grew 43% year over year. This broad electrical exposure includes non-AI markets and thermal products; it is not a measured share of AI-grid revenue. [E9] ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000027/etn06302026exhibit99.htm))

    FCF: Q2 operating cash flow of $1.127 billion less $253 million of capital expenditure produced $874 million FCF. This verifies cash generation, not a full-year forecast. A sufficiently supported FY2026–FY2027 FCF path was not established in the retrieved records. [E9] ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000027/etn06302026exhibit99.htm))

    Research assumption: Backlog conversion must outpace working-capital and capacity-investment requirements. Its inclusion is provisional specifically because the forward FCF qualification is incomplete.

Quanta Services — PWR

    Exposure: Infrastructure construction and installation connect the thesis to physical execution. Its disclosed services span utilities, generation and load centers, but also communications and pipelines. AI-only revenue and FCF are unresolved. [E10] ([investors.quantaservices.com](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/402/quanta-services-reports-second-quarter-2026-results))

    FCF: FY2026 management guidance was $2.0–$2.5 billion using net capital expenditure. Q2 company-defined FCF was $885.968 million; on gross capital expenditure, the comparable calculation is $864.489 million. [E10] ([investors.quantaservices.com](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/402/quanta-services-reports-second-quarter-2026-results))

    Research assumption: Construction volume can translate into cash only if collection timing, labour productivity and contract execution remain favourable. FY2027 cash generation is not independently established.

Why not certify another combination?

    Vertiv has a clearer FY2026 cash-flow guide than the retrieved Eaton evidence: $2.4–$2.6 billion adjusted FCF. Its historical reconciliation subtracts capital expenditure and software investment without an earnings-style add-back. But its power/cooling mix does not establish greater exposure to the upstream connection constraint. [E6] ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1674101/000162828026050323/q22026exhibit991vrt07292026.htm))

    Siemens Energy reported strong cash flow, but the headline measure is pre-tax and advance-payment-sensitive. ABB and Hubbell also have positive cash-generation evidence. Schneider’s half-year record is relevant, but its October 16 Q3 material cannot automatically be admitted at the frozen cutoff. These alternatives remain unresolved competitors, not rejected investments. [E11–E14] ([siemensenergy.com](https://www.siemensenergy.com/global/en/home/investor-relations.html))

5. Reproducible calculations and limitations

Only simple arithmetic was performed; no simulated rankings or undisclosed model were used.

    Eaton broad electrical revenue share:
        ($3,951m + $2,517m) / $8,531m = 75.8%.
        Inputs: Q2 segment table. [E9] ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000027/etn06302026exhibit99.htm))

    GE Vernova broad Power-plus-Electrification share:
        ($5.5bn + $3.6bn) / $11.104bn ≈ 82.0%.
        Rounded segment inputs limit precision. [E7] ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1996810/000199681026000147/gev2q2026form8-k.pdf))

    Quanta Q2 gross-capex FCF:
        $1,095.444m operating cash flow − $230.955m capex
        = $864.489m.
        Adding $21.479m of asset-sale/related insurance proceeds gives
        company-defined FCF of $885.968m. [E10] ([investors.quantaservices.com](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/402/quanta-services-reports-second-quarter-2026-results))

These percentages are not comparable AI-exposure scores. No exposure ratio was invented for missing disclosures.

Material gaps:
    No committed-project dataset jointly measures all five readiness dates.
    No normalised FY2027 FCF forecasts were completed across all eight companies.
    No verified reference-close prices, market capitalisations or FCF yields.
    Backlogs and reservations differ in contractual quality and timing.
    The GE Vernova PDF’s H1 summary image shows $9.913 billion FCF, whereas its reconciliation shows $9.897 billion. That conflict is unresolved; neither H1 figure drives this recommendation. [E7] ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1996810/000199681026000147/gev2q2026form8-k.pdf))

6. Claim-to-evidence ledger

All entries below are primary sources: issuer records or original governmental/intergovernmental research. Issuer guidance is management expectation, not an independently verified outcome. Supporting passages are paraphrased unless quotation marks appear.

E1 — IEA / electrical-power constraint
    Period: Integration conditions and policies surveyed through 2026; prospective constraints.
    Available: October 14, 2026, established by the report landing page.
    Record: Executive-summary sections on demand visibility and operational integration identify large Texas/Virginia queues, speculative requests, non-firm connections and long waits for onsite-generation equipment.
    Uncertainty: Broad assessment; not a U.S. AI-only project-delay census.
    URLs:
    https://www.iea.org/reports/powering-artificial-intelligence
    https://www.iea.org/reports/powering-artificial-intelligence/executive-summary
    ([iea.org](https://www.iea.org/reports/powering-artificial-intelligence))

E2 — Virginia JLARC / transmission mechanism
    Period: Historical conditions through 2024.
    Available: Report dated December 9, 2024; retrieved copy hosted in the state’s 2025 repository.
    Record: Printed page 36 explains that required transmission improvements must precede new load additions; recounts a 2022 pause and a July 2024 customer notice of additional connection time.
    Uncertainty: Historical background, not proof that those particular constraints persist in October 2026.
    URL:
    https://rga.lis.virginia.gov/Published/2025/RD206/PDF
    ([rga.lis.virginia.gov](https://rga.lis.virginia.gov/Published/2025/RD206/PDF))

E3 — Micron / NASDAQ: MU / memory supply
    Period: Calendar 2027–2028 outlook.
    Available: September 30, 2026, dated on prepared remarks.
    Record: Market-outlook page forecasts continuing NAND/DRAM supply constraints and explains cleanroom limitations.
    Uncertainty: Management forecast; no independently measured U.S. deployment loss.
    URL:
    https://s25.q4cdn.com/621799436/files/doc_financials/2026/q4/Q4-FY26-Prepared-Remarks.pdf
    ([s25.q4cdn.com](https://s25.q4cdn.com/621799436/files/doc_financials/2026/q4/Q4-FY26-Prepared-Remarks.pdf))

E4 — NVIDIA / NASDAQ: NVDA / integrated compute supply
    Period: Q2 FY2027 call and outlook through FY2028.
    Available: August 26, 2026.
    Record: Transcript PDF page 7 describes supply as a bottleneck and discusses memory scarcity.
    Uncertainty: Does not isolate GPU-silicon scarcity from other system inputs.
    URL:
    https://investor.nvidia.com/files/content_files/TRANSCRIPT_-NVIDIA-Corp-NVDA-US-Q2-2027-Earnings-Call-26-August-2026-5_00-PM-ET.pdf

7. Conditional monthly review and change policy

These are recommended future research rules, not deployed monitoring.

At each monthly decision:
    Reassess the same U.S. geography and 12–24-month horizon.
    Refresh dated project-readiness, utility-connection and supplier-delivery evidence.
    Separate committed projects from speculative queues.
    Reconcile FCF definitions and distinguish customer advances from sustainable cash generation.

Conditional hold:
    If an incumbent power basket exists, retain the bottleneck thesis while power remains on the critical path and no stronger contradictory evidence emerges. Do not infer that such holdings currently exist.

Conditional rotation:
    Recommend changing the bottleneck only when at least two independent, dated records—including a utility, operator or customer record—show another category delaying committed capacity after power readiness is secured. Prefer quantified delayed capacity or documented commissioning dates over supplier demand commentary.

    Rotate toward memory if powered projects are demonstrably delayed by HBM/DRAM allocation.
    Rotate toward compute if silicon or packaging shortages are separately established.
    Rotate toward cooling or networking if those systems demonstrably become the remaining commissioning gate.

Qualification before a definitive basket:
    Complete comparable FY2027 FCF work and AI-relevant exposure mapping across the fixed roster. Until then, preserve the provisional status rather than manufacture a strongest-three ranking.

P09: Four-Regime Rotation
Dated research recommendation — October 16, 2026

Template ID: P09
Status: Supported initial research recommendation under the fixed convention below.
Evaluation decision time: September 30, 2026, 16:00 America/New_York (2026-09-30T20:00:00Z).
Common research cutoff: 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z, equivalent to October 15, 2026, 23:15 EDT.
Reference market close: October 15, 2026, 16:00 EDT. No ETF prices or valuation calculations are required for this weight-only recommendation.
Retrieval context: Public records retrieved on October 16, 2026, after the research cutoff. Historical decision inputs come from explicitly dated September releases; later observations are excluded.

1. Fixed methodology and conventions

These are delegated research choices, not a claim that the original strategy specified these particular economic proxies. They remain fixed for this trial.

Growth series:
  BLS CES0000000001 — all employees, total nonfarm, seasonally adjusted, in thousands. Payroll momentum is the chosen proxy for U.S. growth, not a direct measure of real GDP. The BLS series metadata confirms the identifier, coverage and units. Current numerical observations on that metadata page are not used as historical inputs. ([data.bls.gov](https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/CES0000000001))

Inflation series:
  BLS CUSR0000SA0 — CPI-U, all items, U.S. city average, seasonally adjusted, base 1982–84=100. The signal uses the officially published monthly percentage changes associated with this series, at their published one-decimal precision. It does not use core CPI or year-over-year inflation. ([data.bls.gov](https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/CUSR0000SA0))

Transformations:
  Let E(m,v) denote payroll employment in observation month m and release vintage v.
  Monthly payroll gain: J(m,v) = E(m,v) − E(m−1,v).
  Growth acceleration: G = J(m,v) − J(m−1,v).

  Let P(m,v) denote the CPI index.
  Monthly inflation rate: R(m,v) = the BLS-published, one-decimal monthly percentage change corresponding to 100 × [P(m,v)/P(m−1,v) − 1].
  Inflation acceleration: I = R(m,v) − R(m−1,v).

Comparison window:
  Compare the latest eligible observation month with its immediately preceding month. For this decision, that is August versus July 2026. No smoothing, annualization, fitted thresholds or alternative-window selection is applied.

Release, lag and revision policy:
  At each evaluation month-end, use the latest scheduled national Employment Situation and CPI releases published by 16:00 ET that day, including any explicitly dated corrections available by that time.
  Use both comparison observations from the same release vintage within each series; the two series need not share a publication date.
  Require both series to cover the immediately preceding calendar month. If either required release or comparison value is unavailable, do not substitute an older month, nowcast or current revised database value: leave the new regime unresolved.
  Use revisions already incorporated into the eligible release. Do not independently splice preliminary benchmark announcements into the published monthly payroll series.
  Never rewrite a historical classification using releases published after its evaluation time.

Sign, zero-change and initialization rules:
  Positive acceleration = rising; negative acceleration = falling.
  Exactly zero at the chosen published precision retains that series’ previously established monthly sign.
  If zero occurs without a previously established sign, initialization remains unresolved.
  Initialize only when both signs are resolved. No prior regime or portfolio is assumed.
  Neither zero-change nor missing-data handling is needed for this reconstruction.

2. Reconstructed signs and recommendation

Growth:
  July payroll gain: +21 thousand.
  August payroll gain: +162 thousand.
  Both are reported in the September 4 release’s seasonally adjusted Summary Table B. ([bls.gov](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_09042026.htm))

  G = 162 − 21 = +141 thousand jobs.
  Growth sign: RISING.

Inflation:
  July monthly CPI change: +0.1%.
  August monthly CPI change: +0.4%.
  Both are reported in Table A of the September 11 release and corroborated by the Department of Labor PDF. ([bls.gov](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_09112026.htm))

  I = 0.4 − 0.1 = +0.3 percentage points.
  Inflation sign: RISING.

The two subtractions were also checked using the permitted calculator capability. These are acceleration signals: “growth rising” means faster payroll gains, and “inflation rising” means a faster monthly price increase—not merely positive employment growth or a positive price level change.

Resulting September 30, 2026 classification:
  Growth rising / inflation rising.

Initial prescribed research allocation:
  GLD: 50%
  DBC: 50%
  SPY: 0%
  TLT: 0%
  SGOV: 0%

This allocation follows the supplied regime map mechanically. It is an initial target recommendation, not a claim about existing holdings or a completed trade.

3. Claim-to-evidence and vintage ledger

A. Growth inputs and historical vintage

Entity/identifier: BLS CES0000000001.
Observation periods: July and August 2026.
Values: Monthly gains of +21,000 and +162,000 jobs, respectively.
Publication/availability: September 4, 2026, 08:30 EDT (2026-09-04T12:30:00Z).

4. Evidence conflicts, limitations and interpretation

The search result for the mutable CPI landing page contained an inconsistent index-level snippet. I excluded that snippet and all index-level figures from the calculation. The dated CPI archive’s monthly rates agree with the dated Department of Labor PDF, including visual verification of page 1. Original strategy mandate (verbatim reference; scope override controls):
After each quarterly earnings cycle, build a directed graph over a frozen S&P 500 constituent universe using primary-source earnings releases, prepared remarks, and earnings-call transcripts from the latest completed cycle. Equally own the 10 U.S.-listed stocks with the highest PageRank scores and rebalance only after a new earnings cycle. 2. Fixed research conventions

The following conventions are declared for this trial. They are methodological choices, not facts inferred from a computed ranking. No ranking was computed, and these choices were not tuned against scores.

Universe and share classes

The intended frozen universe is the S&P 500 membership effective at October 15, 2026, 4:00 p.m. EDT, including only changes already effective then—not announced future changes.

Use one node per constituent issuer, consistent with a company-mention graph. If several indexed common-share classes represent the same issuer, collapse them to one issuer node. Choose the lexicographically first official constituent ticker as its canonical investable identifier, retaining every class/ticker alias in the universe ledger. Preserve official ticker punctuation and exchange identifiers.

All frozen issuers must remain nodes, including isolates, companies without eligible documents and dangling nodes. Missing documents must never be interpreted as verified zero mentions.

The actual roster and node count remain unverified. This convention does not constitute a completed universe snapshot.

Cycle and fiscal-calendar policy

Define reporting-season cohorts by fiscal-quarter end dates:

  Q1 cohort: February 1–April 30.
  Q2 cohort: May 1–July 31.
  Q3 cohort: August 1–October 31.
  Q4 cohort: November 1–January 31 of the following year.

These windows intentionally accommodate common non-calendar fiscal calendars. They are not assertions that every issuer’s fiscal labels match calendar-quarter labels.

For 52/53-week calendars, use the actual reported period-end date. For an annual release, include the separately identified fourth-quarter results and accompanying earnings communications; exclude a standalone annual report as a substitute corpus document. If a restructuring creates multiple short periods, retain separately reported quarterly periods in the applicable window. If no qualifying reporting period exists for a frozen issuer, record an explicit coverage exception rather than importing an arbitrary earlier quarter.

Set nominal source-completion deadlines at the end of the second calendar month after each cohort closes. For the Q2 2026 cohort, the deadline is September 30, 2026, 11:59:59 p.m. EDT. Only eligible material demonstrably available by that deadline enters that cohort.

Under this convention, Q2 2026 is the latest temporally closed candidate at the decision cutoff. Q3’s fiscal-period window has not yet ended. However, elapsed deadlines alone do not establish a completed earnings cycle: each frozen issuer’s release/call status must be verified. That certification was not completed.

Contemporaneous context supports treating Q2 as an earlier reporting season: FactSet’s September 18, 2026 article studied Q2 calls conducted June 15–September 14. Its window differs from this memo’s convention, and its study does not establish full coverage of this universe. ([insight.factset.com](https://insight.factset.com/more-than-65-of-sp-500-earnings-calls-for-q2-cited-ai))

Before claiming a ranking, require:

A missing required primary text remains a corpus gap. No coverage threshold below the complete required corpus is substituted in this trial.

5. PageRank specification and actual computation status

For a verified graph with N nodes, let d(j) be node j’s deduplicated outdegree. Initialize p0(i) = 1/N.

Iterate:

  p(k+1,i) = 0.15/N
             + 0.85 × [
                 sum over j→i of p(k,j)/d(j)
                 + sum over d(j)=0 of p(k,j)/N
               ]

Use uniform teleportation and uniform dangling-mass redistribution across every frozen node. Scores must sum to 1.

Stop when:

  sum over i of |p(k+1,i) − p(k,i)| ≤ 1e-10.

Rank raw converged scores descending. Break exact numerical ties by ascending canonical ticker under the declared share-class convention. Rounded display scores must not determine ties.

A reproducible result would disclose numeric precision, iteration count, final L1 difference, score sum and the complete score vector alongside its graph and source ledger.

Actual result:

  Iterations executed: none.
  Convergence: not tested; not a non-convergence finding.
  Final L1 difference: unavailable.
  Score normalization: untested.
  Scores and top 10: unresolved.
  Equal-weight allocation: not established.

Scalar arithmetic cannot repair missing graph inputs. No calculation has been claimed merely from specifying this recurrence.

## 4. Methodology and declared conventions

Fixed conventions (declared before ranking, not tuned after results):

1. **Eligibility:** Companies that are S&P 500 constituents at the decision cutoff (2026-10-16T03:15:00Z). Membership verified via the current Wikipedia *List of S&P 500 companies* (retrieved 2026-10-15; reflects constituent changes through September 2026) corroborated by independent S&P 500 screeners. Primary S&P DJI PDFs were not separately retrieved; this is a stated limitation, not a hidden gap.
2. **Metric:** Total company-level equity market capitalization (price × total shares outstanding, combining share classes where a company has multiple classes — relevant to Alphabet, not to NVDA or AAPL which have single classes). Free-float index weight and share price alone are explicitly *not* used.
3. **Valuation time:** Regular-session close of 2026-10-15, 16:00 America/New_York, for all decision-driving figures (E1, E5). Context rows (Alphabet, Microsoft) use 2026-10-14 closes and are labeled as such; they do not affect the #1 determination.
4. **Tie-break:** Lexicographic company-name order — not triggered (NVDA > AAPL by ≈ $260B).
5. **Sufficiency standard:** Leader is "sufficiently verified" when ≥2 independent sources agree on the same #1 at the same valuation date and the arithmetic (price × shares) reproduces the quoted cap within rounding. Both conditions hold for NVDA.
6. **Arithmetic reproduction (independent check):**
   - NVDA: $217.23 × 24.15B shares ≈ $5.246T — matches quoted $5.244–5.25T (E1, E2, E4).
   - AAPL: $342.00 × 14.59B shares ≈ $4.990T — matches quoted $4.99T (E5, E6).
   - Gap: $5.246T − $4.990T ≈ $0.256T ≈ 5.1%.

**Coverage:** Full 503-constituent screen was not exhaustively enumerated; however, no constituent other than NVDA and AAPL is near the $5T level on any retrieved October 2026 evidence (next candidates are Alphabet ~$4.25T and Microsoft ~$3.96T, both >$1T below NVDA). Coverage is adequate to establish the leader; it would not be adequate to establish a fine-grained full ranking, which is not required here.

**Material unresolved items:** None affecting the #1 determination. Residual uncertainty is limited to (a) secondary-source market-cap aggregation conventions (e.g., treatment of unvested shares), which affects levels by ≲1% and cannot flip a 5% gap; and (b) S&P membership evidence being secondary compilation rather than a directly retrieved S&P DJI primary record.

---

## 5. Conditional hold / switch policy (proposed only — not executed)

This is a description of the strategy's forward-looking review rule, stated as a recommendation policy. **No orders were placed or queued, no account state was changed, no schedule or monitor was deployed, and no ongoing monitoring was started.**

- **Review cadence (proposed):** After every regular US market close (16:00 America/New_York on trading days), recompute company-level total market capitalization for all S&P 500 constituents using the same conventions declared in §4.
- **Unchanged-leader inaction:** If NVDA remains the #1 company-level market-cap constituent at that close, take no action; the 100% NVDA target is unchanged.
- **Switch condition:** If any other S&P 500 constituent's total company-level market cap exceeds NVDA's at a regular-session close, the policy proposes selling the former leader (NVDA) and moving the full allocation to the new leader at the next regular-session trading opportunity (e.g., the following session's open). Exact ties are broken by lexicographic company-name order.
- **Membership-exit condition:** If NVDA ceases to be an S&P 500 constituent (delisting, removal, corporate event), it is no longer eligible; the leader must be re-identified among remaining constituents under the same rules.
- **Evidence-failure condition:** If, on a future review, the leader cannot be sufficiently verified from public evidence (e.g., conflicting same-date data wider than the leader–runner-up gap), the policy defaults to hypothetical cash with any provisional candidate labeled as such, per the missing-data policy — this did not apply at the current decision point.

**Known fragility (disclosed):** Leadership between NVDA and AAPL has changed hands during 2026 (E12: Apple led on 2026-07-27; NVDA led by mid-October). The 5.1% gap at the reference close is real but not large relative to observed multi-week swings between these two names, so the daily-review rule is materially relevant rather than ceremonial.

---

## 6. Unresolved evidence that could change the leader

1. **Post-cutoff price moves** (outside this memo's scope): any close after 2026-10-15 in which AAPL's cap exceeds NVDA's would trigger the switch rule in §5. NVDA earnings are indicated for ~2026-11-18 and Apple's for ~2026-11-02 (stockanalysis.com), both potential volatility events.
2. **Primary S&P DJI constituent confirmation** was not directly retrieved (spglobal.com press releases/PDFs); membership rests on the current Wikipedia list plus corroborating screeners. A removal announcement dated after the last Wikipedia edit but before the cutoff would, if it existed, be a gap — none was found in searches through the cutoff.
3. **Market-cap vendor conventions** (fully diluted vs. basic shares outstanding, treatment of dual-class totals) differ by ≲1% across sources; none of the retrieved differences approach the 5.1% leader gap.
4. **Stale context rows:** Alphabet/Microsoft figures are 2026-10-14 vintage (E8, E9) and were not used in the #1 determination; a same-close refresh would not plausibly close a >$1T gap.

---

## 7. Decision summary

**Decision:** Allocate 100% of hypothetical cash to **NVDA — NVIDIA Corporation**, the verified S&P 500 company-level market-cap leader at the 2026-10-15 16:00 EDT close (~$5.25T vs. AAPL ~$4.99T), subject to the daily post-close review and conditional switch policy in §5. Status: **verified** (not provisional). No execution, account change, schedule, or monitor has occurred; none is requested by this memo.

## 1. Recommendation / Status

**No security meets the P03 trigger in the frozen window.** The screen requires (a) ≥3 distinct members of Congress disclosing **purchases** of the same U.S.-listed security within the window, and (b) sum of disclosed range-**lower** bounds ≥ **$500,000**. Within covered public data, **no ticker satisfies both conditions.**

This is reported as an **explicit no-qualifier status**, not an unresolved block. The strongest apparent candidate — MSFT — is a **false positive** on closer reading (details in §5). Because the strategy permits ≤5 equally weighted new positions *only on a qualified trigger*, the correct action is **no new allocation; hold cash pending a verified trigger.** No initiate, no add, no order, no schedule.

The signal for the largest true cluster is in fact **negative**: MSFT carries a larger and more recent *sell* cluster (8 members, Jul 21–Sep 28) than its buy cluster.

## 2. Method, Conventions, Inputs

## 5. Why MSFT Fails the Window Test (the only non-obvious case)

1. Coldpine's MSFT figure is a **90-day trade-date** cluster, whereas P03 measures the **30-day disclosure-availability** window. These are different objects.
2. The **$822K–$1.8M** total is dominated by **Josh Gottheimer** ($250K–$500K + $500K–$1M = **$750K–$1.5M** lower bound $750K), whose MSFT purchase **disclosed 2026-09-14**, i.e. **two days before** the window opens. Excluded by the frozen window rule.
3. Excluding Gottheimer and the non-member (E6, Trump), the remaining MSFT buyers contributing **purchase disclosures inside the window** are **Fields (Oct 1, $1K–$15K)** and **McClain (Oct 12, $1K–$15K)** — **2 distinct members**, lower-bound sum **≈ $2K**, far below **$500K**. Other cluster members' purchases (Taylor, Khanna) surfaced on earlier disclosures and/or are trivial.
4. Therefore MSFT: **distinct members with qualifying in-window purchases < 3**, and **confirmed lower-bound sum ≪ $500K**. **Does not qualify.**
5. Corroborating signal: MSFT also has the **largest sell** cluster (8 members, E8).

1. **Consensus provider (intended):** Institutional bottom-up broker consensus as aggregated by **LSEG I/B/E/S** (with **FactSet** consensus acceptable as an equal-status substitute). Free public substitutes (Zacks live pages, ChartMill, Yahoo analyst pages) are **not** accepted as point-in-time records for the 2026-09-30 decision because their displayed vintages are mid-October 2026 (e.g., Zacks TSLA/SHOP/NFLX estimate pages dated 2026-10-12/13/15), not the decision date.
2. **Fiscal forecast period:** **Next-twelve-months (NTM) consensus EPS**, formed from the fiscal quarters ending after the decision date; fallback to next-fiscal-year (FY+1) EPS if NTM cannot be constructed from public endpoints. Sector/aggregate FactSet commentary that uses calendar Q3 2026 or CY2026 is treated as context only, not as the security-level ranking input.
3. **30-day endpoint convention:** Consensus EPS vintage at **t0 = 2026-08-31 16:00 ET** and **t1 = 2026-09-30 16:00 ET**. Post-September revision data (including all of October 2026) are inadmissible as decision inputs even when retrieved later.
4. **Upward-revision strength:**  
   \( \text{Strength}_i = \dfrac{\text{EPS}^{NTM}_i(t_1) - \text{EPS}^{NTM}_i(t_0)}{\left|\text{EPS}^{NTM}_i(t_0)\right|} \)
5. **Upward-revision breadth:**  
   \( \text{Breadth}_i = \dfrac{\text{Up}_i - \text{Down}_i}{N_i} \)  
   where Up_i / Down_i = number of distinct covering analysts who raised / lowered NTM EPS between t0 and t1; N_i = analysts contributing at t1. Requires \( N_i \ge 3 \) at both endpoints.
6. **Normalization:** Cross-sectional **z-scores** of Strength, Breadth, and momentum computed **within the S&P 500 membership at t1** over names that pass qualification (item 8).
7. **Six-month momentum:** Total return on **split- and dividend-adjusted closes**:  
   \( M_i = \dfrac{\text{AdjClose}_i(\text{2026-09-30})}{\text{AdjClose}_i(\text{2026-03-31})} - 1 \)  
   (If 2026-03-31 is not a trading day for the security, use the last prior trading-day close; no interpolation.)
8. **Composite score (frozen weights):**  
   \( S_i = 0.25\,z(\text{Strength}_i) + 0.25\,z(\text{Breadth}_i) + 0.50\,z(M_i) \)  
   (Revision block = 50% of the composite, split equally between strength and breadth; momentum = 50%.)
9. **Qualification threshold:** (a) S&P 500 member at t1; (b) \( N_i \ge 3 \) at both revision endpoints with non-missing consensus EPS at both; (c) complete adjusted-close pair for momentum. Names failing any test are excluded, not zero-filled.
10. **Missing-data policy:** Exclusion, not imputation. **If fewer than five companies qualify, the recommendation is the set of qualifiers at equal weights, explicitly labeled a partial candidate sample** — never a universe-wide top five. If zero or the security-level revision screen cannot be constructed at all, the **ranking is unresolved**.
11. **Deterministic ties:** Sort by \(S\) desc → Strength desc → Breadth desc → \(M\) desc → ticker A–Z.
12. **Equal weights:** Five qualifiers (if five exist) at 20% each, in recommendation units only; no orders.

## 8. Material unresolved items and conflicts

1. **Binding gap:** No free, point-in-time, security-level 30-day EPS revision strength and breadth panel for the S&P 500 at 2026-08-31/2026-09-30. Until such a panel exists, the P05 top-five output **cannot be verified** under any provider choice.
2. **Provider conflict (unresolved):** FactSet vs. I/B/E/S vs. Zacks consensus levels and revision counts systematically differ (different contributor sets, treatment of one-time items, fiscal alignment). No adjudication without dual-vintage files.
3. **Fiscal-period conflict (unresolved):** MU’s fiscal year ends late September; NTM construction at 2026-09-30 mixes fiscal labels across names. The frozen convention (NTM) mitigates but does not eliminate vendor calendarization differences.
4. **Window mismatch (unresolved):** The secondary five-name list does not document a 30-day measurement window; LSEG weekly counts available here cover only part of the window.
5. **Universe file (limitation):** Membership timing was policed from change tables, not a certified 2026-09-30 constituent file.

## 9. Conditional review / change policy (no schedule deployed)

This memo states a **conditional recommendation policy** only. Nothing was ordered, booked, scheduled, or monitored.

- **At each future regular month-end close (America/New_York):** re-run the frozen conventions (§2) with endpoints shifted to that month-end and the preceding month-end for revisions, and the corresponding six-calendar-month window for momentum; re-derive the S&P 500 membership at that month-end first.
- **Hold condition:** If, at the next review, (a) a licensed point-in-time consensus panel meeting §2 items 1–5 is available and (b) at least five names qualify, replace the slate with the new top five at equal weights (20% each) as a research recommendation.
- **Partial-slate condition:** If 1–4 names qualify, recommend only those names at equal weights (1/n each), labeled a **partial candidate sample**, never a universe-wide top five.
- **Unresolved condition (current state):** If security-level PIT revision data remain unavailable, the standing output remains **UNRESOLVED / no verified slate**; provisional watchlists may be refreshed for research continuity but must retain their provisional label.
- **Immediate intra-month change:** Not part of this template. Any change before the next month-end would require a predeclared override rule, which this memo does not create.
- **Execution disclaimer:** No orders were placed or queued; no broker, venue, private account, or private connector was accessed; no account state was changed; no monitoring or schedules were deployed; no completed rebalance is claimed.

**Template ID:** P09 (Four-Regime Rotation) — reconstruction of the 2026-09-30 month-end classification.

**Bottom line (primary result):**
- Growth = **falling**; Inflation = **rising**.
- Regime = growth falling + inflation rising → **50% GLD + 50% SGOV** (recommended initial allocation; no prior portfolio/regime supplied).

## 1. Chosen conventions (declared before presenting the result; held fixed)

1. **Growth series.** BEA *Real Gross Domestic Product*, seasonally adjusted annual rate, percent change from preceding quarter (NIPA headline; FRED `GDPC1` equivalent). Revision-aware: use the estimate *vintage* published by the cutoff.
2. **Growth comparison window.** Latest quarter available at the cutoff vs the immediately preceding quarter, both at the same cutoff-available vintage. Sign rule Δ = latest − prior.
3. **Inflation series.** BLS *Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), U.S. city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted*, series ID `CUUR0000SA0`. Measured as the **12-month percent change**.
4. **Inflation comparison window.** Latest observation available at the cutoff vs the immediately preceding observation (a 1-month window on the 12-month rate). Computed at **full published index precision (3 decimals)**, not from the rounded 1-decimal headline. Sign rule Δ = latest − prior.
5. **Rising/falling sign rule.** For both components: **rising iff Δ > 0; falling iff Δ ≤ 0** (ties break to the "non-increasing"/falling side).
6. **Missing-release policy.** Use the most recent observation actually published by the cutoff. If fewer than two comparable observations of a series exist before the cutoff, that component is *unresolved* (and the allocation becomes unresolved).
7. **Initialization rule.** No prior portfolio or regime state is supplied. This memo treats 2026-09-30 as the **initial** classification and recommends the single mapped allocation. Subsequent action is recommended **only when the monthly regime changes**; otherwise hold.
8. **Alternate series (growth or inflation) deliberately not mixed.** Method is kept to one series per component so the rule is fixed and reproducible within the trial.

---

## 2. Inputs (verified, with vintages)

**Growth — BEA Real GDP, % change SAAR (QoQ):**

| Second | 2026-08-26 08:30 ET | 1.5 | 2.1 | −0.6 |
| **Third (+2026 annual update)** | **2026-09-30 08:30 ET** | **2.2** | **2.5**(revised) | **−0.3** |

The 2026-09-30 08:30 ET third estimate was published **before** the 16:00 ET evaluation time, so it is the cutoff-available vintage. **Growth sign = falling** under every vintage (Δ<0 in all three). Robust.

**Inflation — BLS CPI-U, all items, NSA, 12-month % change (full-precision computation):**

| Observation | Index level (1982-84=100) | Published via | Publication date/time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jul 2025 | 323.048 | July 2026 CPI release | (base) |
| Aug 2025 | 323.976 | Aug 2026 CPI release | (base) |
| Jul 2026 | 333.918 | CPI release (July) | 2026-08-12 08:30 ET |
| Aug 2026 | 334.980 | CPI release (August) | 2026-09-11 08:30 ET |

Arithmetic (reproducible):
- Jul 2026 YoY = 333.918 / 323.048 − 1 = **+3.3648%**
- Aug 2026 YoY = 334.980 / 323.976 − 1 = **+3.3965%**
- Δ = 3.3965 − 3.3648 = **+0.0317 pp → rising**

Cross-checks: BLS published headline prints = 3.4% (July) and 3.4% (August); a secondary aggregator reported the unrounded July YoY as +3.36% and August as +3.4%, consistent with the computation above. **Inflation sign = rising** on the declared full-precision convention.

## 3. Classification and prescribed allocation

---

## 6. Coverage, conflicts, limitations (must-read)

- **Precision conflict (material, unresolved):** BLS prints the 12-month rate to 1 decimal. At that published precision July = 3.4% and August = 3.4%, a **tie** (Δ = 0). Under the declared tie rule (Δ ≤ 0 → falling) the rounded reading would yield *inflation falling*, i.e. **growth falling + inflation falling → 100% TLT**, not GLD/SGOV. The full-precision index-level computation (Δ = +0.03 pp) yields *rising*. This memo's primary result rests on the declared **full-precision** convention (§1.4); the alternative allocation is flagged because the sign is *not robust* to this choice. See §8.
- **Revision/re-availability:** CPI NSA indexes are revisable for 10–12 months. July-2025 base (323.048) appears in the 2025-08 release, the 2026-07 release, and the current BLS API, i.e. stable across the relevant span. October-2025 CPI is a genuine gap in the series (2025 appropriations lapse) but is not used here. I could not obtain an independent ALFRED point-in-time snapshot within budget (FRED CSV timed out; bls.gov/dol.gov PDF endpoints returned 403), so vintage stability of the CPI base is established from *named releases* rather than a separate vintage archive.
- **Growth revisions are large but sign-robust:** the annual update moved Q1 from 2.1% to 2.5% and Q2 from 1.5% to 2.2%, yet Δ stays negative (falling) across advance, second and third vintages.
- **No independent secondary growth series used** (e.g., payrolls); a different growth proxy could in principle change the growth sign. Not checked here; declared single-series method.
- Distinctions: **Verified** = release quotes/index values above. **Supplied assumption** = the declared conventions in §1. **Estimate/computed** = the two YoY figures and deltas (reproducible arithmetic). **Provisional** = the GLD/SGOV allocation insofar as it depends on the precision convention. **Unresolved** = which of GLD/SGOV vs TLT is "correct" if one insists on 1-decimal published precision (the tie).

---

## 7. Conditional review / change policy (no execution)

- **Initial (this memo):** 2026-09-30 regime = growth falling + inflation rising → recommend **50% GLD + 50% SGOV**.
- **No prior holdings/regime were supplied**, so no trade is asserted to have occurred, and no "change" is claimed. The above is an initial recommendation.
- **Ongoing rule (conditional):** At each following month-end, recompute growth (BEA real GDP vintage available then) and inflation (CPI-U 12-mo YoY, full precision, latest two observations). Recommend an allocation change **only if the regime bucket changes**; if the regime is unchanged, hold. Mapping remains exactly: rising/falling→SPY; falling/falling→TLT; rising/rising→GLD+DBC; falling/rising→GLD+SGOV.
- Because no positions are supplied, if the evaluator holds an existing portfolio, apply this as a conditional instruction: "if current regime ≠ target regime, rebalance to the mapped weights; if equal, no action."

**No orders were placed or queued; no broker, venue, account, connector, schedule or monitor was accessed or changed; nothing was executed.** This memo is produced solely from public web sources and arithmetic in the response.

---

## 8. Summary recommendation and its sensitivity

- **Primary recommendation:** **50% GLD + 50% SGOV** (growth falling, inflation rising, full-precision convention).
- **Sensitivity (disclosed, not tuned):** if the inflation sign is instead read from BLS's 1-decimal published prints (3.4% vs 3.4%, a tie → falling), the regime is growth falling + inflation falling and the allocation would be **100% TLT**. The full-precision index computation (+0.0317 pp) is the declared primary because it uses BLS's actual index levels rather than display rounding; the tie is nonetheless a genuine, material fork.
- **Growth sign is robust** across all available vintages: falling.
- **Unresolved:** none for the growth component; the inflation component is resolved only under the declared precision convention (exact unresolved input = whether "change" is measured at 3-decimal index precision or 1-decimal headline precision).

Run standard PageRank on that graph with damping factor 0.85 and dangling-node redistribution. Equally own the 10 U.S.-listed stocks with the highest PageRank scores and rebalance only after a new earnings cycle. **Memo date:** 2026-10-15

## Decision

- **Company:** NVIDIA Corporation  
- **Ticker:** **NVDA**  
- **Target allocation from hypothetical cash:** **100% NVDA**
- **Hypothetical cash allocation:** 0%
- **Estimated company-level market capitalization at the reference close:** **approximately $5.25 trillion**

Public market-data sources identify NVIDIA as the largest company by market capitalization at the October 15 close. The closest credible contender, Apple, was approximately $4.99 trillion. The rounded lead was therefore approximately **$0.26 trillion**, or **5.2%** over Apple.

No broker, account, trading venue, private connector, schedule, monitor, or order was accessed or used. No order or account change occurred.

## Methodology and conventions

1. Eligible companies: S&P 500 constituents evidenced as of the decision period.
2. Valuation measure: total company-level equity market capitalization, not index weight or share price alone.
3. Share classes: consolidated where the data provider reports a company-level figure. Alphabet’s Class A and Class C shares are treated as one company.
4. Valuation time: regular U.S. market close on October 15, 2026, 16:00 EDT.
5. Tie rule: lexicographic company-name order, as specified. No tie occurred.
6. Ranking approach: direct comparison of the leader with the nearest credible mega-cap contenders, supported by market-cap ranking pages and close-date market data.
7. Rounding: figures are reported to two decimal places in trillions. Differences calculated from rounded figures are approximate.
8. Source hierarchy: S&P Dow Jones Indices for index membership; public secondary market-data providers for close prices and market capitalization. No primary exchange market-cap file or issuer share-count record at the exact close was retrieved.

## Contender comparison

| Company | Ticker / identifiers | S&P membership evidence | October 15 close | Company-level market cap | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **NVIDIA Corporation** | NVDA; Nasdaq | S&P’s September 30 factsheet lists “Nvidia Corp — NVDA” among the S&P 500’s top constituents. The S&P 500 constituent page also supports the index roster. | **$217.23** | **~$5.25T** | **Leader** |

| Alphabet Inc. | GOOG / GOOGL; Nasdaq | S&P’s constituent page identifies Alphabet Inc. Class A / GOOGL and separately lists the Class C security; company-level capitalization is consolidated here. | **GOOGL: $349.22** | **~$4.27T** | Below Apple and NVIDIA |
| Microsoft Corporation | MSFT; Nasdaq | S&P’s constituent page identifies Microsoft Corp. / MSFT as an S&P 500 constituent. | **$539.44** | **~$4.01T** | Below Alphabet, Apple, and NVIDIA |

### Ranking arithmetic

Using the close-date figures:

- NVIDIA minus Apple: `$5.25T − $4.99T ≈ $0.26T`
- NVIDIA lead over Apple: `$0.26T ÷ $4.99T ≈ 5.2%`
- NVIDIA minus Alphabet: approximately `$0.98T`
- NVIDIA minus Microsoft: approximately `$1.24T`

The lead is material relative to the rounding precision of the reported figures.

## Material conflicts and limitations

1. **No independent 500-row close-date recomputation.** Public search exposed close-date market-cap pages and ranking evidence, but not a single independently downloadable, exact-close file containing every S&P 500 constituent. The recommendation therefore relies on:
   - official S&P membership material;
   - direct close-date market-cap pages for the leader and closest contenders; and
   - cross-checks from another market-cap provider.

2. **Alphabet share-class inconsistency.** One retrieved S&P-500 ranking snippet displayed GOOGL and GOOG as separate entries with values that appeared to double-count Alphabet’s company capitalization. That presentation was not used. Alphabet is consolidated as one company under the mandated convention. This conflict does not threaten the NVDA result because even the consolidated Alphabet figure is materially below NVIDIA.

3. **Secondary market-cap data.** StockAnalysis, FinanceCharts, and CompaniesMarketCap are secondary sources. Their figures can differ due to share-count updates, treatment of multiple classes, corporate actions, and rounding. The observed NVIDIA–Apple gap is approximately $260 billion, much larger than the reported rounding differences.

4. **Membership date gap.** The strongest static official membership evidence retrieved was dated August 31 or September 30, while the reference close was October 15. The official equal-weight page was current through October 14 and states that it uses the same constituents as the capitalization-weighted index. A complete static October 15 constituent roster was not exposed in the retrieved public text.

## Conditional future review and switching policy

This is a proposed policy only:

- After each regular U.S. market close, review the S&P 500 constituent roster and total company-level market capitalization using the same conventions.
- If NVDA remains the highest-capitalization eligible company, maintain the 100% NVDA target; no action is indicated.
- If another eligible S&P 500 company exceeds NVDA on a sufficiently consistent company-level capitalization basis, recommend moving the full hypothetical allocation to that new leader at the next regular-session opportunity.
- If capitalization is exactly tied, select by lexicographic company-name order.
- If membership, share-class treatment, valuation timing, or market-cap evidence is materially incomplete or conflicting, retain hypothetical cash rather than treating an unverified candidate as the leader.
- No daily review, monitoring process, schedule, alert, order, or account action has been deployed.

**Template ID:** P02 — Hedge Fund Consensus

## Conclusion

The requested 10-stock, 10%-each recommendation **cannot be established from the verified evidence gathered within the research budget**.

The declared roster contains 20 distinct SEC 13F filers. However, only 10 managers have sufficiently extracted eligible top-holding data for a reproducible partial count. The remaining 10 have filing metadata but incomplete eligible-stock extraction, unresolved instrument filtering, or unresolved ticker/class mappings.

Therefore:

- The following is **not** a verified P02 basket.
- No 10%-each allocation should be treated as established from this memo.
- The partial sample most frequently observed in the extracted data was:
  1. **AMZN — Amazon**
  2. **Alphabet — GOOG/GOOGL aggregated**
  3. **META — Meta Platforms**
  4. **TSM — Taiwan Semiconductor ADR**
  5. **V — Visa**
- These names are **provisional observations only**, not a recommendation or current-position instruction.

## Declared methodology

### Roster convention

I selected 20 distinct long-horizon or fundamental/activist public-equity managers using this fixed convention:

1. The filer must be a distinct SEC 13F reporting adviser or investment entity.
2. The manager must have public evidence of a fundamental, concentrated, activist, long-only, value, growth-equity, or explicitly long-term investment approach.
3. Affiliated entities are deduplicated by adviser identity and SEC CIK.
4. A filing’s “other included managers” are not counted as separate managers.
5. The roster is fixed before the consensus count; it is not adjusted to favor particular stocks.

This is a defensible convention, not the only possible roster. Appaloosa, Duquesne, Bridgewater, D1, Tiger Global, Coatue, and Viking have less explicit long-term wording in the retrieved evidence than Baupost, Lone Pine, ValueAct, Soros, JANA, Fairholme, Corvex, Pershing Square, and Trian. They remain in the declared roster because they are established discretionary public-equity or multi-strategy managers with long operating histories and current 13F filings.

### Filing and instrument rules

- Common completed quarter: **2026-06-30**.
- Use the latest valid 13F-HR or 13F-HR/A available by the cutoff.
- Use reported market value as of June 30, 2026, not original trade dates or current prices.
- Exclude put and call rows, ETFs, notes, warrants, and other non-stock instruments.
- Include U.S.-listed common shares and U.S.-listed ADRs.
- Aggregate multiple rows for the same issuer and share-class family where the issuer is economically the same.
- Alphabet Class A and Class C are aggregated as **Alphabet / GOOG-GOOGL**.
- Count each issuer once per manager, regardless of multiple SEC rows or voting-discretion categories.
- A manager’s top 10 is ranked by aggregated eligible reported market value.
- Holding-value ties: reported market value descending, then issuer/CUSIP ascending.
- Consensus ties: manager count descending, then canonical ticker/issuer name ascending.
- If the tenth consensus position is tied and the tie cannot be resolved from the declared rule, retain the deterministic lexical rule but label the result provisional.

### Amendment rule

A later HR/A for the same reporting quarter supersedes the original filing when it restates or adds holdings. Duplicate line items from the original filing and amendment are not counted twice. The retrieved evidence did not establish a complete amendment audit for all 20 managers; this is one reason the final basket remains unresolved.

## Conditional future review and change policy

This strategy should be reviewed **only after a new common completed 13F filing cycle**.

At each review:

1. Preserve the declared 20-manager roster unless a manager ceases to qualify as a distinct filer or no longer has a valid 13F.
2. Collect the latest valid HR/HR/A for the common quarter.
3. Reapply the same stock, ADR, option, ETF, issuer-aggregation, and ticker-mapping rules.
4. Require all 20 managers to have supported filings and complete eligible top-10 extraction.
5. Count each issuer once per manager.
6. Rank by consensus count, then the declared deterministic tie rule.
7. Only if the complete ranking is established, target 10% for each of the ten selected issuers.
8. Do not change the basket between filing cycles because of price moves, news, or inferred trades.
9. If fewer than 20 managers or any material mapping/version conflict remains unresolved, retain an **unresolved/provisional** status rather than treating a partial sample as the basket.

If current holdings are later supplied, the conditional rule is: hold names that remain in the next verified basket at their target weight; reduce or remove names that leave it; add names entering it, subject to separate account authorization. No current positions were assumed here.

**No orders were placed or queued. No account state was changed. No broker, venue, private connector, schedule, or ongoing monitor was accessed or deployed.**

## 1. Frozen methodology

### Entry window

The required interval is:

\[
(2026\text{-}09\text{-}16T03{:}15Z,\;2026\text{-}10\text{-}16T03{:}15Z]
\]

The actionable clock is public disclosure availability, not the original transaction date.

Most retrieved records expose only a calendar filing date, not a publication timestamp. For date-only records, I used the conservative operational convention:

- include filings dated **2026-09-17 through 2026-10-15**;
- exclude 2026-09-16 and 2026-10-16 records unless a timestamp establishes inclusion;
- treat filing-date conflicts as unresolved, not silently corrected.

### Security universe

Included: U.S.-listed common stock identified by a ticker or exact share class.  
Excluded from the stock screen: bonds, municipal securities, structured products, private LLC interests, options, and executive-branch disclosures.

`GOOG` and `GOOGL` are kept distinct because the official record identifies the security class.

### Qualification

A security qualifies only if:

1. purchases are attributed to at least **three distinct members of Congress**;
2. the sum of disclosed **lower bounds** is at least **$500,000**;
3. each counted purchase falls in the public-availability window.

A member counts once even if multiple accounts or multiple purchases are reported. Spouse/dependent transactions count under the reporting member only, with ownership retained separately.

No interval midpoint is treated as an observed amount.

### Selection

If more than five securities qualify, the fixed selection order is:

1. highest confirmed lower-bound total;
2. highest distinct-member count;
3. earliest threshold-confirming public availability;
4. ticker in ascending lexicographic order.

Equal weights would apply only to selected qualifying names.

## 6. Coverage limitations and unresolved conflicts

1. **No exhaustive primary corpus was available through the permitted search interface.** The House portal is public, but the permitted search tool did not expose a complete, queryable list of every House PTR available before the cutoff. 2. **Secondary coverage is incomplete or inconsistent.** Aistockwire explicitly describes a 31-member tracked set. Congress Stock Tracker and Capitol Markets provide useful discovery records but are not primary records.

3. **Filing-date conflicts exist.** For BHE, one secondary result reports Oct. 7 while another reports Oct. 12. Both are inside the broad window, but the conflict prevents treating the secondary record as fully verified.

4. **Transaction dates and public-availability dates are different clocks.** The NFLX, SNOW, and MSFT cluster pages often group by transaction date, while P03 requires the availability date. Those cluster pages are not sufficient by themselves.

5. **Range data are not exact amounts.** The lower-bound test is applied only to the left edge of each disclosed range. Midpoints and upper bounds are not used to confirm qualification.

Because these gaps leave the screen unresolved, this memo does not rank securities or label any name as a qualifying pick.

- no exclusion under the stock-universe convention.

If more than five names qualify, use the fixed ranking rules stated above and equal-weight the selected names.

For a verified entry:

- the holding clock starts when the threshold first becomes publicly confirmable;
- the intended holding period is six calendar months;
- if no anniversary date exists, use the last calendar day of the sixth month;
- exit earlier when any member whose purchase helped qualify the entry publicly discloses a sale of that security.

No incumbent holdings were supplied. Accordingly, no current exit is asserted.

Any performance measurement begins at actionable public disclosure availability, not at the original transaction date. The report should use the disclosed price or a documented closing-price convention at the actionable timestamp, with the convention recorded for each entry.

No performance calculation was made because no verified P03 entry was established.
