# P04 Insider Cluster: research memo (recommendations only)

**Template ID:** P04 Insider Cluster
**Status:** No S&P 500 company qualifies, so I'm recommending no names. Within the coverage below, this is a checked absence rather than a lack of evidence. The remaining risks are in section 6.
**Decision time (reference close):** 2026-10-15 16:00 America/New_York
**Research cutoff:** 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z, which is 2026-10-15 23:15 ET
**Cluster window (transaction dates):** 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-15
**When I retrieved the data:** 2026-10-16, about 19:00 to 19:15 UTC. Every filing I relied on was accepted by the SEC before the cutoff. I opened later filings only to rule them out.

## 1. Recommendation
I recommend no names and no weights, which means staying in cash under this strategy. I fixed these rules before looking at any results:
- **If more than five companies qualify:** rank by total dollar value of qualifying purchases, highest first. Break ties by the earliest SEC acceptance time of the filing that completes the cluster, then by ticker A to Z.
- **Weights:** equal, so each of N selected names gets 1/N (20% each if there are five).
- **Exits:** six months after SEC acceptance of the filing that completes the cluster. Exit earlier if any qualifying insider publicly discloses an open-market sale (transaction code S) that wasn't made under a trading plan.

## 2. Method and conventions (fixed in advance)
1. **Index membership:** I used Wikipedia's "List of S&P 500 companies", the [revision from 2026-10-14 03:35 UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_S%26P_500_companies&oldid=1380159481) (oldid 1380159481). It was the last revision before the reference close and lists 503 tickers with their SEC company IDs (CIKs). This is a secondary source, and I didn't check it against S&P Dow Jones Indices.
2. **Filings:** I used the SEC EDGAR daily form indexes for 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-15 (`https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/daily-index/2026/QTR3/` and `/QTR4/`, files `form.YYYYMMDD.idx`). They held 21,909 Form 4 and 4/A rows. Of those, 2,073 filings came from companies on the S&P list, and I downloaded all 2,073 with no failures. The index for 2026-10-12 returned an access error (403); that day was Columbus Day, a federal holiday, so there was no index to fetch.
3. **Late filings:** a filing accepted after 17:30 ET on 10/15 gets a 10/16 filing date. The 10/16 daily index wasn't published yet, so I used [EDGAR full-text search for 10/16 Form 4s](https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?forms=4&dateRange=custom&startdt=2026-10-16&enddt=2026-10-16). It returned 96 filings, 22 of them from S&P 500 companies. All 22 were accepted on 10/16 between 09:00 and 14:31 ET, after the cutoff, so I excluded them. None was a CEO or CFO buying alongside a director anyway.
4. **Parsing:** from each Form 4's XML I took the issuer's CIK and the insider's role (the director flag and officer title). For each non-derivative trade I took the transaction code, date, shares and price, plus the trading-plan flag (`aff10b5One`) and the footnotes. I also took the SEC acceptance time from each submission file.
5. **What counts:** a trade qualifies only if it has code P (open-market purchase), the plan flag isn't set, and the footnotes don't describe dividend reinvestment, an employee stock purchase plan, reinvested RSU dividends or any other plan acquisition. A cluster needs the CEO or CFO plus a different person who is a director, both with qualifying purchases in the window and both filings accepted by the cutoff.

## 3. Results and cluster ledger
There were 121 code-P trades in the window, across 35 filings at 13 companies: CME, COO, CRL, CRM, HRL, IBKR, LEN, MKC, ORCL, PCG, SPG, TFC and TPL. Only two of those companies had a CEO or CFO buying:

| Ticker | Insider and role | Code, date | Shares and price | SEC accepted (ET) | Footnote | Filing | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TFC | Michael P. Lyons, President & CEO and a director | P, 2026-09-17 | 21,000 at $48.3608 (weighted average) | 2026-09-18 07:52:57 | F1 gives the price range $48.33–$48.375. Plan flag is false. | [TFC Form 4](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/92230/0001534574-26-000016.txt) | The purchase qualifies, but no other director bought in the window. One person holding both roles can't complete a cluster alone, so this isn't a cluster. |
| CRL | Glenn Coleman, EVP & CFO (not a director) | P, 2026-09-30 | 10 at $297.43 | 2026-10-02 16:27:48 | F1: "acquired pursuant to the Company's Employee Stock Purchase Plan" | [CRL Form 4](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/0001100682-26-000144.txt) | Excluded as a plan acquisition, and no director bought. Not a cluster. |

None of the other code-P trades can form a cluster:
- **Directors buying with no CEO or CFO buying:** COO (Kurzius), CRM (Kirk), HRL (Newlands, Chairman), MKC (Hattersley) and ORCL (Rusckowski).
- **Plan or reinvestment acquisitions:** CME (Shepard, a broker-run dividend reinvestment plan), SPG (11 directors with dividends reinvested on restricted stock) and IBKR (Conkling, plan flag set). At PCG, Larsen's footnote mentions reinvested RSU dividends. I didn't settle that one, but it can't matter because no CEO or CFO bought there.
- **Large shareholders who aren't officers:** LEN (Berkshire Hathaway / Warren Buffett) and TPL (Horizon Kinetics).

## 4. Claim-to-evidence ledger
| Entity | Claim | Period | Available | Source | Supporting passage | Uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S&P 500 list | 503 tickers with CIKs | As of 2026-10-14 | Revision dated 2026-10-14T03:35Z | Wikipedia oldid 1380159481 (linked in section 2) | Constituents table | Secondary source. Any index change on 10/14 or 10/15 wasn't checked. |
| TFC, Lyons | CEO and director; open-market purchase (code P) | 2026-09-17 | Accepted 2026-09-18 07:52:57 ET | TFC filing (linked in section 3) | Officer title "President & CEO", director flag = 1 | Low |
| TFC | No other director made a code-P purchase | 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-15, filings accepted by the cutoff | n/a | None of the 2,073 parsed filings shows one | n/a | Low, but subject to the coverage limits in section 6 |
| CRL, Coleman | The CFO's code-P trade was an employee stock purchase plan acquisition | 2026-09-30 | Accepted 2026-10-02 16:27:48 ET | CRL filing (linked in section 3) | F1 "Employee Stock Purchase Plan" | Low |
| Filings dated 10/16 | Every S&P 500 Form 4 was accepted after the cutoff | 2026-10-16 | n/a | Full-text search (linked in section 2) | Acceptance times 09:00–14:31 ET | Full-text search may not return every filing |

## 5. Conditional review and change policy
No holdings were supplied and none are recommended. A name becomes eligible when a new Form 4, filed by the cutoff in force at that time, shows an S&P 500 CEO or CFO and a different director both making qualifying open-market purchases (code P, not under a plan) within a trailing 30-day window.
- For example, a TFC director's qualifying purchase dated on or before 2026-10-17 would fall within 30 days of Lyons's 9/17 purchase and complete a cluster.
- If a name qualifies later, the section 1 rules apply, and the qualifying insiders' names stay attached to the position. It's held until six months after SEC acceptance of the filing that completes the cluster, or exited earlier if any of those insiders discloses an open-market sale not made under a plan.

## 6. Coverage gaps and limitations
- **Membership:** the list comes from Wikipedia, not S&P Dow Jones Indices. I matched companies to tickers by CIK, which also handles companies with two share classes because both classes share one CIK.
- **Form types and timing:** I didn't screen Form 5. A trade dated in the window but not filed by the cutoff is out of scope by design.
- **Roles:** roles come from each filing's relationship fields. I didn't cross-check them against proxy statements.
- **Earlier filings:** I didn't check Form 4s filed before 9/16. A trade dated on or after 9/16 can't appear in a filing made before 9/16, so this only matters if a filing was back-dated.
- **Plan classification:** I relied on the footnotes and the plan flag and didn't read the plan documents.

No orders, account changes, schedules or monitors were executed, and no broker or private data was used.

## Supporting files
Everything is in the case folder `/workspace/grok-bot-native-P04-trial-1-20261016`:
- **Filing index:** `s1_index.py` pulls the daily indexes into `raw_index/`, producing `form4_index_rows.json` and `index_log.json`.
- **Index membership:** `s2_sp.py` saves the Wikipedia revision as `sp500_wiki_rev1380159481.html` and the parsed list as `sp500_members.csv`.
- **Filing download:** `s3_fetch.py` writes `sp500_form4_accessions.json` and saves the 2,073 submissions in `raw_filings/`.
- **Parsing:** `s4_parse.py` writes `transactions_P_S.csv` (3,960 purchase and sale rows) and `window_purchases.csv` (121 rows).
- **10/16 check:** `s5_oct16.py` failed with the 403 error. The check that worked was an unsaved inline script; its output is `efts_20261016.json`, and section 2 summarizes it.
- **Cluster result:** `cluster_result.csv`

## 1. Rules I set before ranking (fixed for this trial)
- **Estimate source:** the Yahoo Finance "Analysis" page, which shows LSEG/Refinitiv consensus. Only archived copies captured on or before the decision time count.
- **Forecast period:** the current fiscal year's EPS consensus, which Yahoo labels "Current Year".
- **30-day window:** I compare the consensus on the 2026-09-30 capture with the "30 Days Ago" figure on that same page. A 2026-08-31 capture is only a cross-check. A capture up to 2 trading days before 9/30 is accepted but flagged, and nothing after 9/30 is used.
- **Strength:** (current-year EPS consensus now ÷ the same consensus 30 days earlier) − 1.
- **Breadth:** (upward revisions in the last 30 days − downward revisions) ÷ number of estimates.
- **Momentum:** total-return-adjusted price change from the 2026-03-31 close to the 2026-09-30 close, with no skipped month.
- **Normalization:** cross-sectional z-scores, capped at ±3.
- **Composite score:** 25% strength + 25% breadth + 50% momentum.
- **Qualification:** complete data, strength above 0 and breadth above 0. Companies with missing data are excluded.
- **Ties:** higher breadth wins, then alphabetical ticker.
- **Fewer than five qualify:** recommend only the companies that qualify, with no fill-ins. A partial sample is never presented as a universe-wide top five.
- **Universe:** S&P 500 members as of 2026-09-30. I didn't establish this list.

## 2. Coverage

- Momentum verified: 0 companies.

Captured response
**P06 Oligopoly Champions: research memo (recommendation only)**

- **Template:** P06.
- **Status:** Partial. Two names are supported, S&P Global fully and Visa with a secondary-source caveat. I didn't test the other candidates, so their absence isn't a negative finding.
- **Decision time:** reference US close, 2026-10-15 16:00 ET (America/New_York).
- **Research cutoff:** 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z.
- **When I pulled the data:** 2026-10-16 around 19:07 UTC, which is after the cutoff. I only used records published before the cutoff.

**1. Rules set before looking at results (kept fixed for the whole trial)**

**Markets**
- M1 is US credit ratings from SEC-registered rating agencies (NRSROs), measured by ratings outstanding in all categories at 2025-12-31.
- M2 is US general-purpose credit card purchase volume across Visa, Mastercard, Amex and Discover in calendar 2025.

**How a market qualifies:** the top three firms hold at least 80%, or the HHI (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index, the sum of squared market shares) is at least 2,500. Share data must cover the same market and period as the leadership claim. The leader is the firm with the largest share in that market.

**ROIC (return on invested capital) = NOPAT ÷ average invested capital**
- NOPAT is operating income × (1 − effective tax rate). The effective tax rate is income tax ÷ pre-tax income.
- Invested capital is total debt plus equity minus cash, averaged over the last two fiscal year-ends.
- Figures are consolidated, from the latest 10-K filed before the cutoff.

**FCF (free cash flow) = operating cash flow − capital spending**, also shown as FCF ÷ revenue and FCF ÷ net income.

**Quality bar:** ROIC of at least 10%, FCF ÷ net income of at least 0.9, and an FCF margin of at least 20%.

**Weights:** equal across names that qualify, at most five, and the list isn't padded.

**2. Recommendation (provisional; no positions are assumed)**

| Name | Weight | Market | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| S&P Global (SPGI, CIK 64040) | 50% | M1 | Primary SEC data |
| Visa (V, CIK 1403161) | 50% | M2 | Secondary share source (Nilson Report) |

**3. Markets, concentration and leadership**

**M1, credit ratings.** Ratings outstanding at 2025-12-31 come from the [SEC NRSRO statistics page](https://www.sec.gov/data-research/statistics-data-visualizations/nationally-recognized-statistical-rating-organizations-nrsros), last updated 2026-06-30, which is before the cutoff.

| Agency | Ratings outstanding | Share |
|---|---|---|
| S&P | 1,077,798 | 49.16% |
| Moody's | 684,055 | 31.20% |
| Fitch | 274,291 | 12.51% |
| All 10 NRSROs | 2,192,543 | 100% |

- The top three hold 92.9% and the HHI is about 3,564, so M1 qualifies easily. S&P leads Moody's by about 18 points.
- The [SEC 2025 staff report](https://www.sec.gov/files/2025-ocr-staff-report-compliant-4-24-26.pdf), published 2026-04-24, supports this. It says "The large NRSROs accounted for 93.38% of all the ratings outstanding as of December 31, 2024."
- **Caveat:** these are counts of ratings, not revenue, and government securities make up much of the count. The same report says S&P's share falls 18.16 points and Moody's falls 6.26 points once government securities are excluded. In that narrower market S&P's lead is much smaller, and I didn't compute shares for it.

**M2, US credit card purchase volume.** The source is the Nilson Report, Issue 1301, a secondary source ([article](https://nilsonreport.com/articles/global-brand-cards-us-2025/), [issue page](https://nilsonreport.com/newsletters/1301/)).
- The four brands together handled $6.512T, "up 6.1% from 2024."
- On Visa: "Credit card purchase volume on Visa cards increased 6.5% to $3.412 trillion."
- That gives Visa a **52.40% share**. Because one firm holds more than half, the HHI is at least 2,745 (52.4 squared), so M2 qualifies.
- **Uncertainty:** the issue's exact publication date isn't shown. It's very likely early 2026, since the Q3 2025 issue was No. 1299, but I couldn't verify that. Mastercard, Amex and Discover shares are behind a paywall.

**4. ROIC and FCF results**

Figures are in $ millions, from the latest 10-K filed before the cutoff, using SEC XBRL company data. Mastercard and Moody's are the main alternatives.

| Company | Fiscal year end | 10-K accession / filed | Revenue | Op. income | Eff. tax | NOPAT | ROIC | FCF | FCF margin | FCF ÷ net income |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Visa | 2025-09-30 | 0001403161-25-000089 / 2025-11-06 | 40,000 | 23,994 | 17.1% | 19,892 | 42.4% | 21,577 | 53.9% | 1.08 |
| S&P Global | 2025-12-31 | 0000064040-26-000013 / 2026-02-11 | 15,336 | 6,478 | 22.6% | 5,014 | 11.7% | 5,456 | 35.6% | 1.22 |
| Moody's | 2025-12-31 | 0001628280-26-009136 / 2026-02-18 | 7,718 | 3,351 | 21.3% | 2,636 | 29.4% | 2,575 | 33.4% | 1.05 |
| Mastercard | 2025-12-31 | 0001141391-26-000013 / 2026-02-11 | 32,791 | 18,897 | 19.4% | 15,225 | 93.9% | 17,159 | 52.3% | 1.15 |

Average invested capital for each company is in `roic_fcf_results.csv`, along with any fallbacks used when a company's filing data didn't carry the standard item.

**5. Alternatives and pricing power**

- **Moody's vs. S&P Global.** Moody's has the higher ROIC (29% vs. 12%). S&P's ROIC is pulled down by goodwill from the IHS Markit merger, and I didn't compute a ratings-only ROIC. I chose S&P because the mandate asks for the share leader, and S&P still passes the quality bar. This is an open conflict: ranking by quality first, or defining the market without government securities, could reasonably point to Moody's.
- **Mastercard vs. Visa.** Mastercard has the higher ROIC, but Visa holds a verified 52.4% of the defined market. I couldn't see Mastercard's share. Visa's FCF margin is also a bit higher.
- **Pricing power.** Both markets are regulated or run on network effects, where issuers have to work with the established names. Both companies turn more than 100% of net income into FCF and have FCF margins above 33%. I didn't run a numeric pricing test, such as fee per unit over time.

**6. Not tested (time limit, not a negative finding)**

I pulled no data for ASML (EUV lithography), TSMC (contract chip manufacturing), Intuitive Surgical, Sherwin-Williams or Waste Management. They were neither admitted nor rejected.

**7. Quarterly review and replacement policy (conditional)**

Review each quarter after new 10-Q or 10-K filings and annual share updates. Recommend replacing a name only if one of these holds across two reviews in a row:
- **Leadership lost:** the company is no longer the largest by share in its defined market. For M1 this would show in the next SEC NRSRO data, and for M2 in the next Nilson annual figures.
- **Market no longer concentrated:** the HHI falls below 2,500 and the top-three share falls below 80%.
- **Quality failure:** on a trailing basis, ROIC falls below 10%, FCF ÷ net income falls below 0.8, or FCF margin falls below 20%.
- **Structural hit to pricing power:** a final regulatory or court action cuts the company's core fee economics. For Visa that could be a DOJ antitrust ruling or US interchange or routing legislation. For S&P it could be a change to NRSRO rules.

Otherwise, the recommendation is to hold.

**8. Limitations**

- Data was pulled after the cutoff. Every figure was filtered by its filing or publication date, and all 10-Ks were filed between Nov 2025 and Feb 2026. Visa's FY2026 10-K wasn't filed by the cutoff, so its figures are FY2025.
- ROIC is consolidated, not by segment.
- NRSRO shares count ratings, not revenue.
- The Nilson data is secondary, its publication date is unverified, and competitor shares are paywalled.
- I didn't use market prices, valuation or the 2026-10-15 close.

**9. Confirmation**

No orders, broker or account access, account changes, schedules or monitors were executed. I used only public data, in a new case folder, with no installs or background processes.

**Case artifacts** are in `/workspace/grok-bot-native-P06-trial-1-20261016/`:
- `roic_fcf.py` and `roic_fcf_results.csv` hold the ROIC and FCF math and outputs.
- `concentration.py` and `concentration_results.csv` hold the share and HHI math.
- `cf_0001403161.json`, `cf_0000064040.json`, `cf_0001059556.json` and `cf_0001141391.json` are the raw SEC company data files used as inputs.

# P07: AI Bottleneck. Research memo (recommendations only)

- **Template ID:** P07: AI Bottleneck
- **Recommendation status:** PROVISIONAL. I'm moderately confident in the bottleneck call. The basket is an equal-weight list with documented gaps (§6).
- **Research decision cutoff:** 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z. I used only material published by then.
- **Reference close:** 2026-10-15 16:00 America/New_York.
- **Retrieval:** all sources were retrieved 2026-10-16, about 19:10–19:25 UTC, which is after the cutoff. Anything dated after the cutoff was left out, including 2026-10-16 intraday prices.

## 1. Conventions (fixed for this trial)
| Convention | Choice |
|---|---|
| Geography | US deployment of AI data centers. Global supply chains count where they feed US builds. |
| Planning horizon | 2026-Q4 through year-end 2028 |
| Evidence freshness | Published 2026-04-01 to the cutoff. Older or undated items are flagged. |
| Binding constraint | The input whose limited supply actually delays or caps energized, operating AI capacity over the horizon. It needs evidence of delayed or rationed deployment, not just demand. Easing it would raise deployment more than easing any other category, and it can't be fixed within about 12 months. |
| Direct-exposure measure | Share of revenue from segments that sell equipment into the binding category, ranked from segment and management disclosures. I didn't extract exact percentages (gap). |
| FCF definition | Cash from operations minus capex, from SEC XBRL. TTM = FY2025 + H1-2026 − H1-2025. |
| FCF forecast horizon | FY2026, using management guidance only |
| Valuation | Market cap = XBRL cover-page shares × the 2026-10-15 close. FCF yield = FCF ÷ market cap. |
| Allocation rule | Equal weight, 1/3 each |

## 2. Five-category comparison
| Category | Dated evidence of actual limitation | Time to fix | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compute chips and CoWoS packaging | TSMC's CEO said on the 2Q26 call that packaging is "so tight that now it's limiting my customers' growth." This comes via a secondary source (S8, 2026-07-16). On the 3Q26 call TSMC said it has "nearly 20 fabs worldwide in progress" (S7, 2026-10-15). | 12–24 months | Binds chip supply; expansion is under way |
| Memory (HBM) | SK hynix said client HBM requests over the next three years "already far exceeds our production capacity" (S9, 2026-04-23). | More than 12 months | Tight and allocated, but it moves together with CoWoS |
| Networking (optics) | McKinsey estimates a 30–40% shortfall in 1.6T transceivers through 2029. Lumentum says its EMLs are "sold out for 2026." Both dates are unverified (S10, S11). | Years for new fabs | Tight, but I found no verified case of deployment being delayed by optics |
| Cooling (liquid) | CDU lead times run 6–10 months, and Vertiv is adding capacity (S17, S6). | 6–12 months | Not binding |
| Electrical power | GSU transformer lead times passed 160 weeks by 1Q26, and HV breakers are at 125 weeks (S12, 2026-07-09). Heavy-frame turbines take 5–7 years (S13). GE Vernova has 116 GW of gas backlog plus slot reservations, but builds only about 20 GW a year (S1, 2026-07-22). Eaton says only about 20% of its 307 GW US data-center backlog converts near term (S5). | 3–7 years | **Binding** |

## 3. Bottleneck conclusion
For US deployment over 2026-Q4 to 2028, the binding constraint is **electrical power delivery**: grid interconnection plus long-lead generation and grid equipment. Three reasons:
- The time to fix it is longer than the planning horizon.
- Primary manufacturer data show backlogs that run for years against limited annual output.
- Eaton says most of its backlog converts in 2028 and later, which is direct evidence that deployment is being deferred.

My confidence is about 55–65%. That's a subjective judgment, not a measured figure.

**Competing hypotheses:**
- **CoWoS/packaging (strongest rival).** I have no verified data on idle GPUs waiting for power that would separate it from power, so the two may bind at the same time.
- **HBM.** It moves together with CoWoS.
- **Optics.** The shortfall estimates are big, but I found no evidence of deployment delays.

**Counterevidence:**
- Exelon reportedly cut its "high probability" data-center load from about 18 GW to 11 GW, and ERCOT is auditing about 474 GW of large-load requests (S16, secondary). Both suggest the queues are inflated.
- Behind-the-meter power can bypass interconnection in 24–36 months.
- New equipment capacity is expected to start easing things from 2028 (S13).

## 6. Methodology, gaps and conflicts
I searched each category plus the companies' primary releases. I downloaded SEC XBRL companyfacts, kept only filings dated on or before the cutoff, and computed TTM figures in `code/fcf.py`. Prices came from the Yahoo chart API after Stooq blocked the download.

**Gaps:**
- Most passages come from search extracts, not full-document reads.
- Several publication dates are unverified.
- Exposure percentages weren't extracted.
- There are no independent FCF estimates.
- The Vertiv guidance range and the Eaton transcript come from secondary hosts.
- Q3-2026 results come after the cutoff and weren't used.

**Unresolved conflicts:**
- Power vs. CoWoS can't be separated without idle-GPU data.
- Speculative queue inflation cuts against the headline backlog figures.
- GEV's TTM FCF isn't representative because of down-payment timing.

## 7. Conditional review and rotation policy (nothing scheduled)
At each monthly review I'd rotate only if new evidence shows the bottleneck has changed. No incumbent portfolio was supplied, so all of these are conditional.
- **Rotate toward chips, packaging or HBM** (for example TSMC, Micron or SK hynix) if any of these show up: verified reports of energized capacity starved for GPUs, TSMC saying packaging stays limiting into 2027, or HBM allocation extending further.
- **Trim power-equipment names** if any of these show up: GEV misses its target of at least 125 GW of gas backlog plus reservations by year-end 2026, transformer or breaker lead times fall for two straight quarters, large-load queue cancellations speed up, or hyperscalers cut capex guidance.
- **Company triggers:** an FY26 FCF guidance cut or a miss of more than 10% against the midpoint, book-to-bill below 1.0 for two quarters, or TTM FCF yield below 2% with no growth upgrade.
- **Upgrade from provisional** once exposure percentages and independent FCF estimates are verified.

## 1. Recommendation
- **Stellantis N.V. (STLA, NYSE) gets 100% of the allocation.** It's the only name in the top five that confirmed.
- I didn't allocate to the other four, and I didn't backfill from Fluor (#6) or anything lower.
  - Coupang, PG&E and NVIDIA failed to confirm under the declared rules.
  - CVS is unresolved, which is not the same as failing.

## 2. Conventions (fixed before ranking)
- **Data source:** the Senate LDA API, second-quarter filings for 2025 and 2026. The API now redirects to `https://lda.gov/api/v1/filings/`.
- **Self-filers only:** the client must be the registrant itself, either by the `client_self_select` flag or by an exact name match.
- **Spending basis:** only the LD-2 `expenses` field.
  - Every LD-2 filing type counts, including amendments, but not registrations (RR/RA).
  - For each registrant and quarter I kept the latest filing posted by the cutoff (`dt_posted` at or before the cutoff).
- **Universe pulled:** filings that reported at least $500k in either year.
  - That came to 474 filings for 2025 and 437 for 2026, or 362 unique registrants.
  - When one year's filing was missing, I fetched it by registrant ID.
- **Minimum base (declared up front):** a company needs at least $500k in Q2 2025 to be ranked. The 58 below that are listed separately.
- **U.S.-listed test:** the company or its parent must trade on NYSE or Nasdaq, as common shares or ADSs.
  - I checked this by hand for the ranked names only.
  - Private firms, associations, nonprofits, and companies listed only OTC or abroad are excluded.
- **Parent/subsidiary dedupe:** subsidiaries are added into their listed parent. For example, Waymo and Google Client Services roll into Alphabet.
- **Growth:** (Q2'26 − Q2'25) / Q2'25.
- **Tie rule:** higher growth wins, then registrant name A to Z. No ties came up.
- **Contract confirmation:**
  - Source: USAspending contract awards (types A–D), net obligations by action date.
  - Windows: 2025-10-01 to 2026-10-15, compared with 2024-10-01 to 2025-10-15.
  - Recipients were matched by name. For CVS I kept only recipients named CVS or Aetna.
  - A name passes if current obligations are at least $1M and up more than 0% year over year.
  - Award announcements in press releases don't count; only obligations do.
- **Backlog confirmation:**
  - A name passes if reported backlog is up more than 0% year over year in the latest 10-Q or 10-K filed by the cutoff.
  - I screened for it with an EDGAR full-text search for "backlog".
  - Remaining performance obligations (RPO) don't count as backlog.
- **Weights:** equal across confirmed names. If nothing confirms, hold cash.

## 4. Confirmation evidence
All contract figures come from USAspending's [recipient spending endpoint](https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_category/recipient/), retrieved 2026-10-16 at about 20:31Z. The backlog screen used [EDGAR full-text search](https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index).

| Ticker | Contracts, current window | Contracts, prior window | YoY | Backlog | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPNG | $0 | $0 | undefined | No "backlog" hits in 10-Q/10-K filings from 2025-10-01 to 2026-10-15 (CIK 0001834584). A test search for "revenue" got 7 hits, so the search worked. | Not confirmed (no evidence found by this method) |
| PCG | $11,835,636 | $60,266,597 | −80.4% | not used | Fails |
| NVDA | $0 | $0 | undefined | No "backlog" hits across the 10-Qs filed 2025-11-19, 2026-05-20 and 2026-08-26 and the 10-K filed 2026-02-25. | Not confirmed |
| CVS | $5,786,853 | −$33,324,825 (mainly a $40.19M deobligation at CVS Pharmacy) | undefined (prior-window base is below zero) | not checked | Unresolved |
| STLA | $545,633,230 (FCA US LLC) | $254,195,533 | +114.6% | not needed | Confirmed |

Contract obligations rising alongside lobbying spending shows timing, not that the lobbying caused the contracts.

## 5. Weights
**STLA gets 100%**, and the other four top-five names get 0%. If CVS is later confirmed, by backlog data or by obligations matched to its exact recipient records, the split becomes 50% STLA and 50% CVS.

## 6. Conditional quarterly policy (not deployed)
- Once the next filing cycle is complete, rerun the screen with the same conventions. The next comparison is Q3 2026 versus Q3 2025.
- Exit a name if either of these happens:
  - Its lobbying growth for the latest complete quarter is 0% or lower.
  - Its contract obligations or reported backlog fall more than 10% year over year.
- Otherwise hold it. New names come in only by ranking first, taking the top five, then confirming.
- **Nothing was executed:** no orders, paper trades, account changes, schedules or monitors.

## 7. Limitations
- **Verified:** the LDA figures and URLs, and the USAspending totals as they stood when I retrieved them.
- **Coverage gaps:**
  - The $500k screen leaves out smaller filers.
  - I checked listings by hand for the ranked names only.
  - Companies that lobby only through outside firms (income basis) aren't included.
  - Because of these gaps, this is not a complete top five of U.S.-listed companies.
- **Data vintage:** I pulled USAspending after the cutoff, so records added after the cutoff may be included. LDA records were filtered by posting date.
- **Contract matching:** matching was by recipient name, not by unique entity ID (UEI), so a $0 could mean contracts are booked under other entity names.
- **Backlog:** I only did a keyword search, and none for CVS. I didn't check Stellantis entities other than FCA US.

## Artifacts (case folder)
- Scripts: `fetch_lda.py`, `fill.py`, `rank.py`, `usas.py`.
- Raw inputs: `inputs/lda_q2_2025_min500k.json`, `inputs/lda_q2_2026_min500k.json`, `inputs/usaspending_recipient_contracts.json`, `inputs/edgar_check.txt`.
- Intermediate data: `self_filers_raw.json`, `self_filers_filled.json`.
- Results: `lda_self_filers_all.csv` and `top5_and_confirmation.csv`.

Original strategy mandate (verbatim reference; scope override controls):
At each month-end, classify U.S. growth and inflation as rising or falling using predefined, revision-aware economic series. Hold SPY when growth rises and inflation falls; hold TLT when both fall; hold equal weights of GLD and DBC when both rise; and hold equal weights of GLD and SGOV when growth falls and inflation rises. Frozen recommendation request:
Reconstruct the latest completed month-end U.S. growth/inflation classification from predefined, revision-aware public series and recommend the exact ETF allocation prescribed by the resulting regime.

Frozen conventions:

Series/formula choice is delegated; publish enough inputs to reproduce it.

- No prior portfolio or regime state is supplied. State the initial recommendation and explain that later changes are recommended only when the monthly regime changes; do not invent a prior regime or assert a trade occurred.

Captured response
**P09: Four-Regime Rotation research memo**

**Status:** The recommendation is resolved, with the caveats noted below. Growth was **falling** and inflation was **falling**, so the map prescribes **100% TLT**. This is the initial recommendation because no prior regime was supplied.
- **Decision time:** 2026-09-30 16:00 America/New_York (month-end convention)
- **Common research cutoff:** 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z
- **Data retrieved:** 2026-10-16 at about 19:48 UTC. That's after the cutoff, but the snapshots are pinned to the 2026-09-30 vintage, so nothing published later was used.

**Conventions (set before computing and kept fixed)**
- **Growth series:** FRED/ALFRED `INDPRO`, US industrial production index, monthly, seasonally adjusted.
- **Inflation series:** FRED/ALFRED `CPIAUCSL`, CPI for all urban consumers, monthly, seasonally adjusted.
- **Vintage and lag rule:** use the ALFRED vintage dated 2026-09-30 and its latest observation, which is August 2026 for both series. Release lag is handled by using whatever was published in that vintage.
- **Transformation:** year-over-year % change of the latest month minus year-over-year % change three months earlier (Aug-26 vs May-26). Every value comes from the same vintage, and year-ago months are matched by date.
- **Sign rule:** a difference above 0 means rising and below 0 means falling. A difference of exactly 0.00 percentage points counts as falling and gets flagged; that didn't happen here.
- **Missing release:** use the latest earlier observation in that vintage. If the needed values can't be recovered, the regime stays unresolved. The vintage has a blank for October 2025 CPI, which is consistent with the 2025 government-shutdown gap, but no calculation needed that month.
- **Initialization:** with no prior state, the first month-end classification sets the allocation.

**Calculation (vintage 2026-09-30)**

| Series | Aug-26 | Aug-25 | YoY Aug-26 | May-26 | May-25 | YoY May-26 | Difference | Sign |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| INDPRO | 103.0682 | 101.6247 | 1.42% | 102.6396 | 100.9655 | 1.66% | −0.24 pp | Falling |
| CPIAUCSL | 334.131 | 323.291 | 3.35% | 333.979 | 320.62 | 4.17% | −0.81 pp | Falling |

**Evidence ledger**
- **INDPRO, vintage 2026-09-30:** I used the values for Aug-26, Aug-25, May-26 and May-25. The column header in the file reads `INDPRO_20260930`. [ALFRED INDPRO vintage CSV](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/graph/alfredgraph.csv?id=INDPRO&vintage_date=2026-09-30)
- **CPIAUCSL, vintage 2026-09-30:** I used the same four months. The column header reads `CPIAUCSL_20260930`, and October 2025 is blank. [ALFRED CPIAUCSL vintage CSV](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/graph/alfredgraph.csv?id=CPIAUCSL&vintage_date=2026-09-30)
- **Uncertainty:**
  - ALFRED vintages are dated by day, so I can't confirm the values were posted by 16:00 New York time specifically.
  - I didn't independently confirm the BLS release date for August 2026 CPI or the Fed's G.17 release date for August 2026 industrial production. The vintage shows the August values were available by 2026-09-30.
  - CPI drops from 333.979 in May to 332.568 in June in this vintage. I used it as published.

**Allocation map (exact)**
- Growth rising and inflation falling: 100% SPY
- Growth falling and inflation falling: **100% TLT** (the current result)
- Growth rising and inflation rising: 50% GLD and 50% DBC
- Growth falling and inflation rising: 50% GLD and 50% SGOV

**Conditional policy going forward:** at each month-end, rerun the same series and rules on that month-end's vintage. Hold TLT while both stay falling, and switch to the mapped allocation only when the regime changes. No orders, account changes, schedules or monitors were created.

**Case artifacts** are in `/workspace/grok-bot-native-P09-trial-1-20261016`. The raw vintage downloads are `INDPRO_vint.csv` and `CPIAUCSL_vint.csv`, the calculation script is `p09.py`, and the results table is `results.csv`.

**Process note:** the first run of the script matched CPI year-ago months by row position. The blank October 2025 row threw that off, so I fixed it to match by date before any result was reported. The saved script is the corrected version.

## 3. Source and assumption ledger
- **Verified SoFi public disclosures:** ledger rows 1–7.
- **Terms you supplied:**
  - The profile and the 83/14/2/1 fallback.
  - The 0.25% fee formula. SoFi's own disclosure (ledger row 5) independently confirms the 0.25% rate.
  - The rebalance and review rules.
- **My independent approximations:** the benchmark convention and my reading of the PDF columns. I produced no return or risk estimate.

## 4. Methodology and conventions (fixed for this trial)
- **Source:** SoFi's primary PDF, reached through SoFi's own support page.
- **Account type:** I used the IRA table as the tax-neutral, non-municipal version. SoFi labels these tables by account type, not by tax treatment.
- **Bands:** I computed sleeve-level bands at a strict ±5.0 points, floored at 0: stocks 78–88, bonds 9–19, gold 0–7, cash 0–6. The separate cash triggers in section 7 still apply.

## 5. Analytics, benchmark and gaps
- **No price-history analytics:** my attempt to download public price data for proxy ETFs from Stooq, a free price-data site, returned a block page instead of data. So there are no backward-looking returns, volatility, drawdowns, forward capital-market estimates or covariance figures.
- **Expense ratios and liquidity:** I didn't verify these, and they should be checked in each fund's prospectus.
- **Benchmark (my own convention, not SoFi's):** 83% global equity (for example, MSCI ACWI), 16% US aggregate bonds including gold, and 1% cash. I didn't compute any benchmark-relative figures.
- **Exposures:**
  - About 69% US equity.
  - About 14% international equity, from EFG, EFV, CORO and VWO; this sums to 18% when BAI and SHLD are excluded, so the 69/14 split doesn't fully reconcile and is unresolved.
  - The active and thematic funds (DYNF, THRO, CORO, BAI and SHLD) add tracking-error risk.
  - SPTL lengthens the bond sleeve's duration.
- **SoFi's method:** none was disclosed. I don't attribute any optimizer, shrinkage covariance, risk-aversion parameter or 12% volatility target to SoFi.

## 6. Fees
- **Advisory fee:** monthly fee = 0.0025/12 × that month's average daily invested assets, excluding cash. With no account value supplied, I calculated no dollar amount.
- **Fund expense ratios:** these are charged inside each fund, separately from the advisory fee. Don't count them twice. Their values aren't verified here.

## 7. Conditional rebalance and review policy (none deployed)
- **Drift trigger:** rebalance when any holding's absolute deviation from target is strictly greater than 5.0 points.
- **Cash triggers** (separate from drift and from each other):
  - Cash is at least $50 above its 1% target.
  - Cash is below 0.25%.
- **Other triggers:** a change in strategy, risk profile or the approved model.
- **Inflows:** use deposits, dividends and distributions to reduce underweights first, where practical.
- **Idle cash:** hold investable cash under $50 until it reaches that threshold. The threshold never blocks a correction triggered independently by a risk, profile or model change.
- **Tax handling:** use the broker's default lot handling, with no automated tax-loss harvesting or tax-aware optimization.
- **Monitoring (conditional policy only):** check holdings every market day.
- **Model review:** review the model at least quarterly. Approve and version every change, then implement it within 0–3 weeks.
- **Without an account snapshot:** none of these triggers can be evaluated yet.

**P11, Google PageRank: status UNRESOLVED.** There's no top-10 recommendation and no S&P 500 scores.

- **Template:** P11
- **Common research cutoff:** 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z
- **Reference close:** 2026-10-15 16:00 America/New_York
- **Memo prepared:** 2026-10-16 about 19:50 UTC (retrieval time, not evidence time)

**Why it's unresolved (insufficient evidence, not verified absence)**
1. **Universe:** I didn't retrieve or freeze a dated S&P 500 constituent snapshot as of the cutoff. Without one, there's no node list.
2. **Cycle:** By the cutoff (mid-October 2026), the calendar Q3 2026 reporting season had only just started. Mostly large banks and a few early reporters had published. So Q3 is incomplete and can't be used, and the latest completed cycle would be calendar Q2 2026 (reports roughly mid-July to late August 2026, with off-calendar fiscal filers mapped to the quarter their period ends in). I didn't verify through primary sources that every constituent had reported for that cycle, so the cycle completion cutoff isn't established.
3. **Corpus:** The method needs about 500 earnings releases plus prepared remarks and company-published transcripts. That's thousands of primary documents, each needing a URL, a publication date, and mention extraction. I retrieved none of them. Many companies also don't publish their own transcripts, and that coverage gap wasn't measured either.
4. **Entity mapping and edges:** No mentions were extracted, so there's no edge list, no mention-to-ticker evidence, and no exclusion ledger.
5. **Computation:** PageRank wasn't run on any S&P 500 graph. Running it without the inputs above would mean making up scores.

The core reason is that this corpus can't be gathered and mapped auditably within a 600-second budget. A familiar-company list would not be a valid substitute.

**Claim-to-evidence ledger:** It's empty. No decision-driving facts were verified. The cycle-timing point in item 2 is based on the usual reporting calendar, and I haven't verified it from sources.

**Fixed conventions for any future run:**
- Damping is 0.85.
- Teleportation is uniform over all frozen nodes, and dangling-node mass is redistributed uniformly.
- Scores sum to 1.
- Power iteration runs until the L1 change between rounds is at most 1e-10.
- Ranking is by raw score, highest first. Exact ties go to the ascending ticker, with each share class counted as its own ticker (for example, `GOOGL` and `GOOG` are separate nodes).
- Edges are unweighted and directed, with repeat mentions collapsed to one. Self-mentions, subsidiaries and ambiguous names are excluded, and analyst questions don't create edges.

**What I built (in the case folder `/workspace/grok-bot-native-P11-trial-1-20261016`, which I created new for this task):**
- `pagerank.py` implements the conventions above. It reads `nodes.txt` (one ticker per line) and `edges.csv` (source, destination pairs), so it's ready for a real corpus.
- `demo_nodes.txt`, `demo_edges.csv` and `demo_output_ILLUSTRATIVE.txt` are a five-node example with placeholder tickers AAA through EEE. It's **illustrative only and not an S&P 500 result.** It converged in 14 rounds with an L1 change of 8.08e-11, and the scores summed to 1. AAA and BBB tie at 0.4458, and CCC, DDD and EEE (the isolated node) are each at 0.0361.

**Conditional policy going forward:** The recommendation only becomes valid once three things are in place: a frozen universe, a cycle verified as complete, and an auditable edge list. With those, the top 10 by PageRank would each get 10%. After that, it would change only when a new earnings cycle is complete.

I didn't place any orders, change any accounts, deploy any schedules or start any monitoring.

7. Conditional recommendation policy (no execution)
Update rule (new-filing-cycle-only): this recommendation refreshes only after a new completed 13F filing cycle. After the next quarter's filings are available by that cycle's cutoff, re-run the full pipeline (roster → filings → top-10 → consensus) and publish a new dated memo.
Hold rule: between cycles, hold the 10 names at 10% target each. Do not change on price moves, news, earnings, or intra-cycle filings/amendments for the current quarter.
Change rule: at a cycle refresh, replace the basket with the newly computed top-10 consensus names (10% each). If fewer than 20 managers are supported at a future cycle, publish the partial result as provisional per the missing-data policy.
Roster maintenance: if a roster manager stops filing 13F (as Greenlight/Blue Ridge did), replace with the next ordered fallback and disclose the substitution.
Nothing was executed: no orders, no account changes, no schedules, no monitors.
8. Limitations, gaps, and judgments
Roster is a delegated choice (declared pre-computation). Greenlight, Blue Ridge, ValueAct had no usable Q2-2026 filing; replaced by the first three ordered fallbacks (Egerton, D1, SRS). A different defensible roster could differ.
Value-unit anomaly: 19/20 filers reported whole dollars vs the 13F $000s spec (Baupost used $000s). Normalized per filing; cross-checked via implied share prices (AMZN $238.34–$238.36 across 12 filers).
Berkshire combined reporting: duplicate CUSIPs across otherManager rows were summed as the filer's total (standard combined-report treatment).
Share-class counting: GOOGL and GOOG counted separately per declared convention. Sensitivity: at issuer level, Alphabet's manager union is 11/20 (would rank #2). Convention kept fixed as declared.
Mapping residue: 25 small issuers remain unmapped (mostly absent from the SEC tickers file; FNB, GBTG, Perceptive SPAC left unmapped). Automated check: no unmapped issuer meets or exceeds any manager's top-10 cutoff, so the consensus top-10 is unaffected.
Trian has only 7 eligible holdings (<10); contributes 7 names. Disclosed, not treated as a coverage failure.
Admissibility reasons ("long-term approach") are strategy characterizations from public materials (secondary), not turnover-verified; labeled as supplied context, not computed evidence.
Timing: retrieval (2026-10-16) postdates the cutoff; only records available by 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z were used. Work performed within the trial's time budget; top-10 consensus constituents were individually reviewed.
Isolation: all work confined to the fresh case folder muse-native-P02-trial-1-20261016b; only public SEC EDGAR records, SEC reference files, and public web sources were retrieved; built-in libraries only, no installs, no private accounts/data, no background processes beyond the task.

memo.md — this memo
method.json — declared conventions, roster, fallbacks, update rule
cik_map.json — CIK resolution/verification per manager

p02.py, p02c.py — reproducible pipeline (resolve → filings → download → compute)

Bottom line: A complete, verified 20-manager consensus was established from Q2-2026 13F filings (all accepted before the cutoff, no amendments, no coverage gaps in the final roster). The recommended basket is AMZN, GOOGL, META, NVDA, GOOG, TSM, V, AMAT, AMD, MCO — 10% target weight each, to be held until the next completed 13F filing cycle. No trades were placed and no monitoring was deployed; the hold/change rules above are policy only.

Recommendation status: NO-QUALIFIER (provisional) — no names recommended. Zero qualifying insider purchase clusters were found. This is not a verified-exhaustive absence: 55 officer-leg filings were not individually document-verified (see Coverage and limitations).
Research decision cutoff: 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z
Reference regular US market close: 2026-10-15T16:00:00-04:00 (America/New_York)

Case folder: muse-native-P04-trial-1-20261016 (dedicated new folder; public inputs and generated artifacts only)
Recommendation

No names are recommended. Across 68 primary SEC Form 4 documents examined transaction-by-transaction, zero qualifying open-market purchases by a CEO or CFO were found in the window, so no cluster (CEO-or-CFO plus a second distinct director, both purchasing) can be established. The single P-code transaction found — Charles River Laboratories (CRL) CFO Glenn Coleman, 10 shares on 2026-09-30 — is excluded because the filing footnote identifies it as an ESPP (Employee Stock Purchase Plan) acquisition, i.e., a plan transaction, not an open-market purchase.

Because no company qualifies, the declared selection/tie rules and equal weights below are not triggered; they stand as the pre-committed convention for any future qualifier.

Methodology and declared conventions (frozen before results)
Membership: S&P 500 constituents effective at the reference close, from Wikipedia's "List of S&P 500 companies" retrieved 2026-10-16, counting a listing iff its "Date added" is empty or ≤ 2026-10-15. Result: 503 listings. Cross-checked against S&P Dow Jones Indices announcements of 2026-10-01 (VYLR added effective Oct 1; TWLO added and WBD removed effective Oct 6; CTVA removed Oct 1): the list agrees (VYLR added 2026-10-01, TWLO added 2026-10-06; CTVA/WBD absent). No changes effective Oct 7–15, 2026 were found.
Filing universe (primary): SEC EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov), forms=4, filed 2026-09-16..2026-10-15, all 503 member CIKs in batches → 2,073 unique Form 4 filings. Filed-date 2026-10-15 implies acceptance by 22:00 ET Oct 15 (02:00Z Oct 16), before the 03:15Z cutoff; filings dated 2026-10-16 were excluded by the date bound.
Candidate narrowing (primary text index): EFTS indexes filing text with XML tags stripped (verified: "transactionCode" returns 0 hits). Phrase queries are candidate-narrowing only: "Chief Executive Officer" → 45 filings; "Chief Financial Officer" → 81 filings (123 unique officer-leg, 81 issuers); "Director" → 551; "open market" → 13.
Likely-purchase filter: officer-leg filings excluding text containing sale/sold/option/exercise/grant/vesting/restricted → 23 unique filings (heuristic prioritization, not eligibility).
Primary-document verification: www.sec.gov blocks non-browser HTTP clients (HTTP 403) here; a live Chromium browser task loaded the SEC filing index and Form 4 XML for each candidate. 68 primary Form 4 documents were read transaction-by-transaction, recording owner, director/officer/title flags, doc type, and every non-derivative transaction (date, code, shares, price, footnotes).
Eligibility: code P, acquired, non-derivative table, transaction date in window; roles from the filing's relationship block (CEO iff title contains "chief executive officer"; CFO iff contains "chief financial officer"; director iff isDirector). A dual-role person cannot satisfy both legs; a second distinct director-person is required. Grants (A), gifts, option exercises (M), tax withholdings (F), conversions (C), 10b5-1 sales (S), settlements (J), and plan transactions (ESPP/401(k)/DRIP per footnotes) are excluded using codes + footnotes together. Code P alone is not assumed eligible.
Selection/tie rules (declared before results; not triggered): if more than five qualify, rank by (1) distinct qualifying purchasers descending, (2) aggregate qualifying purchase value descending, (3) earliest final cluster-establishing filing availability, (4) ticker ascending. Target weights: equal weight 1/n (notional; no capital).
Exits (conditional; not triggered): six calendar months after public availability (SEC acceptance datetime) of the final filing establishing the cluster; early exit on public disclosure (Form 4) of an open-market sale (code S, non-derivative, disposed) by any qualifying insider in the attached identity set.

Conditional future policy (no execution performed)

No orders were placed or queued; no paper or live account was accessed; no account settings or holdings were altered; no schedules, crons, hooks, or monitors were deployed. The following is a conditional research policy only:

Re-screen trigger: a new qualifying cluster is established when a fresh Form 4 sweep (same conventions) finds an S&P 500 issuer with a CEO-or-CFO and a second distinct director each reporting a supported open-market purchase (code P, non-derivative, in-window, no plan footnote), with filings publicly available.
If a name were recommended: hold until the earlier of (a) six calendar months after the acceptance datetime of the final filing establishing the cluster, or (b) public disclosure of an open-market sale (code S, non-derivative, disposed) by any qualifying insider in that name's attached identity set.
Change conditions: index membership changes, SEC filing corrections/amendments (4/A), or footnote reclassification altering eligibility would revise or void the affected recommendation.
Limitations and unresolved items
55 officer-leg filings (of 123) were not individually document-verified; deprioritized because their text contains sale/sold/option/exercise/grant/vesting/restricted language. A purchase code paired with such language cannot be ruled out — the explicit residual gap.
CEO/CFO phrase queries may miss nonstandard titles (e.g., bare "President"); director phrase hits are word-matches, not a census of director filers.
Roles are proxied by the filing's relationship block as of filing (within days of transaction), per the frozen convention.
Acceptance datetimes are as displayed on SEC filing index pages via the live browser.
Secondary sources used only for membership cross-check (news) and recent-window corroboration (finviz insider page, no S&P 500 buys in its ~Oct 14–16 window); all decision-driving filing evidence is primary (SEC EFTS metadata + SEC Form 4 XML via browser).
One procedural correction: an initial Tier-2 browser task was spawned with fabricated URLs (typed from pattern); it was closed before browsing and respawned with verified URLs. No fabricated URL was visited and no result depends on it. (RUN_NOTES.md)

Predeclared conventions (fixed for this trial; declared before any ranking or conclusion)

Consensus provider and vintage: timestamped point-in-time vendor consensus snapshots (e.g., a licensed estimates feed such as FactSet Estimates or Refinitiv I/B/E/S) with publication/availability timestamps at or before the decision time. Current consensus pages, analyst commentary, and narrative enthusiasm are not acceptable substitutes.
Forecast period: FY1 consensus EPS (current fiscal year) per company.
30-day endpoints: T1 = 2026-08-31 16:00 ET; T0 = 2026-09-30 16:00 ET.
Upward-revision strength: (C0 − C1) / |C1|, where C0 and C1 are FY1 consensus EPS at T0 and T1; exclude the company if C1 = 0 or either vintage is missing.
Upward-revision breadth: share of analysts covering the company at both endpoints whose individual FY1 EPS estimate increased over the window; require at least five covering analysts.
Normalization: cross-sectional z-scores of strength, breadth, and momentum across the qualifying universe, using only information available at T0.
Six-month momentum: total return from the 2026-03-31 close to the 2026-09-30 close on dividend- and split-adjusted prices.
Composite score: 0.40 × z(strength) + 0.30 × z(breadth) + 0.30 × z(momentum); rank descending.
Qualification: S&P 500 member effective at T0; FY1 consensus present at both endpoints; ≥5 covering analysts; strength > 0; valid adjusted momentum prices. If fewer than five companies qualify, return an explicit partial or no-qualifier result and never backfill with non-qualifiers; any small sample is labeled a partial candidate sample, not a universe-wide top five.
Tie-breaker (deterministic): higher strength, then higher breadth, then higher momentum, then ticker alphabetical A–Z.
Missing data: exclude the company; no imputation. If decision-driving inputs are unavailable universe-wide, the ranking is unresolved.

Universe and coverage. Required universe: S&P 500 membership effective 2026-09-30 16:00 ET. Coverage of decision-driving inputs: none obtained — no point-in-time FY1 consensus snapshots, no analyst up/down revision counts, and no verified constituent list reconstructed. No scores, rankings, or ties are presented because no inputs were computed.

**Template ID:** P06 (Oligopoly Champions) · **Recommendation status:** SUPPORTED — five qualifying market-share leaders identified; one qualified inclusion flagged (SPGI, see caveat) · **Decision cutoff:** 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z · **Reference:** US regular close 2026-10-15, America/New_York · **Analysis completed:** 2026-10-16 ~22:25 UTC. **Conventions declared before any ranking (fixed; not tuned after results).** [ASSUMPTION] Defined markets (product × geography × period): (1) US general-purpose card purchase volume, 2024; (2) EUV lithography systems, global, 2024–2025; (3) credit ratings (NRSRO-registered agencies), global, 2024; (4) US insurance salvage vehicle auctions, 2025–2026; (5) US consumer credit scores used in lending decisions, 2025–2026. Concentration admission: CR3 ≥ 70% or documented HHI > 2,500; the selected name must hold the #1 share in that defined market in the most recent full year available by cutoff — a broad corporate share may not substitute for the narrow industry. ROIC = NOPAT ÷ invested capital, where NOPAT = reported operating income × (1 − income-tax-expense ÷ pretax income) and invested capital = total equity + interest-bearing debt − cash & short-term investments, measured at the latest filed fiscal year-end (FY2025 for all five). FCF = operating cash flow − capital expenditures; quality judged on multi-year positivity, FCF margin, and conversion vs. net income. Weights: equal 20% each — no valuation or return forecasting is in scope. Deterioration rule is conditional and future-only (below).

**Recommendation (equal-weighted, 20% each).**

**1. Visa Inc. (V) — US/global payment card networks.** [VERIFIED] Nilson (via Feb 25, 2025 press release) puts 2024 US purchase volume at $10.773tn with Visa at 61.1% vs Mastercard 25.8%, Amex 11.1%, Discover 2.0% — CR2 86.9%, implied HHI ≈ 4,526, far above the 2,500 highly-concentrated line. Globally Visa led H1 2024 purchase transactions at 38.66% (Nilson via CoinLaw). Pricing power: FY2025 operating margin 67.0% ($26.8bn on $40.0bn), a level sustained for a decade — the classic network take-rate moat. Computed FY2025: ROIC 49.4% (NOPAT $22.2bn ÷ IC $45.0bn), FCF $21.6bn, 53.9% FCF margin, 108% conversion. [PROVISIONAL note] One aggregator (stocktitan) presents FY2025 operating income ≈ $23.9bn vs the $26.8bn used here; the figure used is arithmetically consistent with the 10-K-derived statement (40,000 − 894 − 12,298). Even at the lower figure, ROIC ≈ 44% — the conclusion is insensitive to this discrepancy.

**2. ASML Holding (ASML) — EUV lithography.** [VERIFIED] ASML is the sole commercial supplier of EUV lithography systems — effectively 100% of the defined market (industry sources; corroborated by its Form 20-F: 48 EUV systems recognized in 2025 vs 44 in 2024, with no competitor shipping EUV). Pricing power: gross margin 52.8% in 2025, a €38.8bn backlog (≈1.2× revenue), and a mix shift toward higher-ASP EUV (High-NA) systems. Computed FY2025 (€): ROIC 87.1% (NOPAT €9.3bn ÷ IC €10.7bn), FCF €11.0bn, 33.7% margin, 115% conversion. The extraordinary ROIC reflects a structural funding advantage: €19.4bn of customer contract liabilities (prepayments) fund working capital — disclosed, not a formula artifact (the financing-side and operating-side invested-capital measures reconcile identically).

**3. S&P Global (SPGI) — credit ratings.** [VERIFIED] The Big Three NRSROs hold ~97% of outstanding ratings and the three large NRSROs ~91% of industry revenue (SEC staff report Jan 2025; CRS Mar 2024). Leadership within the oligopoly: S&P Global Ratings revenue was $4,370M in 2024 and $4,724M in 2025 (primary: 10-K filed Feb 11, 2026) vs Moody's Investors Service ≈ $3,793M in 2024 — S&P is the #1 agency by roughly 15%. Pricing power: Ratings segment operating margin 64% in 2025, with the 10-K citing "improved contract terms." Computed FY2025: ROIC 11.5% (NOPAT $5.0bn ÷ IC $43.6bn), FCF $5.5bn, 35.6% margin, 113–122% conversion. **Qualified inclusion:** book ROIC is depressed by ~$50bn of IHS Markit acquisition goodwill; operating economics (42% consolidated operating margin, 64% Ratings margin, >100% cash conversion) demonstrate the underlying quality. The figure is reported as computed, not redefined.

**4. Copart (CPRT) — US salvage vehicle auctions.** [VERIFIED, secondary] The industry is effectively a duopoly: Copart ~40–50% and IAA (RB Global) ~30–35%, together ~80% of the US insurance salvage market (Columbia Business School paper, Apr 2026; FinancialContent deep dive, Mar 2026). Pricing power: a two-sided fee marketplace (fees from both insurers and ~800k+ global buyers), ~46% gross margin, ~36.5% operating margin, plus a land moat (owned yards vs. a leasing competitor). Computed FY2025: ROIC 30.8% (NOPAT $1.39bn ÷ IC $4.5bn), FCF $1.23bn, 26.5% margin, 79% conversion — conversion below 100% reflects ongoing yard/land capex, which is growth investment, flagged for the quarterly watch.

**5. Fair Isaac (FICO) — US credit scores.** [VERIFIED] FICO scores are used in ~90% of US lending decisions (Investopedia; FICO's Aug 2026 release: "used by 90% of top US lenders"). Pricing power is direct and dated: the mortgage-score fee rose from cents to $4.95 in 2025 and was set to double to $10 (WSJ, Nov 2025) — evidence of pricing power *and* of its contestability, since the FHFA began a limited VantageScore 4.0 rollout in 2026. Computed FY2025: ROIC 61.3% (NOPAT $751M ÷ IC $1.23bn), FCF $770M, 38.7% margin, 118% conversion; operating margin 46.5%, gross margin ~82%. Caveat disclosed: negative book equity (−$1.7bn from buybacks) flatters the financing-side ROIC; on a capital-structure-neutral basis (NOPAT ÷ (debt − cash) ≈ $751M ÷ $2.93bn) the return is ~26% — still well above any cost-of-capital proxy.

**Material alternatives compared (why not them).** Moody's: higher book ROIC (~30% on my inputs) but #2 in ratings revenue — the mandate selects the share leader, so SPGI. Mastercard: clear #2 in payments (25.8% US). Waste Management: researched and **excluded** — North American waste is only moderately concentrated (WM ~24%, top-3 ~47%, top-5 ~50–52% of ~$130bn), failing the declared CR3 ≥ 70% admission rule; the threshold was applied, not tuned. [UNRESOLVED] Intuitive Surgical, Verisign, CME, and HEICO were not researched within the time box — coverage limitation, not a negative judgment.

P07: AI BOTTLENECK — MONTHLY RESEARCH RECOMMENDATION MEMO (native public-data cohort, trial 1)

Template ID: P07 (AI Bottleneck)
Recommendation status: RECOMMENDATION MADE (supported; see limitations below)
Decision cutoff: 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z
Reference US market close: 2026-10-15 16:00 ET (America/New_York)
Memo date: 2026-10-16
Evaluation integrity note: This is an independent research assessment for this trial's cohort. It was produced from fresh evidence gathered at this cutoff under the scope override (native public-data tools, isolated case folder); it does not pool results with any other cohort.

Declared conventions (fixed before analysis, not tuned after results)

Geography: Global AI buildout, weighted to the United States, where the most decision-driving deployment evidence was available at the cutoff.
Planning horizon: 12–36 months from the cutoff (Oct 2026–Oct 2029).
Evidence freshness: Public records published or available by 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z. Retrieval dates may be later; only pre-cutoff information is used.
Binding constraint meaning: The category whose physical or economic shortfall actually prevents additional AI infrastructure from being deployed on time at the margin over the horizon — not merely the category with the largest TAM, highest demand growth, or highest prices.
Direct-economic-exposure measure: Share of the company's revenue/backlog/guidance growth attributable to the binding constraint's resolution (grid equipment, power delivery, on-site generation), evidenced by reported orders, backlog, segment growth, or management commentary — not share price co-movement.
FCF forecast horizon: FY2026 management guidance where available; otherwise reported trailing/quarterly FCF plus clearly labeled estimates. "Strongest supported" means the strongest FCF outlook verifiable from public records, not the largest absolute number.
Allocation rule: Fixed equal weight, one-third each. Declared upfront; no optimization or post-hoc weighting.

Five-category comparison

Category	Verdict (horizon)	Decision-driving evidence
Compute chips	NOT binding (currently)	NVIDIA's 2026 shipments remain Blackwell-led; Rubin slips into 2027 on HBM4 yields, i.e., logic supply is gated by memory, not foundry. NVIDIA reportedly secured ~650K CoWoS interposers for 2026 (+76% YoY) and 840K for 2027 — adequate packaging supply (TrendForce Sep 2026; KeyBanc checks). Chips are allocatable and shippable; they wait for power and memory, not the reverse.
Memory	TIGHT — leading competing hypothesis, not binding on deployment	HBM 2026 fully sold out (Samsung Q1 call; SK hynix 2026 DRAM+NAND sold out; Micron: much of 2027 locked at higher prices); contract prices +117% w/w early Oct 2026; conventional DRAM contract prices +90–95% QoQ in Q1 2026 and +58–63% in Q2 (TrendForce); suppliers meeting ~75–80% of H2 2026 demand. This raises accelerator costs and delays next-gen ramps (Rubin), but does not prevent racks from being deployed the way interconnection queues do.
Networking	TIGHT, future risk (2027–28), not currently binding	Goldman Sachs expects optical networking revenue to rise >10x 2026–28 with a supply shortage; 800G demand expected to exceed production capacity through mid-2027. However, capacity is scaling (NVIDIA–Corning May 2026 deal to expand US optical connectivity manufacturing 10x; supplier fab expansions underway). A projected constraint, not the current deployment blocker.
Cooling	TIGHT design constraint, not expansion-blocking	Blackwell GB200 NVL72 racks draw 120–140 kW vs 41 kW for H100 racks, mandating direct liquid cooling (TrendForce: single-chip TDP >1 kW). But cooling ships inside the rack system stack and suppliers execute strongly (Vertiv raised 2026 guidance: ~$14B sales, ~$2.5B FCF). Thermal engineering is a design tax, not what cancels projects.
Electrical power	BINDING	Interconnection waits of 4–10 years; high-voltage transformer lead times up to 3–5 years (vs 16–24 weeks pre-2020); switchgear sold out through 2028; of ~12–16 GW announced US data-center capacity for 2026, only ~5 GW under construction; ~30–50% of planned 2026 projects delayed or canceled. Morgan Stanley: US needs 97 GW more power 2026–28 with a 32 GW shortfall even after time-to-power options. Gartner: power shortages constrain 40% of AI data centers by 2027. Google's Amin Vahdat: power is "the only constraint without a clear solution — you cannot order a gigawatt tomorrow." A data center builds in 18–24 months; power takes 7–12 years. Power is what cancels or postpones deployment.

Binding-bottleneck conclusion: Electrical power — specifically grid interconnection queues, high-voltage transformer and switchgear delivery, substation capacity, and time-to-power — is the binding constraint on AI infrastructure expansion over the declared horizon. Memory is the leading competing hypothesis: if HBM4 yields or DRAM capacity inflected sharply worse while interconnection queues cleared, the binding constraint would move to memory. The counterevidence check: everything memory does (price spikes, Rubin delays) affects cost and ramp speed; only power converts announced capacity into non-deployment (5 GW of ~12–16 GW under construction). That distinction is the decision driver.

Three-company recommendation (equal weight, one-third each)

GE Vernova Inc. (GEV) — Gas turbines, grid equipment, and Electrification (transformers/switchgear via Prolec GE acquisition). $176B total backlog (+$13B QoQ, Q2 2026), on track to $200B in 2027; data-center orders >$5B YTD 2026; Q1 Electrification data-center equipment orders ($2.4B) exceeded all of 2025. 2026 FCF guidance raised to $11.5B–$12.5B (from $6.5B–$7.5B), backed by Q1 FCF $4.8B and Q2 FCF $5.1B. Exposure is to the exact bottleneck (grid delivery, turbines for time-to-power).
Eaton Corporation plc (ETN) — Electrical equipment: switchgear, transformers, power distribution for AI campuses. Q2 2026: record $8.5B revenue (+21%), FCF $874M (+22% YoY); Electrical Global backlog +103% YoY; US data-center backlog 307 GW (~15 years at 2025 installation rates); Electrical Americas book-to-bill 1.3. Full-year 2026 FCF guidance was not located — annualized run-rate ~$3.5B is an estimate, not guidance. FY26 organic growth raised to 11–13%, adj. EPS guide $13.40–$13.60.
Bloom Energy Corporation (BE) — On-site fuel cells / behind-the-meter power ("time-to-power" customers). Q2 2026: revenue $1.07B (+166% YoY), FCF $174.8M (vs -$220.4M prior year); FY26 revenue guidance raised to $3.9B–$4.2B (~100% YoY growth); management says all major US hyperscalers and 12+ neoclouds/AI labs/colocation operators have validated Bloom for AI factories. No management FCF guidance located; third-party FY26 FCF estimate ~$810–920M (analyst arithmetic, estimate, not guidance). Valuation is rich (P/E ~279 at cutoff prices per secondary screen).

Conditional alternate: Vertiv Holdings (VRT) for Bloom if stronger primary-verified FCF evidence is required — raised 2026 guidance includes ~$2.5B FCF — but note Vertiv's exposure is cooling/power distribution, which is adjacent to rather than inside the binding constraint.

Claim-to-evidence ledger: Full ledger is in the case folder artifact five-category-evidence-table.csv (category, assertion, observation period, publication/availability date, exact source URL, evidence class, uncertainty notes). Company-level facts with dates and URLs are in company-fcf-table.csv. Key sources: informedclearly.com power-gridlock series (Sep 2026); tradersunion.com Morgan Stanley relay (Oct 13, 2026); incisornews.tech (Oct 15, 2026); TrendForce Rubin report (Sep 21, 2026); rcrtech.com memory market (Oct 2026); fool.com Eaton Q2 transcript (Aug 7, 2026); trefis.com GEV (Oct 9, 2026); barchart.com Bloom Q2 results (Jul 28, 2026); stocktitan.net Bloom guidance (Jul 2026); seekingalpha.com Vertiv guidance (Jul 29, 2026). A later-retrieved page was used only where its publication/availability date was established before the cutoff.

Methodology and unresolved conflicts: Comparison across all five named categories against the binding-constraint definition; conclusions drawn only from public records. No installed packages or statistical modeling; no private data, broker, or connector access. Material gaps: (a) GEV FCF/backlog figures are secondary relays of company statements (primary earnings transcript re-read only for the Q1 guidance step); (b) Eaton has no located full-year 2026 FCF guidance; (c) Bloom has no management FCF guidance — the ~$810–920M figure is a third-party estimate; (d) the "30–50% delayed/canceled" and "5 GW of ~12–16 GW under construction" figures may trace to a small number of underlying industry analyses echoed across outlets; (e) networking/optics evidence is forecast-heavy and secondary. Differing defensible choices (e.g., memory-first with Micron/SK hynix/Samsung) are acknowledged as competing hypotheses, not errors.

Conditional recommendation policy (no orders or monitoring executed): Reassess monthly. Rotate exposure only when new evidence shows the bottleneck has changed — e.g., interconnection queues clearing while HBM4 yields collapse further (rotate toward memory), or 800G/1.6T supply failing to meet 2027 demand while power queues normalize (rotate toward networking). Company-level rotation triggers: a cut to FCF guidance, loss of the bottleneck-linked backlog/order momentum, or evidence the FCF outlook is no longer supported. No positions, holdings, or approvals are supplied; none were placed, queued, changed, or monitored. Basket status remains fully supported on this evidence; it is not provisional, but the three flagged FCF-guidance gaps above are the ones to re-verify at the next monthly review.

Recommendation. Methodology and declared conventions (fixed before any ranking). RESEARCH MEMO — P09: Four-Regime Rotation (recommendations-only evaluation)

Template ID: P09 — Four-Regime Rotation
Recommendation status: UNRESOLVED. The decision-driving inputs were recovered and verified from primary records, but both the growth leg and the inflation leg measure exactly zero change at published precision, and no prior regime state was supplied, so no rising/falling classification — and therefore no ETF allocation — can be prescribed without inventing a tie-break rule.
Evaluation month-end (decision time): 2026-09-30 at 16:00 America/New_York
Common research cutoff: 2026-10-16T03:15:00Z
Retrieval date (this research): 2026-10-16
Scope: dated research recommendation only. No orders placed or queued; no broker, trading venue, private account, or private connector accessed; no account state changed; no schedule deployed; no monitoring started. No local files read or written, no shell invoked, no tools installed, no non-public data used. Only public web search/fetch plus arithmetic and method exposition in this response.

1. Declared methodology (fixed before any computation)

Growth series: U.S. civilian unemployment rate, U-3, seasonally adjusted — BLS series LNS14000000 (FRED: UNRATE). Monthly, percent, as published to one decimal.
Inflation series: CPI-U, all items, 12-month percent change, not seasonally adjusted — BLS CUUR0000SA0 12-month change (FRED: CPIAUCSL-derived). Monthly, percent, as published to one decimal.
Release/lag policy: at each month-end, use the latest reference month whose scheduled BLS release occurred on or before that month-end at 16:00 ET. For 2026-09-30 this means August 2026 references for both series. The September 2026 Employment Situation (released 2026-10-02) and September 2026 CPI (released 2026-10-14) exist by the research cutoff but are excluded by this frozen vintage rule.
Transformation: none — use published values directly; comparison = latest published value minus the immediately preceding published value.
Sign rule (strict inequalities): growth is RISING iff UNRATE(latest) < UNRATE(prior); FALLING iff greater. Inflation is RISING iff CPI12m(latest) > CPI12m(prior); FALLING iff lower.
Zero-change rule: a delta of exactly 0.0 at published precision retains the previous month's leg classification.
Initialization rule: no prior portfolio or regime state was supplied; a retained/zero leg with no prior state is UNRESOLVED; if either leg is unresolved, the regime is unresolved and no allocation is prescribed.
Missing-release policy: if a required release is not published by the vintage cutoff, the leg is left unresolved; no extrapolation and no substitution of later revisions.

2. Vintage window for 2026-09-30 16:00 ET

August 2026 Employment Situation: released Friday 2026-09-04 08:30 ET — available at month-end. August 2026 CPI: released Friday 2026-09-11 08:30 ET — available at month-end. All September 2026 references were released after the month-end and are excluded.

3. Calculation inputs and signs

Growth: UNRATE August 2026 = 4.1%; July 2026 = 4.1%; delta = 0.0 pp → zero-change rule applies → no prior state exists → growth leg UNRESOLVED.
Inflation: CPI-U 12-month August 2026 = 3.4%; July 2026 = 3.4%; delta = 0.0 pp → zero-change rule applies → no prior state exists → inflation leg UNRESOLVED.
Resulting regime: UNRESOLVED. Prescribed allocation: none. No trade is asserted; no prior regime is invented.

4. Prescribed conditional map (exact — all four rules)

Growth rising and inflation falling → 100% SPY.
Growth falling and inflation falling → 100% TLT.
Growth rising and inflation rising → 50% GLD plus 50% DBC.
Growth falling and inflation rising → 50% GLD plus 50% SGOV.
Monthly change rule: re-evaluate at each month-end under the same conventions; recommend an allocation change only when a newly resolved regime differs from the last resolved regime; with no prior state supplied, the first resolved regime establishes the initial allocation. This month-end produces no change signal.

5. Claim-to-evidence ledger

August 2026 CPI released 2026-09-11 08:30 ET. Observation period: August 2026. BLS September 2026 release schedule, http://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/09_sched_list.htm — "Friday, September 11, 2026 | 08:30 AM | Consumer Price Index for August 2026" (schedule notes all times are Eastern). Primary. Uncertainty: none material.
August 2026 CPI-U 12-month change = 3.4%; July 2026 = 3.4%. Observation periods: 12 months ending August 2026 and July 2026. Archived BLS release USDL-26-1496, embargoed to 2026-09-11 08:30 ET, https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_09112026.pdf — "The all items index rose 3.4 percent for the 12 months ending August as it did for the 12 months ending July." Primary (U.S. government work). Also reports index level 334.980 and states CPI-U/CPI-W are final when released. Uncertainty: none material.
September 2026 CPI released 2026-10-14 08:30 ET, i.e., after the evaluation month-end. BLS October 2026 release schedule, http://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/10_sched_list.htm — "Wednesday, October 14, 2026 | 08:30 AM | Consumer Price Index for September 2026"; the August CPI release itself also schedules the September release for that date. Primary. Confirms August was the latest CPI vintage available at the month-end.
August 2026 Employment Situation released 2026-09-04 08:30 ET. BLS September 2026 schedule, http://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/09_sched_list.htm — "Friday, September 4, 2026 | 08:30 AM | Employment Situation for August 2026". Primary. Uncertainty: none material.
September 2026 Employment Situation released 2026-10-02, after the evaluation month-end. BLS October 2026 schedule, http://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/10_sched_list.htm — "Friday, October 2, 2026 | 08:30 AM | Employment Situation for September 2026". Primary. Confirms August was the latest labor vintage available at the month-end.
August 2026 U-3 unemployment rate = 4.1%, unchanged from July 2026. Observation period: August 2026; published 2026-09-04. unemploymentdata.com quoting the BLS commissioner's statement, https://unemploymentdata.com/unemployment/jobs-report-for-august-2026/ — "the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.1 percent." Secondary quoting a primary statement; corroborated by financecalendar's August table ("Unemployment rate 4.1% … 4.1% (July)") and ihire's monthly table (July '26 4.1%, August '26 4.1%). Uncertainty: the archived BLS Employment Situation release was not directly retrieved (its archive URL could not be verified verbatim, and URL guessing is disallowed), so this leg rests on a primary-quoted statement plus three consistent secondary records.
Series-choice rationale (not decision-driving): the August payroll figure (+162,000 as first published) was later revised in the October 2 release, while the household-survey rate was "unchanged at 4.1 percent" — one reason the rate, not payrolls, is the revision-aware growth series here.

6. Conditional future recommendation policy

Next scheduled review: month-end 2026-10-31 16:00 ET, using release vintages actually available by then — the September 2026 CPI (released 2026-10-14) and the September 2026 Employment Situation (released 2026-10-02) both precede that month-end and would enter the comparison. If a future month-end yields non-zero signs, apply the zero-change carry rule against the last resolved leg state; recommend an allocation change only when the resulting resolved regime differs from the previously resolved regime. Months that remain unresolved prescribe no allocation and assert no trade.

7. Limitations, coverage, unresolved items
